docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Documentation · version 0.1

  • Synteny

    Pairwise and self synteny with LAST, BLAST or DIAMOND, quota alignment, synteny depth, and orthologous synteny by the Orthology Index.

    Pairwise synteny

  • Whole-genome duplications

    Native Ka/Ks (NG86, LPB93, GY94; no PAML needed), Ks mixture models, and WGDs placed on the species tree by four lines of evidence. Works from transcriptomes too.

    WGDs and Ks

  • Ancestral genomes

    Gene orders at every node of the species tree, ancestral chromosomes, and karyotypes on the tree with fusions, fissions and translocations.

    Ancestral genomes

  • Polyploids

    Biased fractionation with a permutation test, and subgenomes assigned by homology to progenitor-like genomes.

    Subgenomes

  • Many genomes

    Pan-genes linked by syntenic orthologues, riparian plots, synteny networks, phylogenomic profiles and network trees.

    Pan-genes and networks

  • Figures

    Interactive HTML dot plots, publication figures in a colour-blind-safe house style, or the original JCVI look pixel for pixel.

    Gallery

docs.title: MCscan3
docs.text:
Synteny, whole-genome duplication and genome evolution analysis

Abstract. MCscan3 is a single command-line program for comparative genomics, from genome annotations to an interactive report. It detects synteny between and within genomes, estimates Ka and Ks, places whole-genome duplications on the species tree, reconstructs ancestral gene orders and karyotypes, partitions polyploid subgenomes, builds pan-genomes, calls structural variants from whole-genome alignments, scaffolds assemblies and annotates transposable elements. It is the successor to MCScan, the Python MCscan of JCVI, and MCScanX. Every command is documented here with a worked example on published genomes: the exact command, its console output, every output file with its columns, and the figures it draws.

Quick start Command reference Installation

mamba env create -f environment.yml && conda activate mcscan3   # or pip, see Installation
mcscan3 pipeline run genomes/ -o results --cpus 8 --ks    # then open results/report.html

docs.title: One command, one report
docs.text:
mcscan3 pipeline run takes a directory of genomes (GFF3 with genome or CDS, or BED with CDS/proteins), finds orthologues, computes synteny for every pair, builds pan-genes, ancestral karyotypes, duplicate classes and WGD calls, and writes a self-contained HTML report with an interactive dot plot of every genome pair.

The report of a six-eudicot run: summary, interactive dot plots, pan-genes, ancestral karyotypes and WGDs on one page.

docs.title: How to cite
docs.text:
MCscan3 is not yet published (manuscript in preparation). Until it is, please cite the works it builds on, and the method papers given on the page of each command you use (mcscan3 cite prints the list):

  1. Tang H, Bowers JE, Wang X, Ming R, Alam M, Paterson AH (2008) Synteny and collinearity in plant genomes. Science 320:486-488. doi:10.1126/science.1153917
  2. Wang Y, Tang H, DeBarry JD, et al. (2012) MCScanX: a toolkit for detection and evolutionary analysis of gene synteny and collinearity. Nucleic Acids Res 40:e49. doi:10.1093/nar/gkr1293
  3. Tang H, Krishnakumar V, Zeng X, et al. (2024) JCVI: a versatile toolkit for comparative genomics analysis. iMeta 3:e211. doi:10.1002/imt2.211

MCscan3 builds on MCScan and JCVI (Haibao Tang) and MCScanX (Yupeng Wang). New features reimplement published methods, which are cited on each command's page.

docs.title: Deviations from JCVI
docs.text: Rule (from the extraction brief): ported features reproduce JCVI v1.6.7 exactly. When JCVI has a bug, the original behaviour stays the default, an opt-in flag enables the fix, and the case is recorded here. Entries marked proposed are awaiting a decision (see open questions in the Phase 0 checkpoint).

docs.title: A. JCVI v1.6.7 defects found while generating golden outputs (Phase 0)
docs.text:
Decision (project owner, 2026-09-28): a defect that makes a feature crash is fixed by default in MCscan3 (there is no behaviour to preserve). The parity reference for such a feature is JCVI v1.6.7 plus the minimal fixes in tools/jcvi_fixes.patch (every changed line is marked MCSCAN3 FIX A.<n>), run in .venv-jcvi-patched; those golden cases end in -fixed. Defects that silently change results are kept as the default with an opt-in fix.

Each is reproduced by a golden case whose exitcode.txt is non-zero and whose cmd.txt carries a note.

docs.title: C. Platform and representation notes (no behaviour change intended)
docs.text: Topic Original MCscan3 BLAST line class compiled Cython (cblast); falls back to a pure-Python class that formats numbers differently one pure-Python BlastLine that reproduces the compiled class exactly (verified on 185,849 real hits + edge cases) %g formatting of BLAST e-values/scores C sprintf, so output depends on the C library. macOS libc keeps a trailing zero on exact ties that round down (%.2g of 205 → 2.0e+02; glibc → 2e+02) reproduces the golden outputs (macOS) on every platform; MCSCAN3_PRINTF=standard gives C-standard %g. Emulation validated on 715,115 conversions BlastLine.orientation compiled class exposes a C char, i.e. the integers 43/45, so Python code comparing with "-" never matches (only affects out-of-scope blast chain/condense) the strings "+"/"-" HiGHS solver not available opt-in backend, run in a worker process (OR-Tools bundles HiGHS; both in one process can crash) ortholog omg-parse output order Python set order of groups, per glob file order files and groups sorted; same groups synteny matrix row/column order Python set order of chromosome names (changes with the hash seed between runs) natural sort order; identical counts phylo prepare gene order within each family file Python set order (changes with the hash seed between runs) column order of the MCscan row; same records phylo build ML tree (PhyML) PhyML seeds its random generator from the clock, so reruns (JCVI's too) may root the same tree differently or differ in the last digit of a branch length same; parity tests compare unrooted splits and branch lengths phylo build NJ tree EMBOSS PHYLIP via Biopython wrappers (removed from current Biopython) the same programs and options, called directly; not verified here (EMBOSS is not packaged for osx-arm64) Figure theme seaborn set_theme (notebook context, deep palette, --style), which also remaps the colour codes "k", "g", ... the same rcParams and colour codes, recorded as data (tools/gen_plot_data.py); no seaborn dependency. Figures are pixel-identical (PNG) and identical apart from metadata (SVG, PDF) ColorBrewer palettes palettable the same colour tables, recorded as data; no palettable dependency plot histogram figures R/ggplot2 (Rscript required) matplotlib, in ggplot2's default look; same data, bins and file names (<file>.<format>; the original always wrote .pdf unless --base). The text mode is byte-identical Dot plot grid colour option --theme (Set1 colour index) --grid-color; --theme selects the figure theme (classic or mcscan3). The legacy layer translates --theme Figure metadata Creator: Matplotlib ... Creator: MCscan3 <version> (PNG, PDF, SVG); nothing visible plot microsynteny --glyphcolor=orthogroup colours hash(orthogroup), which changes with the hash seed between runs a CRC32 of the sorted group members: the same colours on every run (the default orientation colouring is unaffected) must_open supports s3://, prompts before overwriting with checkexists=True no S3, never prompts

docs.title: B. Behaviour questions (not bugs)
docs.text: Topic JCVI behaviour Question gff bed --primary_only keeps the first transcript per gene Owner asked for longest-isoform prep: add opt-in --longest (Phase 6.1 / prep gff2bed) ASCII plots (ks report, histogram --ascii) print literal rich markup such as [green] and, because of a format bug, the line [bold white] instead of the title Decided: byte-identical by default; --plain prints the title and no markup fractionation offdiag hard-codes B. napus chromosome names (A0x/C0x) Port as-is, or mark legacy-only like napus/merge/segment? Report text on stderr synteny summary/stats, ks report, fractionation diff print results to stderr mixed with log lines Decided: MCscan3 also prints reports to stderr (plain text; log lines have their own mcscan3: format), keeping stdout for data. Parity tests compare the report lines of both.

docs.title: Migrating from JCVI
docs.text: MCscan3 contains the MCscan-related features of JCVI v1.6.7 (the version the outputs are verified against, see SOURCE_VERSION.md). Each JCVI command has one MCscan3 command, listed below.

docs.title: Running old command lines
docs.text:
Put mcscan3 legacy in place of python -m jcvi.. The rest of the line stays the same:

python -m jcvi.compara.catalog ortholog grape peach --no_strip_names   # JCVI
mcscan3 legacy compara.catalog ortholog grape peach --no_strip_names    # the same run in MCscan3
mcscan3 ortholog run grape peach --no-strip-names                       # the new spelling

mcscan3 legacy prints the new command name, then runs it. The MCscan tutorial runs unchanged this way (tested in tests/test_tutorial.py, with outputs identical to JCVI's).

docs.title: Option spelling
docs.text:
• Options are lower case with hyphens: --no_strip_names becomes --no-strip-names and --tandem_Nmax becomes --tandem-nmax. Legacy command lines are translated automatically.

  • Renamed options:

  • --theme is now --grid-color

docs.title: Outputs and behaviour
docs.text:
Outputs are byte-identical to JCVI's for the same inputs. Figures are pixel-identical by default, and --theme mcscan3 selects the new house style. Every deliberate difference is listed in DEVIATIONS.md. The main ones are:

  • Commands that always crashed in JCVI v1.6.7 work. Their reference outputs are JCVI plus the minimal fixes in tools/jcvi_fixes.patch.
  • Silent JCVI bugs keep JCVI's behaviour by default and have opt-in fixes, such as ortholog omg-prepare --integer-weights and the --plain text histograms.
  • Reports go to stderr, as in JCVI; data goes to stdout or files.
  • Figure metadata says Creator: MCscan3 <version>.

docs.title: Dependencies and external programs
docs.text: MCscan3 needs neither JCVI nor its compiled extensions. seaborn and palettable are replaced by recorded values, R is replaced by matplotlib for plot histogram, and the gmm-bic program is replaced by a built-in mixture fit (ks report --fit). External aligners and tools (LAST, BLAST+, DIAMOND, bedtools, ClustalW, MUSCLE, PAL2NAL, PAML, Gblocks, PhyML, RAxML, EMBOSS PHYLIP, CLUSTER 3.0) are found on PATH, or in the directory named by MCSCAN3_<PROGRAM>_PATH (e.g. MCSCAN3_LASTAL_PATH). plot tree, phylo draw and the rooting and NJ steps of phylo build need the phylo extra (pip install mcscan3[phylo], which installs ete4).

docs.title: New in MCscan3
docs.text:
These commands have no JCVI counterpart.

MCscan3 command Description Method mcscan3 prep genome Longest-isoform BED, CDS and protein from a genome GFF3 and FASTA Longest coding transcript per gene, CDS spliced from the genome and translated. mcscan3 align mmseqs Search proteins or CDS with MMseqs2 (BLAST tabular output for synteny) Steinegger M, Söding J (2017) MMseqs2 enables sensitive protein sequence searching for the analysis of massive data sets. Nat Biotechnol 35:1026; run as an external tool. mcscan3 align many Search many genomes in one run (optionally on a GPU); one .last file per pair One combined database and one search for all genome pairs, as in all-against-all orthology searches (Emms & Kelly 2019, Genome Biol 20:238); GPU search with MMseqs2-GPU (Kallenborn et al. 2025, Nat Methods); MMseqs2 or DIAMOND run as external tools. mcscan3 ortholog hogs Hierarchical orthologous groups at every node of a species tree, guided by synteny Hierarchical orthologous groups after Altenhoff AM et al. (2013) Inferring hierarchical orthologous groups from orthologous gene pairs. PLoS One 8:e53786 and Majidian S et al. (2025) Orthology inference at scale with FastOMA. Nat Methods 22:269; synteny-weighted links; reimplemented. mcscan3 ks kaks Ka, Ks and Ka/Ks of gene pairs with MCscan3's own estimators (no PAML) Native NG86 (Nei & Gojobori 1986), LPB93 (Li 1993; Pamilo & Bianchi 1993) and GY94 maximum likelihood (Goldman & Yang 1994) on protein-guided codon alignments; in the spirit of KaKs_Calculator. mcscan3 ortholog soi Keep orthologous synteny: blocks whose anchors are mostly orthologs (Orthology Index) Zhang R-G, et al. (2025) SOI: robust identification of orthologous synteny with the Orthology Index and broad applications in evolutionary genomics. Nucleic Acids Research; reimplemented from the paper. mcscan3 dup classify Classify duplicated genes: WGD, tandem, proximal, transposed, dispersed, singleton Qiao X, et al. (2019) Gene duplication and evolution in recurring polyploidization-diploidization cycles in plants. Genome Biology 20:38 (DupGen_finder); reimplemented from the paper. mcscan3 wgd ksd Whole-paranome or anchor-pair Ks distribution with node weighting Zwaenepoel A, Van de Peer Y (2019) wgd - simple command line tools for the analysis of ancient whole-genome duplications. Bioinformatics 35:2153; Chen H, Zwaenepoel A, Van de Peer Y (2024) wgd v2. Bioinformatics 40:btae272; reimplemented from the papers. mcscan3 wgd peaks Peaks of a Ks distribution (kernel density, bootstrap intervals) Zwaenepoel A, Van de Peer Y (2019) wgd - simple command line tools for the analysis of ancient whole-genome duplications. Bioinformatics 35:2153; Chen H, Zwaenepoel A, Van de Peer Y (2024) wgd v2. Bioinformatics 40:btae272; reimplemented from the papers. mcscan3 wgd mix Mixture models of a Ks distribution: GMM, ELMM, Bayesian GMM (BIC/AIC) Zwaenepoel A, Van de Peer Y (2019) wgd - simple command line tools for the analysis of ancient whole-genome duplications. Bioinformatics 35:2153; Chen H, Zwaenepoel A, Van de Peer Y (2024) wgd v2. Bioinformatics 40:btae272; reimplemented from the papers. mcscan3 wgd blocks Median Ks of each syntenic block (segment-guided Ks) Zwaenepoel A, Van de Peer Y (2019) wgd - simple command line tools for the analysis of ancient whole-genome duplications. Bioinformatics 35:2153; Chen H, Zwaenepoel A, Van de Peer Y (2024) wgd v2. Bioinformatics 40:btae272; reimplemented from the papers. mcscan3 wgd correct Rate-correct a species-divergence Ks onto a focal species' scale Sensalari C, Maere S, Lohaus R (2022) ksrates: positioning whole-genome duplications relative to speciation events in KS distributions. Bioinformatics 38:530; relative rate test with an outgroup. mcscan3 wgd tree-map Place gene duplications on a species tree by reconciling gene trees Chen Z, et al. docs.title: MCscan3 0.1.0: release summary
docs.text: For review by Haibao Tang (MCscan, JCVI) and Yupeng Wang (MCScanX).

docs.title: What MCscan3 is
docs.text: MCscan3 is a standalone Python package that holds the MCscan-related features of JCVI v1.6.7 (commit e10b884), rebranded and restructured. Each feature has its own API module, command (mcscan3 <group> <feature>), tests and documentation page. Every derived file names the JCVI file it comes from (BSD licence; see LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY). MCscan3 needs neither JCVI nor its compiled extensions, and it runs on Python 3.10–3.12.

docs.title: How parity was established
docs.text:
• Golden outputs. 166 cases were run with the original JCVI on reduced Ensembl Plants data: grape chromosomes 6 and 8, peach 6, poplar 6 and 16. MCscan3 reproduces every output byte for byte, or pixel for pixel for PNG figures. Unit goldens cover the shared core (BLAST lines, %g formatting, range chaining, quota ILP instances, and so on).
  • JCVI bugs. Ten commands crash on every run in JCVI v1.6.7. Their references come from JCVI plus a minimal patch (tools/jcvi_fixes.patch, each line marked). Silent bugs keep JCVI's behaviour by default and have opt-in fixes. All 22 are listed in docs/DEVIATIONS.md.
  • The tutorial. The MCscan (Python) tutorial runs through mcscan3 legacy with only the python -m jcvi. prefix changed, and its outputs are identical to JCVI's. The quick-start page, in the new command syntax, is tested the same way.
  • Speed. On the golden cases MCscan3 takes 0.06–1.2x the wall time of JCVI (Checkpoint 3b).

docs.title: Deviations worth your attention
docs.text:
Full list: docs/DEVIATIONS.md.

  1. Crash fixes (on by default; there was no working behaviour to preserve):
  2. synteny from-spa and synteny layout
  3. ortholog enrich and ortholog layout
  4. ks gc3
  5. fractionation validate and gff-select
  6. phylo prepare, build and draw
  7. synfind --scoring=density
  8. dotplot --synteny
  9. ks --fill
  10. synteny --tree
  11. several ribbon options
  12. phylo prepare --addtandem
  13. External programs replaced. ks report --fit fits the log-normal mixture itself instead of calling gmm-bic. plot histogram draws with matplotlib instead of R; its text mode is unchanged.
  14. Hash-seed-dependent orders made deterministic. omg-parse group order, the synteny matrix axes, phylo prepare record order and microsynteny orthogroup colours. The contents are unchanged.
  15. Option spelling is lower case with hyphens, translated automatically by the legacy layer. The dot plot's --theme (a Set1 colour index) is now --grid-color, because --theme selects the figure theme.
  16. Platform emulation, for identical output on every platform. This covers the C %g formatting (macOS libc behaviour), the compiled BlastLine class, and Unix sort tie-breaking.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• The phylo build neighbour-joining step (EMBOSS PHYLIP) is ported but unverified here, because EMBOSS is not packaged for Apple silicon. Its failure path matches JCVI's.
  • PhyML seeds its random generator from the clock, so trees are compared as unrooted splits.
  • The phylo draw reference comes from matplotlib 3.10.9 (JCVI's apps.phylo needs the old Biopython). The leaf-name font differs; the tree is identical.
  • The pure-Python BLAST parser is 3.8x slower per line than JCVI's Cython one, but it is not a bottleneck end to end.

docs.title: Verification at release
docs.text:
• pip install . in a fresh environment without JCVI, then the full test suite, including the aligner-based tests (the result is in docs/development/CHECKPOINTS.md).
  • grep -rni jcvi src/ finds only attribution headers, the legacy layer and the citation text in __about__.py.
  • Importing mcscan3 and every module under it loads no jcvi module.
  • Every registry entry is parity-verified, or legacy-only with a written reason (tested).
  • mkdocs build --strict passes without warnings.

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
docs/ROADMAP.md (Phase 6) lists the features planned on top of this core: - longest-isoform preparation - DupGen_finder-style duplication classes - SOI ortholog filtering - wgd2-style Ks and WGD inference - Tree2GD-style analyses - GENESPACE-style pan-gene sets - synteny networks and trees (after Zhao & Schranz)

They are clean-room implementations, with no code copied from those tools.

docs.title: MCscan3 roadmap: Phase 6 (after the JCVI extraction is complete)
docs.text:
Status (2026-09-29): all seven items are implemented, tested and documented. Their registry status is new. The commands are listed in the table below, and the migration guide has a "New in MCscan3" section. The open questions were settled as follows, following the owner's instruction to proceed with defaults:

  • Gene trees: wgd tree-map takes gene trees as input (Newick files). MCscan3 does not build them, so IQ-TREE, MAFFT and OrthoFinder are not dependencies. Rooting (minimum duplication), reconciliation and counting are built in.
  • Pan-genes: pan genes uses MCscan3's own synteny (the anchors of ortholog run), not OrthoFinder.
  • Networks: Infomap, used in the original network studies, is replaced by MCL (built in) or Louvain (networkx).
  • Maximum-likelihood trees: network profile --phylip writes the binary matrix for RAxML or IQ-TREE. The built-in trees are NJ or UPGMA.

Requested by the project owner on 2026-09-28. These start only after Phases 0–5 of docs/development/EXTRACTION_PROMPT.md are finished and signed off. They are new features, so they follow the same five-part structure (module, CLI command, registry entry, tests, docs page), but their registry status is new and they have no JCVI parity tests. Instead they get correctness tests on synthetic data and, where possible, comparisons against the published tool's outputs.

Clean-room rule: the extraction task forbids copying code from tools other than JCVI. The features below are re-implementations of the published methods (from the papers), cite the original tools, and must not copy their source code. Several of those tools are GPL-licensed, which is incompatible with MCscan3's BSD-3 license.

# Feature Proposed group / commands Method reference (to cite) 6.1 Raw genome GFF3 + FASTA → longest-isoform BED/CDS/PEP in one step (done) prep genome JCVI formats.gff bed / load behaviour; new --longest option 6.2 Duplicate-gene classification (WGD, tandem, proximal, transposed, dispersed, singleton) (done) dup classify DupGen_finder (Qiao et al. 2019, Genome Biology) 6.3 Synteny-based ortholog filtering using the Orthology Index (SOI) (done) ortholog soi SOI (Zhang et al. 2024/2025) 6.4 Genome-wide Ks distributions and WGD inference (paranome, anchor Ks, mixture models, peak calling, Ks correction) (done) wgd ksd, wgd peaks, wgd mix, wgd correct wgd v2 (Chen, Zwaenepoel et al. 2024, Bioinformatics) 6.5 WGD placement on a species tree from gene trees (done) wgd tree-map Tree2GD (Chen et al. 2023) 6.6 Pan-gene / pan-synteny analysis across many genomes (synteny-constrained orthogroups, riparian plots) (done) pan genes, plot riparian GENESPACE (Lovell et al. 2022, eLife) 6.7 Multi-species synteny network, clustering, and phylogenomic profiling / tree building from the network (done) network build, network cluster, network profile, network tree Zhao & Schranz 2017/2019, PNAS

Note: the extraction prompt lists "Orthology Index, WGD peak fitting, … networks, pangenomes" as out of scope for the extraction task and defers them to the MCscan3 Feature Catalog. This roadmap records the owner's request so they are scheduled right after it.

The open questions (gene-tree dependencies, and OrthoFinder or MCscan3's own clustering for pan-genes) were settled as described at the top of this page.

docs.text:

"Full pipelines, not stubs" (owner, 2026-10-04).

wgd v2-style paranome Ks without external tools KaKs_Calculator, PAML, wgd v2 7.21 Transcriptome-based WGD inference (no genome): assemblies/ORFs to paralog families, Ks distributions, mixture models, placement with transcriptome orthologs WGDetector, wgd 7.22 Synteny-network figures: pairwise species heatmap mirrored (raw similarity / phylogeny-corrected), network graph, profile heatmap with clusters, network tree; Tree2GD-style figures SynNet, Tree2GD 7.23 Karyotype plot redesign: centred layout, light and dark themes, GENESPACE-inspired styling JCVI karyotype, GENESPACE 7.24 Large-scale orthology and network construction: FastOMA-style linear-time families and HOGs feeding the synteny network; GPU paths FastOMA, OMAmer 7.25 Annotation format utilities: GFF3/GTF from any source normalised (IDs, parent links, feature types), GTF <-> GFF3, CDS/protein/transcript extraction from genome + annotation, longest isoform, chromosome renaming to match the FASTA, validation and statistics gffread, AGAT 7.16 Remaining plot items (Mb axes, scaffold pooling, highlights, circular, interactive dot plot); pansyn-style features (awaiting the owner's answer) GENESPACE, pansyn, plotsr

docs.title: Phase 8: deep-time genome structure (requested 2026-10-24)
docs.text:
Same rules as Phases 6-7 (clean-room from the papers, cited, never copied or named after the tools; tests with a known answer; validation on real genomes; docs page), plus: robust, fast (vectorised, linear or near-linear in genomes where the method allows) and benchmarked against the tools that inspired them.

# Feature Commands (planned) Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 8.1 Macrosynteny of distant genomes: chromosome-pair ortholog enrichment (one-sided Fisher, FDR), Oxford dot plots ordered by enrichment, ancestral linkage groups (given, or found de novo from co-occurrence across genomes), fusions, fissions and fusion-with-mixing per genome, mapped on the species tree macro test, macro algs, macro fusions, macro plot Simakov et al. 2020 Nat Ecol Evol; Simakov et al. 2022 Sci Adv; Schultz et al. 2023 Nature; CephChromosomes (Schmidbaur et al. 2022 Nat Commun) 8.2 Multi-genome microsynteny blocks (ortholog-anchored gene neighbourhoods), blocks dated as ancestral or novel at each node of the species tree, syntenic gene density against random blocks, density transitions along the tree Done 2026-10-25 (Leiden family groups, E-values, shuffle null; 98% of planted blocks recovered exactly, no false blocks, over 20 seeds). micro blocks, micro nodes, micro density Simakov et al. 2013 Nature; Zimmermann et al. 2019 Nat Ecol Evol; Robert et al. 2022 BMC Genomics 8.3 Conserved non-coding elements (CNEs) from genome alignments inside syntenic blocks (I/C window scan, exon and repeat masking, two-way merge, repeat filter), CNE density and genomic regulatory blocks (GRBs) with their target genes Done 2026-10-24 (one LAST run per genome pair inside syntenic blocks; Arabidopsis vs Brassica rapa in about 2 minutes). cne find, cne grb, cne plot Kikuta et al. 2007 Genome Res; Tan et al. 2019 PLoS Comput Biol (CNEr); Harmston et al. 2017 Nat Commun 8.4 Hierarchical orthologous groups (HOGs) at every node of the species tree, bottom-up from gene families by species overlap; ancestral gene adjacencies propagated over HOGs (bottom-up, top-down parsimony, linearisation, edge dating), feeding ancestral genomes Done 2026-10-24 (simulation with a WGD: HOG orthologs F1 0.998 with synteny vs 0.976 for OrthoFinder, 1.3 s vs 104 s; ancestral adjacencies precision ≥0.99 and recall ≥0.97 at every node). ortholog hogs, ancestral adjacencies Majidian et al. 2025 Nat Methods (FastOMA); Bernard et al. 2025 Nat Ecol Evol (EdgeHOG); Muffato et al. 2023 (AGORA) 8.5 Karyotype comparison: a known ancestral karyotype painted on genomes through synteny blocks (optionally the blocks of one Ks event), with copies; trajectories from the ancestor (EEJ, NCF, RCT, TRA, FIS, WGD) mapped onto the tree by Dollo, giving each ancestor's karyotype; the ancestral karyotype written as a genome. Done 2026-10-24. karyotype map, events, genome WGDI (Sun et al. 2022 Mol Plant); AKRUP; Wang et al. 2015 Plant Cell; Murat et al. 2017 Genome Biol

Done in the same session (2026-10-24): align many (one search for all pairs, CPU or MMseqs2-GPU), pipeline run --search/--gpu/--jobs, faster network build/cluster/tree, Leiden and Infomap, network stats/gainloss/compare (covers 7.4 and most of 7.19).

docs.title: Phase 9: whole-genome alignment, structural variation, introgression and pangenome views (requested 2026-10-25)
docs.text:
The owner asked for: the miscellaneous JCVI visualisation tools; SyRI- and DEEPSPACE-like analyses (DEEPSPACE by J. T. Lovell); whole-genome alignment tools; introgression tools such as KCFtools; similar whole-genome and pangenome comparison tools; a pipeline to see large structural variation and other pangenome features; and visualisation tools for comparing genomes and haplotypes. Supersedes Phase 7 items 7.7, 7.12 and the plotsr/pansyn part of 7.16. Clean-room, own command names, validated on real genomes.

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 9.1 Whole-genome alignment wrapper and chaining (minimap2/LAST/AnchorWave-style anchors), PAF/MAF/SAM in, collinear chains out; annotation-free (DNA-level) synteny across many genomes Done 2026-10-25 (wga align, wga chain; Col-0 vs Ler-0 aligned in 51 s, 111 blocks). minimap2, LAST, AnchorWave, DEEPSPACE 9.2 Structural rearrangements between two assemblies: syntenic regions, inversions, translocations, duplications, not-aligned regions, plus SNPs/indels within syntenic regions (VCF + table) Done 2026-10-25 (sv call, sv plot; 90/90 planted SVs over 10 simulations, no false calls, SNP recall 99.1% with none wrong; Col-0 vs Ler-0 in 3 s: the known 1.17 Mb chr4 inversion recovered, 575k SNPs). SyRI (Goel et al. 2019) 9.3 Multi-genome/haplotype SV pipeline: chained pairwise calls along a genome order, pan-SV table (presence per genome), SV size spectra, core/variable genome in bp Done 2026-10-25 (sv pan, sv merge; six Arabidopsis assemblies in 10 min: 29,535 pan-SVs, 92.8 Mb core / 23.4 Mb variable; the chr4 inversion shared by all non-Col accessions and Sha's chr3 inversion recovered). SyRI, plotsr, pansyn, PGGB 9.4 Introgression scans: k-mer containment/identity of a query genome or reads in windows against donor references, introgressed blocks called by HMM-like segmentation, per-sample haplotype painting Done 2026-10-25 (introgress scan, introgress plot; FracMinHash k-mers, Viterbi segmentation, breakpoints refined to the sampled k-mer: simulated blocks recovered within 114 bp; Kyo painted by five accessions in 25 s and 1.9 GB). KCFtools, IBSpy, k-mer IBS methods 9.5 Genome and haplotype comparison viewers: stacked-chromosome rearrangement plot, haplotype painting along chromosomes, pairwise identity heatmaps in windows, interactive HTML browser of alignments and SVs Done 2026-10-25 (stacked plot sv plot, painting introgress plot, view identity (exact per-window identity from CIGAR, or k-mer estimate; five accessions vs Col-0 in 3.5 s), view matrix (containment ANI of six genomes in 15 s), view browse (self-contained canvas browser of alignments, SVs, pan-SVs, paintings, identity)). plotsr, NGenomeSyn, GENESPACE riparian, JCVI 9.6 Remaining JCVI miscellaneous graphics (graphics.* and misc plots not yet ported) JCVI graphics.* 9.7 Genetic-map-based rescaffolding (requested 2026-10-25): place, order and orient scaffolds by markers of one or more linkage maps, split chimeric scaffolds where markers of different linkage groups meet, report conflicts, write AGP and the new FASTA; fast (vectorised) and robust to marker errors (longest consistent marker chain per scaffold) Done 2026-10-25 (scaffold map: Ler-0 contigs with planted misjoins and two simulated maps (one reversed, renamed): all linkage groups and orders right, Spearman rho 1.00; pieces with under two markers cannot be oriented by maps and are reported) Chromonomer (Catchen J et al.), ALLMAPS (Tang H et al. 2015, Genome Biol 16:3) 9.8 Reference-guided scaffolding and correction (requested 2026-10-25): order and orient contigs by whole-genome alignment to one or more related references, break misjoins supported by the alignments, gap sizes from the reference, merge evidence of several references, AGP out; faster and more reliable than single-reference tools via the 9.1 chains and synteny-aware placement Done 2026-10-25 (scaffold ref: Ler-0 cut into 110 contigs with 6 planted misjoins, scaffolded on Col-0 in 5.5 s: exactly the 6 cuts, 109/109 joins right; RagTag 2.1.1 on the same input: 122 cuts, 128/153 joins right, 16 s) RagTag (Alonge M et al. 2022, Genome Biol 23:258) 9.9 Hi-C scaffolding, haplotype- and allele-aware (requested 2026-10-25): Hi-C pairs from SAM/BAM/.pairs (or reads mapped with bwa), binned contact counts, allele table from contig self-alignment or a monoploid reference, pruning of allelic and weak cross-allelic links, partition into chromosomes x ploidy groups with cannot-link constraints (autopolyploids up to octoploid, e.g. sugarcane), rescue of unplaced contigs, order and orientation by a distance-decay likelihood (greedy joins then local search), AGP and FASTA; reference-guided mode (contigs to chromosomes by alignment, Hi-C to separate haplotypes and order them); Hi-C misjoin correction; contact map figures (whole genome and per chromosome); Juicebox-like review (requested 2026-10-25): interactive contact map in the browser with scaffold/contig outlines, zoom, and manual curation (select, move, invert, cut, mark debris, undo) exporting the edited AGP and a Juicebox .assembly file; reading .assembly back to rebuild the FASTA Done 2026-10-25 (scaffold contacts, hic, hicmap, review, apply: simulated octoploid (4 chromosomes x 8 haplotypes) with half the cis contacts mis-mapped to alleles: all 32 haplotypes pure and correctly ordered with the allele table, purity 0.22 without; reference-guided polyploid mode; all planted misjoins found within 1 kb, no false cuts; homologs named and co-oriented; Juicebox-like review page with curation and .assembly export) ALLHiC (Zhang X et al. 2019, Nat Plants 5:833), HapHiC (Zeng X et al. 2024, Nat Plants), YaHS (Zhou C et al. 2023, Bioinformatics 39:btac808), 3D-DNA (Dudchenko O et al. 2017, Science 356:92) 9.10 One scaffolding pipeline combining evidence: reference(s), genetic map(s) and Hi-C, with conflicts reported and the contact map / map-vs-assembly / synteny figures of the result Done 2026-10-25 (scaffold run: references, maps and Hi-C in one graph; Ler-0 with Col-0 and two maps: 6 cuts, 109/109 joins; simulated Hi-C + reference: 95/95 joins) ALLMAPS, RagTag, ALLHiC 9.11 Gene Ontology (requested 2026-10-25): OBO parser (is_a/part_of, alt ids, obsolete terms), annotations from GAF/GPAD/tables with true-path propagation, enrichment and depletion with Fisher exact tests and Bonferroni/Holm/Sidak/BH/BY corrections, GO-slim mapping, semantic similarity (Resnik/Lin), DAG and bubble plots; wired into MCscan3 gene sets: retained WGD duplicates and duplication modes, lineage-specific and core/dispensable pan-genes, HOGs gained or lost on a branch, genes in SVs, introgressed blocks, CNE/GRB targets, subgenome-dominant genes Done 2026-10-25 (go enrich, go sets, go slim, go similarity, pipeline step go; same counts and significant terms as GOATOOLS 1.6.7 on 37,573 Arabidopsis genes, 16x faster) GOATOOLS (Klopfenstein DV et al. 2018, Sci Rep 8:10872) 9.12 Chain-based liftover between assembly versions (requested 2026-10-25): base-level UCSC chains from wga align PAFs, lifting of BED, GFF3/GTF (whole gene models kept on one chain and strand, CDS frame checked on the new genome) and VCF (REF checked, minus-strand indels re-anchored, REF/ALT swapped with genotypes when the new reference carries the old ALT), unlifted records with reasons Done 2026-10-25 (annotate chain, annotate lift) transanno (Okada Y, Tang H), UCSC liftOver/CrossMap 9.13 Annotation-free synteny views (requested 2026-10-25): one genome cut into windows (1-5 kb) aligned to another, window hits chained into synteny blocks like gene anchors (distant/fast presets), per-pair dotplots of the windowed hits with block outlines, and a multi-genome riparian plot phased by a reference (blocks as braids, inversions highlighted, chromosomes ordered by synteny, daisy-chained genomes), with density tracks above Done 2026-10-25 (wga windows, wga riparian; Col-0/Ler-0/Cvi-0/Sha in about a minute per pair) DEEPSPACE (Lovell JT, github.com/jtlovell/DEEPSPACE), GENESPACE (Lovell JT et al. 2022, eLife 11:e78526) 9.14 GFF3/GTF toolkit (requested 2026-10-25): format checking and repair (missing parents, IDs, phases, UTRs, gene/mRNA spans), GFF3/GTF/BED conversion, statistics (genes, transcripts, exons, introns, lengths, isoforms), longest isoform, filtering by type/attribute/length/ORF, sequence extraction (CDS, protein, exons, introns, UTRs, upstream/downstream), merging and deduplicating annotations, renaming IDs, intron/intergenic features, comparison of two annotations Done: gff fix/convert/stats/longest/filter/extract/merge/rename/add/compare; Arabidopsis TAIR10 GFF3 -> GTF -> GFF3 identical at every level, rice fix in 11 s AGAT (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT, doi:10.5281/zenodo.3552717) 9.15 Gene ages (requested 2026-10-25; supersedes 7.13): proteome searched against a taxonomically wide database (DIAMOND/MMseqs2), hits mapped to taxonomy (NCBI taxdump), phylostrata as the oldest node with a homolog, taxonomic representativeness per stratum, homology-detection-failure test (expected bit-score decay with distance, abSENSE-like), synteny support from MCscan3 blocks to rescue or confirm young genes, gene-family ages, age per subgenome/duplicate class, figures GenEra (Barrera-Redondo J et al. 2023, Genome Biol 24:54), abSENSE (Weisman CM et al. 2020, PLoS Biol 18:e3000862), phylostratr (Arendsee Z et al. 2019, Bioinformatics 35:3617) 9.16 Synteny output formats chosen by the user (requested 2026-10-25): every block/anchor output writable as MCscan/JCVI .anchors (default), MCScanX .collinearity (+ .gff), WGDI collinearity/blockinfo, i-ADHoRe multiplicons, SynVisio input, GENESPACE-like syntenic hits and BED/BEDPE, via --out-format on the synteny commands and synteny convert between them. Done: synteny convert (anchors, mcscanx, wgdi, genespace (synHits and syntenicBlock_coordinates, checked with GENESPACE's read_synHits), iadhore, synvisio, bedpe, tsv), --out-format on synteny scan/anchor and ortholog run, pipeline run --synteny-format; WGDI files checked against WGDI 0.75's readers MCScanX (Wang Y et al. 2012, NAR 40:e49), WGDI (Sun P et al. 2022, Mol Plant 15:1841), i-ADHoRe 3.0 (Proost S et al. 2012, NAR 40:e11), SynVisio (Bandi V & Gutwin C 2020) 9.17 Phylotranscriptomics (requested 2026-10-25; needs 9.15 gene ages): transcriptome age index (TAI) and divergence index (TDI, from Ka/Ks of orthologues) across stages/tissues/conditions, flat-line, reductive hourglass, early- and late-conservation tests by permutation, contribution of each stratum, relative expression per stratum, gene-level age-expression profiles, with GO of the driving genes myTAI (Drost HG et al. 2018, Bioinformatics 34:1589; github.com/josuebarrera/myTAI), Domazet-Loso T & Tautz D 2010 (Nature 468:815) 9.18 Project files (requested 2026-10-25): every run writes <prefix>.mcscan3 (gzip tar: command, version, input checksums, outputs and compressed copies of them) and indexes it in the user cache; mcscan3 --cache restores an identical earlier run; project show/fetch/rerun/history. Done MCscan3 9.19 Expression (requested 2026-10-25): expr counts (featureCounts/htseq/Salmon/kallisto/RSEM to counts, TPM, CPM), expr de (genes ranked by Bayes factors with replicate consistency, reference-vs-reference controls and consistently inconsistent genes; values identical to the authors' bayexpress functions), expr homoeolog (homoeolog bias, subgenome dominance, bias changes between conditions; reads subgenome fractionation tables), expr pairs (expression correlation of duplicate/syntenic/ortholog pairs, tau); DE calls and bias categories feed go sets. Done Hoerbst F et al. 2025 (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.31.635902; 10.1101/2025.01.20.633909), Ramírez-González RH et al. 2018 (Science 361:eaar6089), Yanai I et al. 2005 (Bioinformatics 21:650) 9.20 Genome track figures (requested 2026-10-25): view tracks --tracks FILE.ini --region chr:start-end -o result.pdf, pyGenomeTracks-style INI (genes, BED, bedGraph/bigWig, links, synteny between genome rows, x-axis, spacers) for microsynteny figures. Done: view tracks (genes from BED/GFF/GTF, BED, bedGraph, bigWig with pyBigWig, links, vlines, x-axis, spacers, per-track regions, synteny ribbons from anchors/BEDPE; --BED for many regions) pyGenomeTracks (Lopez-Delisle L et al. 2021, Bioinformatics 37:422)

docs.title: Phase 10: centromeres and telomeres (requested 2026-10-25; after Phase 9)
docs.text:
The owner asked to integrate centromere and telomere mining like quarTeT's CentroMiner (and TeloExplorer) once all earlier phases are finished. Clean-room, own command names, validated on telomere-to-telomere assemblies (e.g. Arabidopsis Col-CC, rice T2T).

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 10.1 Telomere detection: telomeric repeat arrays (known motif per clade or found de novo) at chromosome ends, length and completeness per end, T2T status of each chromosome quarTeT TeloExplorer (Lin Y et al. 2023, Hortic Res 10:uhad127) 10.2 Centromere candidates: tandem-repeat monomers (period finding, monomer clustering), satellite arrays along chromosomes, scored with TE density and gene density into a predicted centromere per chromosome quarTeT CentroMiner (Lin Y et al. 2023) 10.3 Integration: centromere/telomere tracks in karyotype, synteny and SV figures; centromere positions to classify fusions (EEJ vs NCF) and to mark pericentromeric SVs — 10.4 Genome landscapes (requested 2026-10-25): contigs, gaps and telomeres (present, incomplete or absent per end; interstitial arrays) from assemblies; sliding-window feature content (genes as CDS and introns, Ty3, Copia, other repeats, centromeric satellites, unknown) as stacked area plots along linearised chromosomes; classification of windows into arm, pericentromere and subtelomere by a classifier trained on the most centromere-like region of each chromosome, with probabilities; overlays on riparian plots geeViz (Lovell JT, github.com/jtlovell/geeViz)

docs.title: Phase 11: transposable elements and subgenome phasing (requested 2026-10-25; started 2026-10-26, ahead of Phase 10)
docs.text: The owner asked for "a newer, more enhanced version of EDTA with a faster implementation, more sub-tools and more in-depth annotation, with TEsorter-like subclassification and insertion-time dating", followed by "SubPhaser-like" subgenome phasing with its figures. Native reimplementations (external tools optional), validated on Arabidopsis, rice and a polyploid (e.g. wheat or Brassica napus) against curated libraries.

docs.title: What goes wrong with EDTA, and what MCscan3 does instead (owner request 2026-10-26)
docs.text:
Moved ahead of Phase 10 on 2026-10-26 ("take EDTA, see what's wrong with it and not fast, integrate new tools and features, make it a world-class detailed repeat annotation, with TEsorter-like things"). From the EDTA README and issue tracker (about 600 closed issues):

Problem with EDTA MCscan3 te About 20 external programs (TIR-Learner with a deep-learning model, HelitronScanner in Java, RepeatModeler, AnnoSINE, LTR_FINDER, LTRharvest, LTR_retriever, RepeatMasker, cd-hit, mdust...); versions break each other (pandas 2, TIR-Learner 4, containers) native discovery of every order (C kernels with pure-Python fallbacks); only HMMER and BLAST/minimap2 needed; external finders optional, as extra evidence Slow steps: TIR-Learner and RepeatModeler run for days on large genomes; whole-genome RepeatMasker k-mer seeded search per chromosome in parallel; library masking split by chromosome; every step cached and resumable Fragile input: sequence names of 13-15 characters at most, failures on large single chromosomes, empty-file and "not found" crashes, silent "no SINE found" stops names mapped internally; any size; every step writes its result (even empty) and the run report says what each step found Inconsistent outputs (intact FASTA, GFF3 and library disagree; superfamily labels lost on reruns) one table of elements from which GFF3, FASTA, library and figures are all written Many "unknown" LTR elements; classification only to superfamily (TEsorter optional) REXdb domain classification to clade built in (Ty1/copia and Ty3/gypsy clades, LINE clades, TIR transposases), with domain order and completeness Helitron false positives; gene fragments in the library hairpin and end-motif scoring for Helitrons; protein-domain and CDS filters for gene fragments; tandem-repeat filter Little analysis after annotation insertion times (K2P, per clade), solo:intact ratios, LAI along chromosomes, Kimura landscapes, density along chromosomes, TE-gene distances, TEs near SVs and in synteny gaps, benchmark against curated libraries

Commands (mcscan3 te ...): ltr, tir, helitron, nonltr (LINE/SINE), tandem, classify, library, annotate (homology masking, fragments, Kimura divergence), age, lai, landscape (figures), bench (against a curated library: sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 per superfamily and a confusion matrix), and run (all of them, resumable).

Build order: 11.1 LTR (kernel, intact elements, TSD/motif/PBS/PPT, identity and age) -> 11.3 REXdb classification -> 11.1 TIR/MITE, Helitron, LINE/SINE, tandem -> 11.2 library and genome annotation -> 11.4 ages, LAI, landscapes -> te run and te bench -> 11.5 phasing.

First head-to-head (2026-10-26, simulated 3.9 Mb genome with 80 intact LTR elements, 8 nested, solo LTRs, truncated copies, tandem duplications and satellites): te ltr found 80/80 with exact boundaries and no false calls in 3 s (4 CPUs); EDTA's LTR module (LTRharvest + LTR_FINDER_parallel + LTR_retriever, 4 CPUs, osx-64 build) found 45/80, no false calls, in 441 s. It missed all 11 elements below 92% LTR identity, 9 of 12 hosts broken by later insertions and 4 of 8 nested ones.

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 11.1 Structural TE discovery, natively and fast: LTR retrotransposons (paired LTRs with TSDs, PBS/PPT; candidate pairs from k-mer seeds), TIR elements (terminal inverted repeats with superfamily TSD lengths), Helitrons (5'TC/3'CTRR ends and hairpin), non-LTR LINE/SINE (poly-A tails, target-site duplications), MITEs; optional wrappers of LTR_FINDER/LTRharvest/TIR-Learner/HelitronScanner EDTA (Ou S et al. 2019, Genome Biol 20:275), LTR_retriever, LTRharvest, TIR-Learner, HelitronScanner 11.2 Library curation: filtering of false positives (gene fragments, tandem repeats, nested elements), clustering to families (80-80-80 rule), whole-genome masking with the library, homology-based annotation of fragments; LTR Assembly Index EDTA, LTR_retriever LAI (Ou S et al. 2018, NAR 46:e126) 11.3 Domain-based classification to clade (TEsorter-like): REXdb protein domain profiles (GAG, PROT, RT, RH, INT, CHD...), domain order, clade calls (Ty1/copia: Ale, Angela, Bianca, Ikeros, Ivana, SIRE, Tork...; Ty3/gypsy: Athila, CRM, Galadriel, Reina, Tekay, Retand...), plus TIR superfamilies and Helitrons TEsorter (Zhang RG et al. 2022, Hortic Res 9:uhac017), REXdb (Neumann P et al. 2019, Mob DNA 10:1) 11.3b te classify as an evidence ensemble (owner request 2026-10-26, "something like Terrier, or a better way"): (1) structure from the finders (LTR motif/TSD/PBS/PPT; TIR terminal motifs and TSD length per superfamily: DTA 8 bp, DTC CACTA and 3 bp, DTH TWA and 3 bp, DTM 9-11 bp, DTT TA; Helitron TC...CTRR and hairpin; LINE/SINE poly-A, Pol III boxes), (2) protein domains (REXdb clades, Pfam/transposase families) with domain order, (3) homology to curated open families (Dfam curated, CC0; user libraries), (4) a hierarchical k-mer/convolutional classifier trained on open curated families (Dfam curated; Repbase only when the user has it), with the class tree and a confidence threshold per level that falls back to the parent (order instead of superfamily) when unsure; optional Terrier or TEsorter runs as extra votes. The calls are combined per level with their evidence and a calibrated probability; disagreements are reported. Benchmarked on held-out families (rice, fruit fly, human, mouse; the Terrier/TEclass2 test sets) against Terrier, TEsorter, DeepTE and the RepeatModeler classifier Terrier (Turnbull R et al. 2025, Brief Bioinform 26:bbaf442), TEsorter, TEclass2, DeepTE, Dfam (Storer J et al. 2021 Mob DNA 12:2) 11.4 Insertion-time dating of intact LTR elements (5'/3' LTR divergence, K2P, substitution rate per clade/species), age distributions per clade, solo-LTR to intact ratios, TE landscapes (Kimura divergence) LTR_retriever, RepeatMasker landscapes 11.5 Subgenome phasing of polyploids from differential k-mers (subgenome-specific k-mers enriched on homoeologous chromosome sets), k-means/hierarchical assignment with bootstrap support, LTR insertions carrying the k-mers dated to time the divergence of progenitors and the polyploidisation, combined with MCscan3 synteny and subgenome dominance; figures: k-mer heatmap and clustering, chromosome painting by subgenome, insertion-time histograms per subgenome, circos SubPhaser (Jia KH et al. 2022, New Phytol 235:801) 11.7 Insertion history (owner request 2026-10-26: "when and where they were inserted, nested insertion"): ages of intact LTR elements (K2P of the two LTRs, rate per species), nested insertions (elements inside other elements, inside their LTRs or internal region) resolved into nesting trees and a relative chronology (an inner element is younger than its host; checks the molecular ages), insertion sites (chromosome region: arm, pericentromere, centromere; distance to genes, intron/promoter/intergenic; target-site duplication motifs and hotspots), and dating against the species tree with MCscan3 synteny: an insertion present at the orthologous position in a related genome is older than their split, absent means younger (insertions placed on branches); figures: age histograms per clade, nesting trees, insertion maps along chromosomes, insertions on the species tree LTR_retriever (dating), TE-nest/TEnest (SanMiguel P et al. 1996 Science 274:765 for nested LTR dating), MCscan3 synteny 11.8 Speed, plots and browsers (owner request 2026-10-26): every step parallel over chromosome chunks (processes; C kernels release the GIL) and cached; GPU when available for the neural classifier and k-mer counting (CUDA or Apple MPS through PyTorch/CuPy when installed, CPU otherwise, same results); a plotting suite (genome composition by order and superfamily, length and age distributions per clade, Kimura landscapes, density along chromosomes and ideograms, nesting trees, LAI along chromosomes, element structure diagrams with domains, insertion maps on the species tree); genome browser output for everything MCscan3 writes: JBrowse 2 configuration (bgzipped and indexed GFF3/BED, BigWig densities, synteny tracks), IGV sessions, UCSC track hubs, and the MCscan3 viewer JBrowse 2 (Diesh C et al. 2023 Genome Biol 24:74), IGV, UCSC track hubs 11.6 Integration: TE tracks in karyotype, synteny, SV, centromere (Phase 10) and browser views; TE-mediated SVs; GO of TE-associated genes —

docs.title: Phase 12: block expression, phylogenomics, orthogroup QC and biosynthetic gene clusters (requested 2026-10-26)
docs.text:
The owner asked for: the useful parts of the metazoan synteny/expression code (Zimmermann et al.); "busco_phylogenomics integrated, better, faster and optimised, with tree plotting modules"; cogeqc-like quality checks and orthobrowser-like views of OrthoFinder results; and "a plantiSMASH-like package that uses hmmscan/pfamscan and synteny to find biosynthetic gene clusters", integrated with RNA-seq co-expression and comparative genomics. Native implementations (HMMER/MAFFT/trimming/tree builders optional), clean-room from the papers and docs.

# Feature Inspiration (cite, do not copy) 12.1 pan run: gene-based and sequence-based (FracMinHash) pan-genome, classes, curves, Heaps' law, similarity (done 2026-10-26) GENESPACE, Mash, FracMinHash, Tettelin 2008 12.2 (done 2026-10-26) micro coexpr: co-expression of the genes of microsynteny blocks across tissues/cell types against shuffled, sampled and sampled-ortholog random blocks (Fisher-z mean correlation, empirical P), tau specificity and cell-type bias per block, paralog content of blocks, intervening-gene gaps with a negative binomial fit Zimmermann B et al. (2019) Nat Ecol Evol 3:1289 (metazoan_synteny code) 12.3 (done 2026-10-26) phylo busco: BUSCO (or compleasm/MCscan3 single-copy) results of many genomes -> shared single-copy sets with occupancy threshold -> parallel alignment (MAFFT or native), trimming, supermatrix with partitions and gene trees -> concatenated ML (IQ-TREE/FastTree optional) and coalescent summary (native ASTRAL-like quartet support), concordance factors; cached and parallel BUSCO_phylogenomics (McGowan J), ASTRAL, gCF/sCF 12.4 (done 2026-10-26) plot phylo tree figures (ete3-like features natively in matplotlib): rectangular/circular/unrooted layouts, support and concordance pie charts, clade highlight, aligned heatmaps/bars (BUSCO completeness, genome size, gene counts, pan classes), tanglegrams of two trees ete3 (Huerta-Cepas J et al. 2016 Mol Biol Evol 33:1635) 12.5 (done 2026-10-26) ortholog qc: orthogroup statistics and figures from OrthoFinder or MCscan3 groups (per-species assignment, species overlap, size distributions, duplications per node), domain-aware homogeneity and dispersal scores with Pfam, BUSCO summary and assembly/annotation statistics comparison cogeqc (Almeida-Silva F & Van de Peer Y, Bioconductor) 12.6 ortholog browse: interactive HTML browser of an orthogroup: gene tree, domain architecture, the synteny neighbourhood of every member, expression orthobrowser (Salk TM, GitLab) 12.7 bgc find: biosynthetic gene clusters: Pfam domains (hmmscan/pyhmmer or native) -> signature enzyme rules per class (terpene, triterpene/saponin, alkaloid, polyketide, saccharide, lignan, cyanogenic glycoside, NRPS/PKS for fungi and bacteria...) -> clusters of co-located signature and tailoring enzymes with gap rules, scored against random genomic windows; plant, fungal and bacterial rule sets plantiSMASH (Kautsar SA et al. 2017 NAR 45:W55), antiSMASH (Blin K et al. 2023 NAR 51:W46) 12.8 BGC evidence integration: co-expression of cluster genes from RNA-seq (expr), conservation of clusters across genomes from MCscan3 synteny (present, partial, rearranged, absent), tandem duplication and pan-genome class of cluster genes, cluster families across genomes (domain-content and synteny similarity), figures (cluster maps with domains, comparative cluster ribbons, co-expression heatmaps, presence on a species tree) and an HTML report per cluster plantiSMASH CoExpress, BiG-SCAPE (Navarro-Muñoz JC et al. 2020 Nat Chem Biol 16:60) 12.9 expr coexp: genes co-expressed with bait genes (Spearman/Pearson, r and P cutoffs, BH, minimum expression, number of baits each gene is co-expressed with), bait network and heatmap; expr qc: sample filtering (share of expression on the top 100 genes, read counts, sample-correlation outliers, block list) CoExp (Pucker B, GitHub bpucker/CoExp) 12.10 expr conserved: co-expression conserved across species: baits per species, co-expressed genes grouped by MCscan3 orthogroups or synteny (or protein clustering), gene trees with co-expressed tips highlighted (MCscan3 tree figures), clusters where co-expressed genes of several species fall together CoExpPhylo (Pucker B et al., GitHub bpucker/CoExpPhylo) 12.11 Read coverage: genome-wide coverage plots of resequencing data (binned, saturated, normalised to the genome average, region zoom) from samtools depth/mosdepth/bedGraph; coverage-based gene presence/absence and zero-coverage regions between samples GKseq2, PAV_finder (Pucker B, GitHub bpucker/GKseq2, PBBtools) 12.12 Utilities: masking monophyletic same-species tips in gene trees; tblastn check for genes missing from an annotation; expression plots of gene sets with outlier filtering PBBtools (Pucker B)

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
Every plot command takes the same image options: --figsize, --dpi, --format (pdf, png, svg, ...), --font, --style (axes background), --cmap, --diverge, --seed (random colours) and --theme.

  • --theme classic (the default) reproduces the original figures. PNGs are pixel-identical to the originals, and SVG and PDF are identical apart from their metadata.
  • --theme mcscan3 is the MCscan3 house style. It uses white panels without a grid and a restrained frame. Colours named by letter in the plots (b, g, r, m, y, c, k) are drawn from the colour-blind-safe Okabe–Ito palette.
mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.anchors --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed --theme mcscan3 --format png

Every saved figure records Creator: MCscan3 <version> in its metadata (PNG, PDF and SVG). Nothing is added to the visible image.

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text:
mcscan3 plot gallery renders every plot from the test data into one HTML page for review. Each figure is shown in both themes, next to the reference image of the original tool:

mcscan3 plot gallery --tests-dir=tests -o gallery     # then open gallery/index.html
mcscan3 plot gallery --only dotplot --only karyotype  # a subset

The command needs a source checkout (it reads tests/golden and tests/data). It exits with status 1 if any figure fails to render; the error is shown on the page.

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text: Every figure on this page comes from one run of mcscan3 pipeline run on six flowering-plant genomes: Amborella trichopoda, Arabidopsis thaliana, grape, peach, poplar and soybean (209,882 genes in all). They were regenerated with python tools/make_docs_gallery.py <run>. Click a figure to open it full size.

docs.title: Interactive dot plot
docs.text:
Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click a chromosome name to zoom to it, and hover over a dot to see its two genes. Dots are coloured by Orthology Index: blue and orange blocks are orthologous synteny (forward and inverted), and grey blocks come from older duplications. Open it on its own page.

mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.lifted.anchors --oi grape.peach.oi -o grape.peach.html

docs.title: Synteny
docs.text: Dot plot of grape vs peach: peach chromosomes are ordered and flipped along grape, and older duplications are grey. plot dotplot --theme mcscan3 --oi Soybean against itself: the two recent WGDs make every region appear about four times. 125 unplaced scaffolds are hidden. plot dotplot --theme mcscan3 Riparian plot: syntenic orthologous blocks between neighbouring genomes, coloured by the grape chromosome they descend from. plot riparian, pan genes

docs.title: Whole-genome duplications
docs.text: Ks of duplicated blocks in soybean, with a log-normal mixture: the peaks at Ks 0.15 and 0.65 are the two soybean WGDs. wgd blocks, wgd mix --plot WGDs on the species tree: the γ triplication, Arabidopsis α and β, two soybean WGDs and the salicoid WGD, each placed where block ratio, quota ratio, Ks peaks and the gene trees of its syntenic paralogs agree. wgd consensus

docs.title: Ancestral genomes
docs.text: Ancestral karyotypes on the species tree: the root's ancestral chromosomes (colours) traced through every reconstructed ancestor and painted on the extant genomes. ancestral tree-karyotype One ancestor painted on every genome. ancestral karyotype Fusions, fissions, translocations and duplications on each branch. ancestral tree-karyotype

docs.title: Many genomes
docs.text: Synteny similarity between genomes, raw (lower) and corrected for phylogenetic distance (upper). network plot Phylogenomic profile: presence of the largest syntenic clusters in each genome. network plot

docs.title: The pipeline report
docs.text:
The report of pipeline run: an interactive dot plot of every pair of genomes, plus pan-genes, ancestral karyotypes, duplicate classes and WGDs. See the report.

Two styles

Every figure on this page uses the MCscan3 house style. The commands ported from JCVI draw in the original JCVI style by default, pixel for pixel. Pass --theme mcscan3 for the house style. See plotting and themes.

docs.title: Quick start: grape vs peach
docs.text:
This tutorial reproduces the classic MCscan tutorial (grape vs peach) with MCscan3 commands. Starting from genome annotations, you find syntenic blocks and draw them as a dot plot, a karyotype and a local synteny view.

The commands below run as written on the small test data in the MCscan3 repository (tests/data: grape chromosomes 6 and 8, peach chromosome 6, from Ensembl Plants). The test suite runs them (tests/test_tutorial.py), so they stay correct. With your own genomes, use your file names.

docs.title: 0. Install
docs.text:
pip install mcscan3              # add [phylo] for tree drawing
mamba install -c bioconda last   # the default aligner (lastal/lastdb)

docs.title: 1. Prepare the inputs
docs.text:
Each genome needs a BED file of genes (one representative transcript per gene) and the matching CDS sequences, named <species>.bed and <species>.cds.

mcscan3 prep gff2bed grape.gff3.gz --type=mRNA --key=transcript_id --primary-only -o grape.bed
mcscan3 prep gff2bed peach.gff3.gz --type=mRNA --key=transcript_id --primary-only -o peach.bed
mcscan3 prep fasta-format grape.cds.fa.gz grape.cds
mcscan3 prep fasta-format peach.cds.fa.gz peach.cds

--key names the GFF attribute that matches the FASTA headers. For Ensembl this is transcript_id; for Phytozome it is Name. --primary-only keeps the first transcript of each gene; use --longest to keep the one with the longest CDS instead.

docs.title: 2. Find syntenic blocks
docs.text:
mcscan3 ortholog run grape peach --no-strip-names --cpus=1

This aligns the CDS sets with LAST, filters the hits, finds syntenic anchors, and extends them by liftover. It writes grape.peach.anchors (the blocks, separated by ###), the lifted anchors and a dot plot, grape.peach.pdf.

docs.title: 3. Look at the blocks
docs.text:
mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.anchors
mcscan3 synteny depth grape.peach.anchors --histogram

The depth histogram (grape.peach.depth.pdf) shows how many peach regions match each grape region, and the reverse. The pattern it reports (for example 1:1) is what you pass as --quota to keep that many blocks per region.

docs.title: 4. Macrosynteny: a karyotype plot
docs.text:
Keep the larger blocks and write them in the compact .simple format:

mcscan3 synteny screen grape.peach.anchors grape.peach.anchors.new --minspan=30 --simple

Then describe the tracks. seqids lists the chromosomes of each genome:

Vv06,Vv08
Pp06

layout places the tracks and says which blocks join them:

# y, xstart, xend, rotation, color, label, va,  bed
 .6,     .1,    .8,       0,      m, Grape, top, grape.bed
 .4,     .1,    .8,       0,      c, Peach, bottom, peach.bed
# edges
e, 0, 1, grape.peach.anchors.simple

mcscan3 plot karyotype seqids layout

docs.title: 5. Microsynteny: a local view
docs.text:
Stack the peach matches along the grape genome (one column per track):

mcscan3 synteny mcscan grape.bed grape.peach.lifted.anchors --iter=1 -o grape.peach.i1.blocks

Pick a region of grape.peach.i1.blocks (a few dozen consecutive lines), and draw it with mcscan3 plot microsynteny using a layout with one line per track. See plot microsynteny.

docs.title: 6. Figures in the MCscan3 style
docs.text:
Every plot command accepts --theme mcscan3, which gives white panels and colour-blind-safe colours, and --format png|svg|pdf. When an output name with an extension is given, that extension wins, and plot karyotype writes karyotype.pdf unless told otherwise:

mcscan3 plot karyotype seqids layout --theme mcscan3 -o karyotype.png

docs.title: Coming from JCVI?
docs.text:
The same steps written as JCVI command lines run unchanged after mcscan3 legacy:

mcscan3 legacy compara.catalog ortholog grape peach --no_strip_names

See Migrating from JCVI.

docs.title: Parity
docs.text:
Every analysis feature (all groups except plot, and phylo draw, which is a figure) is parity-verified: its outputs are byte-identical to the JCVI v1.6.7 golden outputs, and its report text matches the original's.

Group Features Status prep 4 all parity-verified align 3 all parity-verified filter 4 all parity-verified synteny 19 all parity-verified quota 1 parity-verified ortholog 8 all parity-verified ks 8 all parity-verified (multireport and the report --pdf figure are verified by image comparison) fractionation 7 + 4 7 parity-verified; napus, merge, segment, offdiag are legacy-only (hard-coded B. napus study code) ancestral 5 all parity-verified pad 2 all parity-verified synfind 1 parity-verified (both scoring modes) phylo 2 of 3 prepare, build parity-verified; draw is ported with the graphics (Phase 4)

Ten features crash on every run in JCVI v1.6.7. For these, the reference is JCVI plus the minimal fixes in tools/jcvi_fixes.patch (the golden cases ending in -fixed, decided at Checkpoint 0). All other outputs come from unmodified JCVI.

What the parity tests do not cover byte-for-byte, and why:

  • phylo build: PhyML seeds its random generator from the clock, so two JCVI runs may root the same tree differently. Trees are compared as unrooted splits with branch lengths. The NJ step needs EMBOSS PHYLIP, which is not packaged for osx-arm64; its failure path matches the golden, but its success path is untested.
  • align blast/align diamond stdout (tool chatter with timestamps) and the report of ortholog run with BLAST/DIAMOND.
  • phylo prepare gene order within each family file (hash-seed dependent in the original).

docs.title: Deviations
docs.text:
See DEVIATIONS.md. In summary:

  • 20 JCVI defects are catalogued (section A). Crashes are fixed by default; silent result changes keep the original behaviour, with an opt-in fix.
  • Platform and representation notes are in section C. These include C printf and Cython BlastLine emulation, the Unix sort emulation, sorted outputs where the original order depended on the hash seed, and the dropped seaborn/palettable/R dependencies.

docs.title: Runtime versus JCVI
docs.text:
tools/bench.py runs each golden case with JCVI (golden environment) and MCscan3 (fresh processes, same inputs). Times are wall-clock seconds, from one run on an Apple-silicon laptop.

Area JCVI MCscan3 Ratio prep (gff2bed, fasta-format, bed) 0.5–3.1 s 0.4–3.1 s 0.69–1.07 align last / blast (aligner-bound) 7–50 s 6–57 s 0.89–1.14 filter blastfilter / cscore / rbbh 0.6–1.1 s 0.6–1.2 s 0.80–1.05 filter best 0.6–0.7 s 0.7–0.8 s 0.97–1.22 synteny (19 features) 0.5–4.5 s 0.2–1.1 s 0.09–1.00 quota align 1.0–1.3 s 0.6–0.8 s 0.58–0.61 ortholog run (end to end, incl. LAST/BLAST/DIAMOND) 14–79 s 9–73 s 0.66–0.98 other ortholog, ks, fractionation, ancestral, pad, synfind, phylo 0.4–7 s 0.2–3.2 s 0.06–0.97

The BLAST-line question from Phase 2: the pure-Python BlastLine is 3.8x slower than the compiled original per line. End to end, it is not a bottleneck. filter blastfilter runs at 0.80–1.02x JCVI, synteny scan at 0.63–0.73x, and ortholog run at 0.66–0.98x, because MCscan3 starts faster and avoids subprocess round trips. No compiled accelerator is needed.

The only case above 1x beyond measurement noise was filter best, which sorts the BLAST file like Unix sort. The emulation now uses stable key passes instead of a comparison function (7x faster, identical order), which brought it from 2.3–3.3x down to 0.97–1.22x.

docs.title: Checkpoint 4: graphics ported (2026-09-29)
docs.text: All 13 plot features, ks multireport, phylo draw and the dot plot of ortholog run are ported and parity-verified. The original look is the default (--theme classic), and --theme mcscan3 gives the house style. mcscan3 plot gallery renders every figure in both themes next to the original's reference (see Figures and gallery).

docs.title: Image comparison
docs.text:
The goldens were drawn by JCVI with matplotlib 3.11.2, the same version MCscan3 uses. Comparisons are exact unless a tolerance is shown. PNG is compared pixel by pixel. SVG and PDF are compared byte for byte after removing the metadata block, because MCscan3 records itself as the Creator.

Figure Golden cases Result plot dotplot PNG, SVG identical ortholog run dot plot 6 PDFs (LAST, BLAST, DIAMOND, protein, full, quota) identical plot karyotype PNG, SVG (--seed=666) identical plot microsynteny PNG, SVG identical plot ribbon PNG, SVG identical plot chromosome PNG, SVG (--seed=666) identical plot blastplot PNG, SVG (+ .sizes files) identical plot tree PNG, SVG identical plot heatmap PNG, SVG identical plot ks, ks report --pdf PNG, SVG runs (the figure is always Ks_plot.pdf) identical ks multireport PNG identical plot depth (synteny depth --histogram) PDF identical plot glyph-demo PDF identical plot gene-structure PDF identical plot histogram text mode identical; figures are new (the original used R) phylo draw PDF, PNG from JCVI + patch in the Python 3.10 environment (matplotlib 3.10.9) tree identical; RMS 6.1 because matplotlib 3.10.9 drew the italic leaf names upright (tolerance 8)

Every test also checks Creator: MCscan3 <version> in the figure metadata.

docs.title: What made exact parity possible
docs.text:
• The seaborn theme values that JCVI applies (rcParams and remapped colour codes, for example "k" drawn as #1a1a1a) are recorded as data, as are the ColorBrewer tables. Neither seaborn nor palettable is a dependency.
  • Each figure starts from a clean matplotlib state, as a fresh JCVI process did.

docs.title: Crashes fixed while porting the graphics (see DEVIATIONS.md)
docs.text: dotplot --synteny (A.19), ks --fill (A.20), synteny --tree (A.21), ribbon without --reorient (A.13), ribbon with --annotations, --scalebar, --tree or 11-column layouts (A.22), and the phylo draw crash (A.12). ks report --fit works without the external gmm-bic program (A.14).

Check Result pip install . in a fresh Python 3.12 environment without JCVI, then the full test suite (including the slow aligner tests) 355 passed (13.5 min). pad cluster needs MCSCAN3_CLUSTER_PATH when graphviz's cluster shadows CLUSTER 3.0 on PATH grep -rni jcvi src/ only the attribution headers (103 files), the legacy layer, and the citation and credits text in __about__.py import mcscan3, then importing all 150 modules no jcvi module loaded Registry statuses 78 parity-verified, 4 legacy-only with written reasons (tested in tests/test_registry.py) mkdocs build --strict no warnings The MCscan tutorial through mcscan3 legacy runs unchanged apart from the prefix; outputs identical to JCVI's (tests/test_tutorial.py) The quick-start tutorial, new syntax its commands, read from the doc page, reproduce the same outputs Migration guide docs/MIGRATION_FROM_JCVI.md, generated from the registry and kept in sync by a test
