docs.title: Phase 6: new analyses (2026-09-29)
docs.text:
These are the features requested after the extraction (see ROADMAP.md). Each reimplements a published method from its paper, with no code taken from those tools, and cites it on its documentation page. Their registry status is new.

Command Method How it is tested prep genome longest coding transcript per gene, CDS spliced from the genome and translated synthetic genome (minus strand, phase, isoforms, non-coding); same transcripts as prep gff2bed --longest on the peach annotation dup classify DupGen_finder classes, from the paper synthetic genome with a known class for every pair; grape run looks plausible ortholog soi Orthology Index filtering (SOI) constructed blocks with known OI; pairs, OrthoFinder and BLAST RBH inputs wgd ksd paranome (MCL + node weighting) or anchor Ks; yn00 or codeml (pairwise ML) anchor Ks equals JCVI ks calc (golden) to 1e-3; node weights on a known family wgd peaks, wgd mix, wgd blocks KDE peaks; GMM, ELMM (exponential background + log-normal peaks) and Bayesian GMM, chosen by BIC/AIC, multi-start EM, warm-start bootstrap intervals, saturation warning; per-block median Ks ELMM recovers background + peak and picks the no-WGD null on exponential data; weights equal repeated data; grape: the paranome ELMM and the block-level GMM both put γ at Ks 1.36 wgd correct relative rate correction with an outgroup (ksrates) exact numbers; bootstrap on synthetic distributions wgd tree-map Tree2GD-style LCA reconciliation duplications at known nodes; rooting, support and coverage filters pan genes, plot riparian GENESPACE-style pan-genes and braids three synthetic genomes with transitive synteny and neighbour placement; colour propagation network build, cluster, profile, tree synteny networks (Zhao & Schranz) four synthetic species: clusters, profiles and the tree ((A,B),(C,D))

The full suite has 386 tests, plus 22 slow tests that run external aligners. mypy and ruff are clean.

docs.title: Figures, report and documentation site (2026-10-15)
docs.text:
The figures, the pipeline and the documentation were made into one consistent system.

  • House style (mcscan3.plot.style). Every figure that is new in MCscan3 shares its colours, fonts, layout, title and subtitle, and output settings. The mcscan3 theme lists only fonts that are installed, which ends a flood of findfont warnings. Ported figures keep --theme classic byte for byte.
  • Modern dot plot. Chromosome names are shortened and non-overlapping, unplaced scaffolds are hidden (with a note), and the heading is measured to sit above the labels.
  • Interactive dot plots (plot dotplot -o x.html, and every pair in the report). The page draws on a canvas: zoom, pan, click a chromosome to zoom to it, see the genes on hover, and colour by orientation, block or Orthology Index. It needs no network access.
  • Pipeline. run.json records the status, time and notes of every step, plus the report's results. --steps re-runs only the steps given; pipeline report <outdir> rebuilds the report. A table of the steps is printed at the end of each run.
  • Report. Sidebar, summary cards, interactive dot plots, stacked bars, lightbox, sortable tables, dark mode and a table of the run.
  • Documentation site. Material for MkDocs with tabs, a landing page, a gallery made from a six-eudicot run (tools/make_docs_gallery.py) and an embedded interactive dot plot. GitHub Pages deploys it (.github/workflows/docs.yml), and the build fails if the command pages are out of date.
  • Fixes. network plot --kind profile crashed with a RecursionError: with few genomes, scipy's dendrogram recursed through a chain-like tree. The dot plot's orientation palette crashed when some anchors were on hidden scaffolds.

Validated by re-running the six-eudicot pipeline (all steps done), and by checking the report and the site in headless Chromium (no script errors; hover, zoom and pair switching all work).

docs.title: WGDs placed by syntenic paralogs in gene trees (2026-10-22)
docs.text:
• Anchored placement (wgd tree-map --paralogs pairs.tsv --outgroup X). This reimplements PUG (McKain et al. 2016) from the paper:
  • gene trees are rooted on the outgroup's genes when they form a clade, else on the fewest duplications;
  • each paralog pair's last common ancestor is mapped to the species tree, and kept when both child clades hold at least half the species below it;
  • each gene tree gives one vote per event and node;
  • supports, when present, are filtered, and votes at ≥80% support are counted separately.

It writes <prefix>.events.tsv. * wgd consensus, gene-tree line. * The noisy count of duplication bursts is replaced. Each genome's self-synteny anchors are labelled by the Ks mixture component of their block, then placed in the gene trees (consensus.events.tsv). * A Ks peak with fewer than --min-tree-rate (0.05) gene trees per pair is rejected, and it loses its Ks vote too. Such pairs come from tandem arrays or a few large families. * A placement split between two adjacent branches is flagged as possible allopolyploidy. * Bursts remain the fallback when there are no syntenic paralogs. * Counting. Ks peaks less than 1.35 times apart count as one event. Ks and gene-tree counts are capped by the copy ratios when those saw events on the branch. * Fixes. * wgd consensus computed ortholog Ks with PAML yn00, so without PAML the Ks line silently gave nothing. It now uses the native LPB93 estimator, like pipeline run --ks. * pipeline run --steps lost the reference, tree and orthology of the earlier run and reran the all-vs-all orthology search. _previous now restores them, and run.json also records the orthologues directory.

Validated on the six-eudicot run (OrthoFinder gene trees, 12,112 used) with the OrthoFinder species tree and with the accepted one. The calls:

branch before now core-eudicot stem γ triplication γ triplication (4/4) Arabidopsis missed α and β (2/4; 4/4 on the accepted tree) soybean 2 WGDs 2 WGDs poplar 1 WGD 1 WGD grape false 1 WGD none

The false grape call came from a Ks component at 0.35: 7,594 pairs in only 60 gene trees, now rejected. Grape's γ peak (Ks 1.45) and peach's (1.64) are placed on the core-eudicot stem by the gene trees, even where Ks alone placed peach's deeper.

docs.title: 2026-10-22: benchmark framework, synteny-constrained anchoring, MMseqs2, annotation transfer
docs.text:
Work for the NAR paper (docs/development/PAPER_PLAN.md).

  • bench simulate / bench score. A genome-evolution simulator that writes a known answer:
  • codon-level divergence with a per-gene ω, so Ks matches the branch length;
  • rearrangements, tandem and dispersed duplications, and losses;
  • WGDs, triplications and allopolyploidy, with biased fractionation;
  • a genealogy-based truth: orthologs, ohnologs, positional pairs, events and ancestral orders.

bench score gives the precision and recall of anchors against that truth. * synteny anchor. Synteny-constrained anchoring, reimplemented from the GENESPACE paper: * collapses tandem arrays; * chains on condensed gene ranks; * rescues hits within a buffer; * finds secondary blocks.

New in MCscan3 is block-local best-hit extension with a C-score filter. The new defaults are --hits 2 (4 for a genome against itself), --secondary 3 and --mask-buffer 100. They were tuned on the simulated polyploids, where F1 is at least 0.998 in every case. * align mmseqs, and ortholog run --align-soft mmseqs. * annotate transfer. Annotation transfer from one or more references: * splice alignment with minimap2; * each gene's copy chosen by synteny with its flanking anchors; * ORF check and repair; * a union across references. * benchmarks/. A synteny benchmark with these methods, all run on shared DIAMOND hits: MCscan3 anchor, MCscan3 classic, MCScanX and GENESPACE 1.3.1. Peak memory comes from /usr/bin/time. * CLI help. [default: …] text was being stripped by rich markup; it now reads (default: …).

docs.title: MCscan3 extraction plan
docs.text: Source: JCVI v1.6.7 (e10b884), see SOURCE_VERSION.md. Generated with tools/inventory.py (actions) and tools/import_graph.py (imports).

docs.title: 1. Inventory vs. Feature Map
docs.text:
tools/inventory.py confirms every action in the Feature Map exists in JCVI v1.6.7, and that every action of the fully in-scope modules (compara.*, apps.phylo, graphics.* listed) is mapped. Differences and corrections:

Item Finding Proposed action align diamond Not new. JCVI has apps.align.diamond_blastp_main (a function, not a listed action), used by catalog ortholog --align_soft diamond_blastp. Port it as a normal feature; JCVI source = apps.align diamond_blastp_main. plot dotplot No main(); entry point is dotplot_main() under if __name__ == "__main__". Map to graphics.dotplot dotplot_main. plot blastplot No main(); argument parsing is inline in the __main__ block. Map to graphics.blastplot __main__. prep gff2bed longest isoform JCVI gff bed --primary_only keeps the first transcript seen per --parent_key, not the longest. There is no longest-isoform option in gff bed. Parity: keep first-seen as --primary-only. Proposal: add opt-in --longest (new, documented in DEVIATIONS). Needs confirmation. quota align solvers v1.6.7 solves via OR-Tools pywraplp (bundled SCIP backend) first; external scip / glpsol binaries are only fallbacks. Default: OR-Tools SCIP (parity). Fallbacks: GLPK (glpsol), external SCIP. Add HiGHS (highspy) as opt-in. compara.phylogeny lcn Low-copy-number gene selection from OrthoFinder output. Not MCscan-related. Out of scope. compara.pedigree Pedigree/inbreeding. Not MCscan. Out of scope. graphics.align, graphics.wheel, graphics.landscape, graphics.mummerplot, graphics.coverage, graphics.table, graphics.assembly, graphics.grabseeds Not MCscan-related. Out of scope. fractionation napus/merge/segment Project-specific (B. napus). legacy-only unless Haibao confirms.

Minor JCVI bugs noticed so far (logging only, no output change): formats.bed fix/some call logger.debug("...%s".format(x)), so the value is never interpolated. Will record in DEVIATIONS.md when ported.

docs.title: 2. Import graph summary
docs.text: The JCVI internal graph is densely cyclic (apps.base ↔ formats.base ↔ utils.cbook, formats.sizes ↔ formats.agp, etc.), so the transitive closure of every in-scope module is ~35 modules including assembly, AWS, grid, OBO/GO, SAM, and uclust code. Almost all of that is reached only through module-level imports used by out-of-scope actions. The plan below is therefore driven by the names that in-scope code actually calls (tools/import_graph.py --names).

docs.title: 3. Decision per dependency
docs.text: Legend: core = port into mcscan3.core, io = port into mcscan3.io, plot = port into mcscan3.plot, replace = use a standard library / third-party package, drop = not needed.

docs.title: apps
docs.text: JCVI module Names used by in-scope code Decision apps.base OptionParser, ActionDispatcher drop → Typer CLI (mcscan3.cli). Option names/defaults preserved per feature. logger replace → logging.getLogger("mcscan3") configured in mcscan3.log (rich handler optional). sh, popen, Popen, which, getpath, need_update, mkdir, cleanup, get_abs_path, glob, iglob core → mcscan3.core.shell (subprocess-based, same semantics incl. need_update skip logic). getpath reads tool paths from env vars (MCSCAN3_<TOOL>) instead of ~/.jcvirc. flatten, parse_multi_values, sample_N, datafile core → mcscan3.core.utils; datafile only needed for hg38 files in graphics.chromosome (see below). apps.align last, blast_main, diamond_blastp_main, run_lastdb, run_formatdb, run_diamond_makedb Feature modules features/align/{last,blast,diamond}.py. apps.grid MakeManager (only ks batch in scope) replace → write a Makefile as JCVI does (small port into core.shell), or run sequentially. Output parity is on the generated makefile + results. apps.r RTemplate (only graphics.histogram) drop → matplotlib reimplementation (spec). apps.phylo feature module Feature modules features/phylo/*. apps.fetch, apps.cdhit, apps.uclust, apps.biomart only via out-of-scope code drop

docs.title: formats
docs.text: JCVI module Names used Decision formats.base BaseFile, LineFile, DictFile, SetFile, must_open, read_block, flexible_cast, get_number, is_number, longest_unique_prefix, write_file io → mcscan3.io.base. must_open keeps -/stdout, .gz, .bz2 handling. formats.bed Bed, BedLine, BedSummary, sort, sizes, intersectBed_wao, merge, uniq io → mcscan3.io.bed (Bed, BedLine, order, order_in_chr, sort). intersectBed_wao → core.bedtools (calls bedtools intersect -wao, as JCVI). merge/uniq → prep features. Coverage, BinFile, pybedtools, histogram imports are only used by out-of-scope actions → drop. formats.blast Blast, BlastLine, filter, cscore, best, rbbh, filtered_blastfile_name, bed io → mcscan3.io.blast (Blast, BlastLine, BlastSlow); filter pieces used by the pipeline → core; cscore/best/rbbh → filter features. formats/cblast.pyx BlastLine (Cython) replace with pure-Python BlastLine (ported from formats/pyblast.py, __slots__). Benchmark vs. cblast in Phase 2; revisit (Polars / optional compiled ext) only if >3× slower. formats.pyblast BlastLine io (basis of the pure-Python reader). formats.fasta Fasta, translate, some, format replace Fasta with Biopython SeqIO.index wrapper (mcscan3.io.fasta); format → prep fasta-format; translate (used by ks prepare, phylo prepare) → port the function into mcscan3.io.fasta. formats.agp, formats.fastq, assembly.base imports → drop (out-of-scope actions only). formats.gff Gff, GffLine, bed io → mcscan3.io.gff (pure-Python line parser as in JCVI; gffutils, BCBio, annotation.reformat.atg_name, formats.obo only used by other actions → drop). formats.sizes Sizes io → mcscan3.io.sizes; build from FASTA with Biopython; agp helper drop. formats.sam, formats.fastq, formats.agp, formats.obo only out-of-scope drop

docs.title: compara (shared, non-feature code)
docs.text: JCVI Names used Decision compara.base AnchorFile io → mcscan3.io.anchors (AnchorFile, print_to_anchors, blast iterator, block splitting on ###). compara.synteny (shared parts) BlockFile, SimpleFile, check_beds, read_blast, batch_scan, get_orientation, _score, screen io: BlockFile → io.blocks, SimpleFile → io.simple. core: check_beds, read_blast, batch_scan, _score, get_orientation → mcscan3.core.synteny. Each action → its own features/synteny/*.py. compara.ks (shared) KsFile, AbstractCommandline, run_mrtrans, clustal_align_protein, muscle_align_protein, find_first_isoform io KsFile → io.ks; command wrappers → core.external (used by ks and phylo).

docs.title: algorithms / utils
docs.text: JCVI Names used Decision utils.grouper Grouper core → core.grouper algorithms.lis longest_increasing_subsequence, longest_decreasing_subsequence, heaviest_increasing_subsequence core → core.lis utils.range Range, range_chain, range_depth, range_distance, range_interleave, range_minmax, range_overlap, range_span, range_union, range_piles, LEFT, RIGHT core → core.range (drop more_itertools where trivial). algorithms.lpsolve MIPDataModel (+ SCIPSolver, GLPKSolver fallbacks) core → core.lpsolve. OR-Tools default; GLPK/SCIP executables; HiGHS optional. tsp, hamiltonian, min_feedback_arc_set drop (not used by in-scope code). algorithms.graph BiGraph (ancestral), merge_paths (synteny from-spa) core → core.graph (networkx). pygraphviz only for drawing in ancestral adjgraph → optional extra. algorithms.ec GA_setup, GA_run (synteny layout) core → core.ec with deap as optional dependency ([ga] extra). GA is stochastic: parity test must fix the seed and verify JCVI output is reproducible with it. algorithms.matrix, algorithms.maxsum, algorithms.supermap, algorithms.tsp only out-of-scope drop utils.cbook SummaryStats, gene_name, human_size, percentage, thousands, uniqify, seqid_parse, Registry, AutoVivification, fixChromName core → core.utils. utils.table tabulate, write_csv, banner core → core.table. utils.orderedcollections OrderedDict, DefaultOrderedDict, parse_qs replace → stdlib dict / collections; parse_qs → port into io.gff. utils.validator validate_in_choices, validate_in_range replace → Typer choices / click.IntRange. utils.aws via formats.base only drop assembly.base (calculate_A50), assembly.goldenpath, assembly.coverage formats.blast's summary/anchors actions only drop (the spec's formats.blast → assembly.base concern is resolved: not on any in-scope path). annotation.reformat, graphics.landscape only out-of-scope drop

docs.title: graphics
docs.text: JCVI Decision graphics.base (savefig, AbstractLayout, markup, latex, normalize_axes, set_human_axis, palettes set1/set2/set3, discrete_rainbow, draw_cmap, asciiplot, quickplot, …) plot → mcscan3.plot.base. savefig writes Creator: MCscan3 <version> metadata. setup_theme (seaborn) → mcscan3.plot.theme with a jcvi theme (default, parity) and an mcscan3 theme. palettable → inline the few palettes used. set_chinese_font, TeX detection kept minimal. graphics.glyph plot → mcscan3.plot.glyph; demo / gff actions → plot features. graphics.chromosome feature + shared Chromosome, HorizontalChromosome → plot.chromosome_glyphs. hg38 cytoband data files (datafile) → ship only if needed by in-scope options; otherwise drop (human-specific). graphics.synteny (Shade, ymid_offset) and graphics.tree (draw_tree, read_trees) shared helpers → plot, used by karyotype/microsynteny/ribbon. ete4 becomes a [plot]/[tree] optional dependency. graphics.histogram plot → matplotlib rewrite; ASCII mode (stem_leaf_plot, asciiplot) ported as-is. R dependency dropped (parity on ASCII text output; images compared at looser tolerance, documented).

docs.title: 4. Third-party dependencies
docs.text:
Package Needed by MCscan3 status numpy, scipy synteny, ks, pad, plots required matplotlib plots [plot] extra biopython fasta, ks, phylo required natsort bed sorting, chromosome order required networkx core.graph required ortools quota (default solver) required (parity); highspy optional more-itertools range/pad replace with stdlib where trivial, otherwise required rich logging/progress optional deap synteny layout GA [ga] extra ete4 tree drawing, phylo [tree] extra pygraphviz ancestral adjgraph drawing [graphviz] extra seaborn, palettable JCVI theme dropped (palettes inlined) — verify image parity in Phase 4 boto3, ftpretty, genomepy, gffutils, goatools, pysam, pybedtools, CrossMap, pytesseract, Wand, scikit-image, pyefd, pypdf, webcolors, jinja2, graphviz, BCBio out-of-scope code only dropped

External executables (called via core.shell, paths overridable by env var): lastdb/lastal, makeblastdb/blastn/blastp, diamond, glpsol/scip (fallback), bedtools, clustalw2, muscle, pal2nal.pl, yn00, phyml, raxmlHPC, Gblocks, EMBOSS PHYLIP, TreeFix.

docs.title: 5. Golden-output coverage (Phase 0 result)
docs.text:
tools/make_golden.sh defines 141 cases covering all 79 Feature Map commands (see tests/golden/INDEX.md).

  • 127 cases are reference outputs (JCVI succeeded); 14 are expected failures that document JCVI defects (docs/DEVIATIONS.md §A).
  • 69 features have at least one reference output.
  • 10 features have only expected-failure goldens because every invocation hits a JCVI defect: synteny from-spa, synteny layout, ortholog enrich, ortholog layout, ks gc3, fractionation validate, fractionation gff-select, phylo prepare, phylo build, phylo draw. These need a decision on what the parity reference should be (Checkpoint 0, question 1).
  • ks calc and phylo * goldens come from .venv-jcvi-legacy (Biopython 1.78).
  • Determinism verified with --check; the only differences between two JCVI runs are tool chatter on stdout and an R-generated PDF timestamp.

docs.title: 6. Phase 2 results: shared core and file formats
docs.text:
Ported: core.grouper, core.lis, core.range, core.utils, core.cformat (new), core.synteny (scan, liftover, BLAST-to-rank), core.lpsolve (OR-Tools default, SCIP/GLPK fallbacks, HiGHS opt-in), io.base, io.bed, io.blast, io.anchors, io.blocks, io.simple, io.sizes, io.layout.

Parity: tools/make_unit_golden.py runs the original functions on the real test data and seeded random inputs; tests/core and tests/io recompute everything with MCscan3 and compare exactly (including OR-Tools selecting the same blocks on three real quota instances).

BlastLine benchmark (185,849 lines, parse only, loaded machine): compiled original 0.17 s, MCscan3 pure Python 0.63 s (3.8x). The per-line micro-benchmark is above the 3x guideline; the relevant end-to-end comparison (filter blastfilter, synteny scan, ortholog run vs JCVI) is measured in Phase 3. If it stays above 3x, options are a vectorised reader for whole files or an optional compiled accelerator.

Phase 3 note: ancestral adjgraph writes DOT through mcscan3.core.dot (a Graphviz-compatible writer) instead of pygraphviz; the output is byte-identical to the original's, so pygraphviz and the Graphviz C library are not needed.

docs.title: MCscan3 Extraction and Rebranding: AI Coding-Agent Prompt
docs.text: How to use. Paste everything below the line into an agentic coding tool (for example Claude Code) opened in an empty folder on your Mac. The agent downloads JCVI itself. It works in phases and stops after each one for your review; reply "continue" to go on. This prompt is a more detailed replacement for Phases 0 to 3 of the earlier MCscan3_agent_prompt.md.

docs.title: ROLE AND GOAL
docs.text:
You are a senior bioinformatics software engineer. Build MCscan3, a standalone, rebranded Python package containing every MCscan-related feature of JCVI, with each feature implemented as its own separate module, command, test file and documentation page.

MCscan3 is the official successor to MCScan (2008), JCVI's Python MCscan, and MCScanX (2012). The original authors, Haibao Tang and Yupeng Wang, are on the team and will review the code.

Success means: 1. pip install . works on a clean machine with no jcvi package installed. 2. Every JCVI MCscan feature listed in the Feature Map below exists as a separate MCscan3 feature. 3. Every feature produces the same results as JCVI on the test data (parity tests). 4. The branding is consistent everywhere, while JCVI and the original authors are properly credited.

docs.title: NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES
docs.text:
• Parity first. Ported features must reproduce JCVI outputs exactly. If you find a bug in JCVI, keep the original behaviour as the default, add an opt-in flag for the fix, and record it in docs/DEVIATIONS.md.
  • Attribution. JCVI is BSD-licensed. Keep its copyright notice in LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY, and put a header in every derived file: # Derived from JCVI <original path> (BSD license), commit <hash>.
  • Only JCVI code. Do not copy code from any other tool in this task.
  • One feature at a time. Port, test and commit each feature separately. Never leave the test suite failing at a commit.
  • Stop at every checkpoint with a short report: what was done, test results, problems, and open questions. Ask instead of guessing on design decisions not covered here.
  • Python 3.10+, type hints on public functions, docstrings, ruff and mypy clean, pytest for tests.

docs.title: BRANDING SPECIFICATION
docs.text:
Item Value Product name MCscan3 (always this capitalization in text) PyPI / import name mcscan3 Command-line tool mcscan3 Starting version 0.1.0.dev0 (single source of truth in src/mcscan3/__about__.py) Tagline "Synteny, whole-genome duplication and genome evolution analysis" License BSD-3-Clause for new code; JCVI notice kept in LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY Credits line "MCscan3 builds on MCScan and JCVI (Haibao Tang) and MCScanX (Yupeng Wang)."

Branding must appear in all of these places: - mcscan3 --version prints the name, version, tagline, credits line, and "Cite: run mcscan3 cite". - mcscan3 cite prints citations for MCScan (Tang et al. 2008), MCScanX (Wang et al. 2012) and JCVI (Tang et al. 2024, iMeta), plus MCscan3 once published. Also provide CITATION.cff. - Log messages use the logger name mcscan3 with a consistent format. - Every figure saved by MCscan3 records Creator: MCscan3 <version> in its file metadata (PDF and PNG metadata, SVG comment). No visible watermark. - A shared visual theme module (mcscan3.plot.theme) with default fonts and palettes, including a colour-blind-safe palette. - README.md with a logo placeholder (docs/assets/logo.svg, a simple original text-based design; do not use any existing logos). - A documentation site (MkDocs Material) titled "MCscan3".

After branding is complete, the command grep -rni "jcvi" src/ must return only attribution headers and the legacy alias layer described below.

docs.title: "EACH FEATURE SEPARATELY": REQUIRED STRUCTURE
docs.text:
Every feature gets: 1. Its own module under src/mcscan3/features/<group>/<feature>.py containing a pure Python API function (data in, data out, no printing, no argument parsing). 2. Its own CLI command mcscan3 <group> <feature>, a thin wrapper around the API function. 3. Its own entry in a feature registry (src/mcscan3/registry.py) with: name, group, one-line description, JCVI source (module and action), status (ported, parity-verified, legacy-only), and the test file name. 4. Its own test file tests/features/test_<group>_<feature>.py with at least one parity test against JCVI output. 5. Its own documentation page docs/features/<group>/<feature>.md with purpose, inputs, outputs, options, an example command, and its JCVI equivalent.

Add these supporting commands: - mcscan3 features lists all features from the registry as a table (group, command, status, JCVI equivalent). - mcscan3 legacy <jcvi.module> <action> ... maps old JCVI command lines to the new commands, so python -m jcvi.compara.catalog ortholog grape peach becomes mcscan3 legacy compara.catalog ortholog grape peach. It prints a one-line hint with the new command name.

Shared code (file readers and writers, geometry, the union-find Grouper, LIS, range utilities) goes in src/mcscan3/core/ and src/mcscan3/io/, not inside feature modules.

docs.title: TARGET LAYOUT
docs.text:
mcscan3/
  pyproject.toml          # extras: [plot], [dev]; entry point: mcscan3 = mcscan3.cli:app
  README.md  CITATION.cff  LICENSE  LICENSE-THIRD-PARTY
  src/mcscan3/
    __about__.py  __init__.py  registry.py
    cli/                  # Typer root app, one sub-app per group, legacy aliases
    core/                 # grouper, lis, range, lpsolve wrapper, geometry
    io/                   # bed, blast, anchors, simple, blocks, layout, sizes, fasta, gff
    features/
      prep/ align/ filter/ synteny/ quota/ ortholog/ ks/
      fractionation/ ancestral/ pad/ synfind/ phylo/ plot/
    plot/                 # base, glyph, theme, shared drawing helpers
  tests/
    data/                 # small test genomes
    golden/               # outputs produced by the original JCVI
    features/             # one test file per feature
  docs/
    features/             # one page per feature
    DEVIATIONS.md  MIGRATION_FROM_JCVI.md  SOURCE_VERSION.md  EXTRACTION_PLAN.md

Everything else in JCVI (assembly, annotation, variation, projects, most format tools) is out of scope.

docs.title: PHASE 0: DOWNLOAD, INVENTORY AND GOLDEN OUTPUTS
docs.text:
1. On macOS, check prerequisites and report what is missing: Xcode command line tools, Homebrew, uv (or Python 3.10+), git, and the LAST aligner (brew install last if available, otherwise conda/bioconda). Do not install system software without asking.
  2. Clone JCVI: git clone https://github.com/tanghaibao/jcvi.git vendor/jcvi, check out the latest release tag, and record the tag and commit hash in docs/SOURCE_VERSION.md. Add vendor/ to .gitignore; it is reference material only and must never be imported by mcscan3.
  3. Install that JCVI version into a separate virtual environment (.venv-jcvi) to produce golden outputs. MCscan3's own environment must not contain jcvi.
  4. Write tools/inventory.py that parses every in-scope JCVI module, extracts its actions tuple (or single main), and prints the list. Compare with the Feature Map above and report differences.
  5. Map the internal import graph of all in-scope modules, including transitive imports. In docs/EXTRACTION_PLAN.md, record for each dependency whether it will be ported into core/ or io/, replaced with a standard library (for example Biopython, pyfaidx, natsort), or dropped. Note especially: apps.base (option parsing, sh, logging), formats/cblast.pyx (Cython), formats.blast importing assembly.base, apps.r (R dependency), and algorithms.lpsolve (SCIP/GLPK).
  6. Build test data: the grape and peach example from the JCVI MCscan tutorial, reduced to a few chromosomes so the full test suite runs in under two minutes. Add one small polyploid-versus-diploid pair to exercise quota ratios such as 1:2.
  7. Run the original JCVI on the test data for every feature in the Feature Map and save outputs in tests/golden/<group>/<feature>/, together with the exact command used. Figures: save PNG at fixed DPI plus SVG. Write tools/make_golden.sh to regenerate everything.

Checkpoint 0: inventory differences, extraction plan, test data description, and the list of golden outputs (with any features that could not be run and why).

docs.title: PHASE 1: SKELETON AND BRANDING
docs.text:
1. Create the package layout, pyproject.toml, the Typer CLI with one sub-app per group, the registry, mcscan3 --version, mcscan3 cite, mcscan3 features, the theme module, figure metadata, logging, CITATION.cff, README, license files, and the MkDocs skeleton.
  2. Set up GitHub Actions: ruff, mypy, pytest on macOS and Linux, Python 3.10 to 3.12.
  3. Add a test that fails if any registered feature is missing its module, CLI command, test file or documentation page.

Checkpoint 1: output of mcscan3 --version, mcscan3 features (all features listed as not-ported so far), and CI status.

docs.title: PHASE 2: SHARED CORE AND FILE FORMATS
docs.text:
1. Port the shared pieces into core/ and io/: Grouper, LIS functions, range utilities, BED reader (Bed, BedLine, order, order_in_chr), BLAST reader (replace the Cython cblast with pure Python or Polars unless it is more than 3x slower on the test data), anchors/simple/blocks/layout/seqids readers and writers, sizes, and the quota integer-programming wrapper (support SCIP and GLPK as JCVI does; add HiGHS as an optional solver).
  2. Unit tests for each reader and writer, including round trips.

Checkpoint 2: coverage report for core/ and io/.

docs.title: PHASE 3: PORT FEATURES ONE BY ONE
docs.text:
Port in this order, because later features depend on earlier ones: prep → align → filter → synteny scan/liftover/screen/simple/summary/stats/depth → quota → ortholog run (must reproduce the full tutorial pipeline) → remaining synteny features → ortholog catalog features → ks → fractionation → ancestral, pad, synfind → phylo.

For each feature: 1. Write the pure API function, then the CLI wrapper, registry entry, documentation page and parity test. 2. Parity means byte-identical text output compared with the golden file. If JCVI's output order is not deterministic, sort both sides and document it in the test. 3. Commit with the message feat(<group>): port <feature> from jcvi <module>.<action>. 4. Update the feature's registry status to parity-verified only when its parity test passes.

Checkpoint 3a after ortholog run works end to end, and Checkpoint 3b after all analysis groups: parity table (feature, golden file, pass/fail), deviations, and runtime compared with JCVI.

docs.title: PHASE 4: PORT ALL GRAPHICS
docs.text:
1. Port graphics/base.py and glyph.py into mcscan3.plot, applying the MCscan3 theme without changing default JCVI-looking output unless the user passes --theme mcscan3. Default to the JCVI look for parity.
  2. Port each plot feature separately, following the same five-part structure (module, command, registry, test, docs page).
  3. Test figures with image comparison against the golden PNGs (for example pytest-mpl with a small tolerance), and check that figure metadata contains Creator: MCscan3.
  4. Add mcscan3 plot gallery, which renders every plot from the test data into one HTML page for team review.

Checkpoint 4: the gallery and the image-comparison results.

docs.title: PHASE 5: LEGACY ALIASES, DOCUMENTATION AND FINAL VERIFICATION
docs.text:
1. Implement mcscan3 legacy for every ported JCVI action and test that the JCVI MCscan tutorial runs unchanged except for the prefix.
  2. Write docs/MIGRATION_FROM_JCVI.md: a table of every JCVI command and its MCscan3 equivalent, generated from the registry.
  3. Write a quick-start tutorial reproducing the grape-peach MCscan tutorial with the new commands.
  4. Final checks, reported in the last checkpoint:
  5. pip install . in a fresh environment without jcvi, then run the full test suite.
  6. grep -rni "jcvi" src/ returns only attribution headers and the legacy layer.
  7. python -c "import mcscan3" does not import jcvi (check sys.modules).
  8. Every registry entry has status parity-verified or legacy-only with a written reason.
  9. Build the documentation site without warnings.

Final checkpoint: a release summary suitable for Haibao Tang and Yupeng Wang to review, listing every feature, its status, and any deviations.

docs.title: OUT OF SCOPE
docs.text: New analysis algorithms (Orthology Index, WGD peak fitting, subgenome phasing, networks, pangenomes), the MCScanX C++ engine port, and new plot types. Those are later tasks defined in the MCscan3 Feature Catalog. This task delivers a complete, rebranded, parity-verified MCscan core that they will build on.

docs.title: MCscan3 paper plan (target: Nucleic Acids Research)
docs.text:
Requested by the owner on 2026-10-22: make MCscan3 publishable in NAR, benchmark everything, add GENESPACE-style anchoring, add what PanSyn offers, and add synteny-aware annotation transfer across assemblies of one genus that is better and faster than Liftoff.

The rules of docs/ROADMAP.md still hold. New methods are clean-room reimplementations from papers, cited and never copied. Every feature has a module, CLI, registry entry, tests with a known answer, real-genome validation and a docs page.

docs.title: What NAR expects of a software paper
docs.text:
NAR software papers (main issue, or NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics) are judged on these points:

  1. A clear advance. One package that goes from genomes to synteny, orthology (SOI), WGDs, ancestral karyotypes, pan-genes, networks and annotation transfer, and that is more accurate than the tools it replaces, shown with numbers.
  2. Benchmarks against ground truth (precision and recall), not just "looks similar". The ground truth comes from simulated genomes, plus curated real sets.
  3. Head-to-head comparisons with the tools people use, on the same inputs. Report accuracy, runtime and memory.
  4. Scalability: runtime and memory against genome number and size.
  5. Case studies that show biology the other tools miss.
  6. Availability: open source (BSD-3), pip/bioconda, documentation site, tests and CI, a frozen benchmark archive (Zenodo) and a single command that reproduces every figure.

docs.title: Benchmark framework (Phase A; everything else is measured with it)
docs.text:
benchmarks/ holds the scripts, configurations and the code that makes the figures. The data is fetched by script and never committed.

  • A1. Genome-evolution simulator (mcscan3 bench simulate).
  • Starts from an ancestral genome: chromosomes, genes and protein sequences.
  • Evolves it along a species tree with:
    • WGDs and triplications, followed by biased fractionation;
    • tandem and dispersed duplications;
    • inversions, translocations, fusions and fissions;
    • gene loss and gain;
    • sequence divergence (protein-level substitution with rate variation, and CDS from back-translation so that Ks works).
  • Writes BED, PEP and CDS files, plus the truth:
    • orthologs and syntelogs per pair;
    • syntenic blocks;
    • WGD events and their branches;
    • ancestral karyotypes per node;
    • the origin of every gene.
  • A2. Metrics (benchmarks/metrics.py):
  • anchor precision and recall against true syntelogs;
  • block breakpoint accuracy;
  • ortholog F1 (SOI against OrthoFinder against the truth);
  • WGD placement accuracy;
  • ancestral karyotype accuracy: adjusted Rand index of genes grouped into protochromosomes, and adjacency F1;
  • network-tree Robinson-Foulds distance;
  • annotation-transfer recall, exact-CDS rate and correct-paralog rate.
  • A3. Real sets with curated truth:
  • Arabidopsis α pairs (Bowers et al. 2003; Thomas et al. 2006);
  • the maize-sorghum curated syntenic gene list (Schnable lab);
  • the grape γ triplets (Jaillon et al. 2007);
  • the B. rapa LF/MF1/MF2 subgenomes;
  • the ancestral eudicot karyotype (7 chromosomes before γ, 21 after);
  • the accepted eudicot and grass species trees.
  • A4. Competitors (each installed by script, with versions pinned):
area tools synteny MCScanX, JCVI MCscan, WGDI, GENESPACE, i-ADHoRe 3 orthology OrthoFinder, SOI WGD wgd v2, ksrates, WGDI, Tree2GD ancestral karyotype WGDI, AKRUP, AGORA annotation transfer Liftoff, LiftOn, miniprot

docs.title: Method work, ordered by the paper's needs
docs.text: # Work Measured by B Synteny-constrained anchoring (after GENESPACE, Lovell et al. 2022). Steps: collapse tandem arrays to representatives (gene nearest the array's median position); restrict candidates to hits within an orthogroup and at most ploidy best hits per gene; use gene-rank coordinates of representatives; chain collinear runs (block size 5, gaps 5); rescue every hit within 100 genes of an anchor; cluster anchors into regions; for polyploids, mask the primary hits and search again for secondary (homeologous) blocks. New in MCscan3: the SOI score is used inside the chaining, not only as a filter afterwards, and the buffer is adaptive (set by the local gene density). anchor F1 and share of genes on one chromosome per genome, against MCScanX, JCVI, GENESPACE and WGDI, on simulations and real pairs (maize, cotton, grasses, human-chimp) C WGD placement (done in d71b24f: PUG-style anchored gene-tree placement) placement accuracy on simulated trees; eudicot and grass case studies D Ancestral karyotypes and networks validated against AKRUP and WGDI: the 7 and 21 eudicot protochromosomes, grape triplets, grass ancestral karyotype (n = 12 before ρ), and network trees against accepted trees adjusted Rand index, adjacency F1, Robinson-Foulds distance E Synteny-aware annotation transfer (annotate transfer, new). Steps: map the reference transcripts and proteins with minimap2 (splice:hq, secondary hits kept) and optionally miniprot; choose each gene's copy by collinear chaining of candidate loci in gene-rank space, which resolves paralogs and tandem arrays where Liftoff guesses; reconcile several references (assemblies of one genus) by voting on exon structure and keeping the intact reading frame; check and repair the ORF; label each gene intact, partial, pseudogenised, missing or extra copy. gene recall, exact-CDS rate, correct-copy rate, ORF integrity and runtime, against Liftoff and LiftOn, on Arabidopsis accessions, rice and tomato pan-genomes F PanSyn-like integration (PanSyn: Yu et al. 2024, Nature Protocols 10.1038/s41596-024-00966-4; the methods are paywalled, so the modules come from their primary papers): conserved non-coding sequences in syntenic regions (micro); ancestral linkage groups and Oxford dot plots for distant (animal) genomes (macro; Simakov et al. 2022, SYNPHONI); functional enrichment of retained or lost syntenic genes recovery of known ALGs (the 24 bilaterian ALGs), and enrichment of known CNSs H Beyond WGDs (fungi, animals, bacteria): mesosynteny (genes conserved within chromosomes but shuffled; Hane et al. 2011) and core vs accessory (conditionally dispensable) chromosomes; then ancestral linkage groups and Oxford plots; then DNA-level synteny and structural variants (after SyRI/msyd, reimplemented). Later: effector and biosynthetic gene clusters in syntenic context, breakpoint distances, i-ADHoRe-style multiplicon profiles, multi-genome browser recovery of known fungal accessory chromosomes (e.g. Fusarium oxysporum, Zymoseptoria tritici) and of the bilaterian ALGs G Scaling: linear-time families and gene-order indexes (ROADMAP 7.15) time and memory for 10 to 500 genomes

docs.title: Paper figures (draft)
docs.text:
1. The MCscan3 workflow and its features, set against the tools they replace.
  2. Anchoring benchmark: simulations (precision and recall against divergence and ploidy) and real pairs.
  3. WGD placement: simulations, and the eudicot and grass trees.
  4. Ancestral karyotypes against AKRUP and WGDI, and network trees.
  5. Annotation transfer against Liftoff and LiftOn: accuracy and speed.
  6. Scaling, plus one case study.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
The manuscript, Supplementary Methods and Protocols, and the script that rebuilds every table and figure are in paper/ (see paper/README.md). Result tables are versioned in benchmarks/results/.

phase state A1 + A2 (simulator, scoring) done (bench simulate, bench score) B (anchoring) method done (synteny anchor); simulation benchmark running with 3 seeds; real pairs queued C (WGD placement) done E (annotation transfer) method done (annotate transfer); benchmark against Liftoff queued D, F, G, H queued

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
Every command of MCscan3, grouped as on the command line (mcscan3 <group> <command>). Each page is written from the command's own documentation and options, so it matches -h.

Status: parity-verified (output identical to JCVI on the test genomes), ported, new (new in MCscan3, no JCVI counterpart; the page cites the method), legacy-only (kept for old command lines).

docs.title: prep: Input preparation
docs.text: Command Status Description mcscan3 prep gff2bed parity-verified Convert GFF3 features (e.g. mRNA) to BED, optionally one transcript per gene mcscan3 prep fasta-format parity-verified Reformat FASTA and clean up sequence IDs mcscan3 prep genome new Longest-isoform BED, CDS and protein from a genome GFF3 and FASTA mcscan3 prep bed-merge parity-verified Concatenate BED files, prefixing seqids with the file name mcscan3 prep bed-uniq parity-verified Remove overlapping BED features, keeping the best one per pile

docs.title: align: Homology search
docs.text: Command Status Description mcscan3 align last parity-verified Align query against a database with LAST (default MCscan aligner) mcscan3 align blast parity-verified Align with BLAST+ (blastn megablast, or blastp for proteins) mcscan3 align diamond parity-verified Align proteins with DIAMOND blastp mcscan3 align mmseqs new Search proteins or CDS with MMseqs2 (BLAST tabular output for synteny) mcscan3 align many new Search many genomes in one run (optionally on a GPU); one .last file per pair

docs.title: mcscan3 align blast
docs.text:
Align with BLAST+ (mcscan3 align blast; legacy apps.align blast and blast_main).

Group align · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 align blast [OPTIONS] SUBJECT QUERY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Two modes, as in the original:

  • default (apps.align blast): blastn (--task, default megablast) of the query against the database, output <query>.<db>.blast;
  • --pipeline (apps.align blast_main, used by ortholog run --align-soft blast): blastn or blastp (--dbtype prot) with -evalue 1e-5 -max_target_seqs 1000, output <query>.<db>.last so the rest of the MCscan pipeline can use it.

mcscan3 align blast --pipeline --dbtype=prot peach.pep grape.pep  # -> grape.peach.last

docs.title: Options

(default: 0) --evalue E-value cutoff. (default: 0.01) --wordsize Word size. --best Only look for the best N hits. (default: 1) --task blastn task. docs.title: mcscan3 align many
docs.text:
Search many genomes at once, optionally on a GPU.

Group align · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 align many [OPTIONS] FASTAS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. A synteny study of N genomes needs about N²/2 pairwise searches, and each one pays the start-up cost of building and loading a database. Here every proteome goes into one database and every query proteome is searched against it in one run, whose hits are then split into the usual per-pair BLAST tabular files <a>.<b>.last (query genes of a, subject genes of b). This is how all-against-all searches for orthology are run (e.g. OrthoFinder; Emms & Kelly 2019, Genome Biology). One large search keeps every core (or a GPU) busy, which pairwise runs of small genomes do not:

mcscan3 align many grape.pep peach.pep poplar.pep -o hits/              # all pairs + self
mcscan3 align many *.pep -o hits/ --pairs ref:grape                     # each vs grape only
mcscan3 align many *.pep -o hits/ --engine mmseqs --gpu                 # MMseqs2-GPU

Engines:

  • mmseqs (default), MMseqs2 (Steinegger & Söding 2017). With --gpu the target database is padded for the GPU and MMseqs2-GPU runs its gapless prefilter and gapped alignment on NVIDIA GPUs (Kallenborn et al. 2025, Nature Methods; Linux, CUDA, Turing or newer GPU). GPUs are chosen with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. --sensitivity does not apply on the GPU (no k-mer prefilter).
  • diamond, DIAMOND (Buchfink et al. 2021), CPU only (DIAMOND has no GPU version).

Pairs (--pairs): all (every pair, each species against itself too; default), between (no self pairs), ref:<sp1>,<sp2> (every species against these), or a file of a<TAB>b lines.

Differences from pairwise searches: e-values grow with the size of the database, so a hit near the cut-off in a pairwise search can fall out here, and --hits (most hits per query) is per target genome, i.e. the search keeps up to hits × genomes hits per query. Gene names are tagged with their genome inside the search, so the same name in two genomes is not confused.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FASTAS Protein FASTA per genome (.pep ...).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outdir, -o Directory for the ..last files. (default: .) --pairs all, between, ref:[,...] or a file of pairs. (default: all) --engine mmseqs or diamond. (default: mmseqs) --gpu MMseqs2-GPU (NVIDIA GPU, CUDA build). --sensitivity, -s MMseqs2 sensitivity (CPU only). (default: 7.5) --diamond-mode DIAMOND mode, e.g. fast. (default: ultra-sensitive) --evalue E-value cutoff. (default: 1e-05) --hits Most hits per query and target genome. (default: 100) --cpus Number of CPUs to use, 0 = all. (default: 0) --keep Keep the combined databases and raw hits. --path Directory containing the program(s).

docs.title: mcscan3 align mmseqs
docs.text:
Search proteins (or CDS) with MMseqs2.

Group align · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 align mmseqs [OPTIONS] SUBJECT QUERY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. MMseqs2 (Steinegger & Söding 2017, Nature Biotechnology 35:1026) is as sensitive as BLASTP at its high sensitivity settings and much faster on large genomes. The output is BLAST tabular (12 columns, percent identity) in <query>.<subject>.last, the file every MCscan3 synteny command reads. It is used by ortholog run --align-soft mmseqs:

mcscan3 align mmseqs peach.pep grape.pep --cpus 8      # -> grape.peach.last

Defaults: sensitivity 7.5, e-value 1e-5, up to 1000 targets per query. With --dbtype nucl, CDS are searched as nucleotides (--search-type 3). With --gpu, proteins are searched with MMseqs2-GPU (Kallenborn et al. 2025, Nature Methods) against a padded database; this needs an NVIDIA GPU and an MMseqs2 build with CUDA, and --sensitivity does not apply. To search many genomes, align many runs one search for all pairs.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SUBJECT Database FASTA (proteins, or CDS with --dbtype nucl). QUERY Query FASTA.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --dbtype prot (proteins) or nucl (CDS). (default: prot) --sensitivity, -s MMseqs2 sensitivity (1-7.5). (default: 7.5) --evalue E-value cutoff. (default: 1e-05) --max-targets Most targets per query. (default: 1000) --gpu MMseqs2-GPU (NVIDIA GPU, CUDA build; proteins only). --cpus Number of CPUs to use, 0 = all. (default: 0) --outdir Output directory. (default: .) --path Directory containing the program(s).

docs.title: mcscan3 ancestral adjacencies
docs.text:
Ancestral gene adjacencies over HOGs, propagated on the species tree.

Group ancestral · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ancestral adjacencies [OPTIONS] SPECIES_TREE GENE_HOGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after EdgeHOG (Bernard C et al. 2025, Nat Ecol Evol: ancestral gene order from HOGs) and the adjacency approach of AGORA (Muffato M et al. 2023, Nat Ecol Evol 7:355). The ancestral genes of a node are its HOGs (ortholog hogs), so duplications and losses are placed correctly, unlike with whole gene families as ancestral genes (ancestral genomes).

  1. extant adjacencies: along each chromosome of each genome, the genes with a HOG at a node are taken in order (tandem copies of one HOG merge), and every pair of neighbours is an adjacency of the two HOGs;
  2. bottom-up: at every node, the adjacencies of each child are mapped to the node's HOGs (through the HOG hierarchy), and the number of children having each is its support;
  3. top-down: at the root, adjacencies supported by two or more children are kept. At any other node, an adjacency is kept when two or more children support it, or one child does and the parent keeps it (the outgroup confirms it);
  4. linearisation: kept adjacencies, heaviest first (weight: genomes having it), give paths with at most two neighbours per HOG and no cycle: the contiguous ancestral regions (CARs). CARs whose ends are joined in genomes of two children are then scaffolded end to end, as in ancestral genomes (--no-scaffolding to skip);
  5. dating: each kept adjacency is dated to the oldest node keeping it, so the gene order rearranged on each branch shows as adjacencies new at a node.
mcscan3 ortholog hogs species.nwk --bed-dir data --hits *.last --anchors *.anchors -o hogs
mcscan3 ancestral adjacencies species.nwk hogs.genes.tsv --bed-dir data -o anc

Writes, for every internal node, <prefix>.<node>.adjacencies.tsv (HOG pair, support, genomes, age), <prefix>.<node>.cars.tsv (the format of ancestral genomes: CAR, position, HOG, one gene per genome, so ancestral karyotype and tree-karyotype read it) with its family table <prefix>.<node>.families.tsv (gene, HOG), and <prefix>.summary.tsv.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SPECIES_TREE Rooted species tree (Newick) of ortholog hogs. GENE_HOGS Genes table of ortholog hogs (.genes.tsv).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --bed-dir Directory of the .bed files. (default: .) --no-scaffolding Do not join CARs by their conserved ends. --format Image format of the tree figure. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 ancestral genomes
docs.text:
Reconstruct ancestral gene orders at every node of a species tree.

Group ancestral · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ancestral genomes [OPTIONS] SPECIES_TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, following the adjacency approach of AGORA (Muffato et al. 2023, Nature Ecology & Evolution 7:355), reimplemented from the paper. Gene families stand in for gene trees here. For each internal node of the species tree, from the leaves to the root:

  1. Ancestral genes. A family is an ancestral gene of the node when it has genes on at least two of the three sides of the node: its left subtree, its right subtree and the rest of the tree (the outgroups). This is the parsimony rule.
  2. Adjacencies. Each extant genome is reduced to its ancestral genes in chromosome order (tandem copies of a family merge into one). Two ancestral genes are adjacent in the ancestor when they are neighbours in genomes on two different sides of the node. The weight is the number of such species pairs that share the adjacency.
  3. Linearisation. Adjacencies are kept from the heaviest down, unless a gene already has two neighbours or the adjacency would close a cycle. The paths left are the contiguous ancestral regions (CARs), the ancestor's gene order in segments. --min-weight sets the least support kept.
  4. Scaffolding. CARs are joined end to end when genomes on two sides of the node place the same CAR ends next to each other. This recovers block order across small inversions and local shuffles, as AGORA's scaffolding does (--no-scaffolding to skip).
mcscan3 ancestral genomes species.nwk --families pan.pangenes.tsv --bed-dir . -o anc

Genomes are the tree's leaves, with genes from <species>.bed. Gene families can be:

  • a pan genes TSV;
  • a network cluster TSV;
  • an OrthoFinder Orthogroups.tsv;
  • a two-column gene<TAB>family file.

Writes <prefix>.<node>.cars.tsv for every internal node (car, position, family, and one example gene per descendant species) and <prefix>.summary.tsv, and prints one line per node: ancestral genes, adjacencies kept, CARs and the N50 of CAR lengths. Adjacencies are not oriented, and gene duplications are not placed on the tree (see wgd tree-map for that). A family with several genes in a genome contributes each copy's neighbours.

docs.title: mcscan3 ancestral karyotype
docs.text:
Ancestral chromosomes and karyotype painting.

Group ancestral · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ancestral karyotype [OPTIONS] CARS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. ancestral genomes gives contiguous ancestral regions (CARs), which on real data are often many and short. Karyotype figures in the style of WGDI and AKRUP need few units: the ancestral chromosomes (protochromosomes). They are found from the CARs:

  1. profiles: for every CAR and every genome, the share of the CAR's genes on each chromosome;
  2. affinity: two CARs from the same ancestral chromosome share chromosomes in the descendants. Their affinity is the overlap of their profiles (sum of the per-chromosome minima), averaged over the genomes where both are present;
  3. clustering: CARs with at least --min-car genes are grouped by average-linkage clustering of 1 - affinity, into --groups ancestral chromosomes (auto: the number with the best silhouette, from 2 to 60). Smaller CARs join the group they overlap most, and so do groups holding less than --min-group of the ancestral genes.

Each genome is then painted gene by gene with the ancestral chromosome of its family. Labels are smoothed with a sliding majority (--smooth genes each side) and runs shorter than --min-run genes (or 1% of the chromosome) are merged into their neighbours, giving clean blocks. The figure shows the ancestral karyotype (one bar per ancestral chromosome) above one row per genome, with chromosomes as rounded vertical bars coloured by ancestral chromosome:

mcscan3 ancestral karyotype anc.N2.cars.tsv --families pangenes.tsv --bed-dir data -o N2

Writes <prefix>.groups.tsv (CAR, ancestral chromosome, genes), <prefix>.segments.tsv (genome, chromosome, start and end rank, first and last gene, genes, ancestral chromosome) and the figure <prefix>.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CARS CARs of one ancestor (..cars.tsv).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --families The gene families used by ancestral genomes. --bed-dir Directory of .bed. (default: .) --prefix, -o Output prefix. --genomes Genomes to paint, top to bottom, comma-separated (default: the CARs' species). --groups Number of ancestral chromosomes (default: auto). --min-car CARs with fewer genes join a group afterwards. (default: 5) --min-group Groups with less than this share of the ancestral genes are merged. (default: 0.02) --smooth Sliding-majority window (genes each side). (default: 15) --min-run Shortest painted block (genes; at least 1% of a chromosome). (default: 40) --min-frac Leave out chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction. (default: 0.005) --basepair Chromosome lengths in base pairs, not genes. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each gene of an extant genome gets the colour of the contiguous ancestral region (CAR) that contains its family in an ancestor from ancestral genomes. Chromosome fusions, fissions and translocations since that ancestor show as changes of colour along a chromosome. Many extant chromosomes built from one CAR point to a duplication:

docs.title: mcscan3 ancestral tree-karyotype
docs.text:
Species tree with extant karyotypes at the tips and ancestral karyotypes beside the nodes.

Group ancestral · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ancestral tree-karyotype [OPTIONS] TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Every karyotype is painted with the ancestral chromosomes of one focal node (default: the root), found as in ancestral karyotype. Extant genomes sit at the tips of the species tree. Every ancestor reconstructed by ancestral genomes is drawn beside its node, with its own ancestral chromosomes (its CARs grouped the same way) painted in the focal colours. Fusions and fissions along the tree then show as colours joining and splitting:

mcscan3 ancestral tree-karyotype species.nwk --anc-prefix anc --families pangenes.tsv         --bed-dir data --focal N2 -o tree

Nodes are matched to the <anc-prefix>.<node>.cars.tsv files by their descendant species. The figure is <prefix>.<format>.

Fusions and fissions. Along every branch (a reconstructed ancestor to its nearest reconstructed descendant, or to an extant genome) each descendant chromosome is compared with the ancestor's chromosomes through their gene families. A part counts when it holds at least --event-share of the chromosome and --event-genes families:

  • a descendant chromosome made of parts of k ancestral chromosomes: k - 1 fusions;
  • an ancestral chromosome found in k descendant chromosomes that hold different parts of it: k - 1 fissions; when they hold the same part (over half of their families shared), it was duplicated (a WGD) and no fission is counted.

Counts are written to <prefix>.events.tsv (branch, counts, and which chromosomes) and drawn on the tree in <prefix>.events.<format>; --show-events also writes them on the branches of the karyotype figure. Small rearrangements below the thresholds are not counted.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description TREE Rooted species tree (Newick) used by ancestral genomes.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --anc-prefix Prefix of the ancestral genomes outputs. --families The gene families used by ancestral genomes. --bed-dir Directory of .bed. (default: .) --prefix, -o Output prefix (figure: .). --focal Node whose ancestral chromosomes colour everything (default: root). --groups Ancestral chromosomes of the focal node (default: auto). --min-car CARs with fewer genes join a group afterwards. (default: 5) --smooth Sliding-majority window (genes each side). (default: 15) --min-run Shortest painted block (genes). (default: 40) --show-events Write fusion/fission counts on the branches. --event-share Share of a chromosome a counted part must hold. (default: 0.2) --event-genes Families a counted part must hold. (default: 30) --wgd wgd consensus table: draw the called WGDs on the branches. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 annotate chain
docs.text:
Base-level chains between two assemblies.

Group annotate · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 annotate chain [OPTIONS] PAF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after transanno (Okada Y, Tang H: chains from minimap2 alignments for liftover) and the UCSC chain format (Kent WJ et al. 2003, PNAS 100:11484). Alignments of a new assembly (query) to an old one (target) from wga align (PAF with --eqx CIGAR) become one chain each: ungapped blocks with the gaps between them on both genomes. Primary alignments only, so every old base has at most one place (--secondary keeps the others, ranked by score).

The chains are indexed (blocks sorted per old chromosome, with the running maximum of their ends) so that millions of positions are lifted with a few vectorised binary searches (annotate lift):

mcscan3 wga align old.fa new.fa -o old.new
mcscan3 annotate chain old.new.paf -o old_to_new.chain

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PAF Alignments of the new assembly (query) to the old one (target), from wga align.

docs.title: Options

docs.title: mcscan3 annotate lift
docs.text:
Lift annotations and variants to a new assembly through chains.

Group annotate · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 annotate lift [OPTIONS] INP

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after transanno (Okada Y, Tang H; liftgene, liftvcf), UCSC liftOver and CrossMap (Zhao H et al. 2014, Bioinformatics 30:1006), reimplemented on the chain index of annotate chain (positions lifted with vectorised binary searches):

  • BED (any columns after the third kept): an interval goes to the chain aligning most of its bases; it is lifted when at least --min-match of them align there, from its first to its last aligned base; the strand flips on minus-strand chains.
  • GFF3/GTF: genes move as wholes. Every gene picks the chain aligning most of its span; each of its features is lifted on that chain, and the gene is lifted only when all exons and CDS are (--min-match), so models never straddle two places. Parents span their children again; CDS phases are recomputed on the new strand; with --genome every coding sequence is checked (length a multiple of three, start and stop codons, no premature stop) and tagged lift_cds=.
  • VCF (--genome needed): the REF bases must lift contiguously; REF is checked against the new genome. On minus-strand chains alleles are reverse-complemented and indels re-anchored on the base before them. When the new genome carries the old ALT of a biallelic variant, REF and ALT are swapped and genotypes flipped (INFO/LIFT_SWAP). Contig headers follow the new genome.

Records that cannot be lifted go to <prefix>.unlifted.<ext> with the reason:

mcscan3 annotate lift genes.gff3 --chain old_to_new.chain --genome new.fa -o genes.new
mcscan3 annotate lift calls.vcf.gz --paf old.new.paf --genome new.fa -o calls.new

docs.text: Argument Description INP BED, GFF3, GTF or VCF on the old assembly (may be gzipped).

docs.text: Option Description --chain Chains from annotate chain. --paf Or alignments from wga align (old = target). --genome New assembly FASTA (needed for VCF; checks CDS of GFF/GTF). --min-match Least share of a record's bases aligned on its chain. (default: 0.95) --out, -o Output prefix: . and .unlifted..

docs.title: mcscan3 annotate transfer
docs.text:
Transfer gene annotations to a new assembly, guided by synteny.

Group annotate · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 annotate transfer [OPTIONS] TARGET

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. One or more annotated assemblies of the same genus (references) are projected onto an unannotated assembly (the target). Every step is designed to be fast and to pick the right copy of duplicated genes:

  1. Spliced alignment. The mature transcripts of each reference (exons spliced, 5' to 3'; the CDS when exons are not annotated) are aligned to the target in one minimap2 run (-x splice:hq, Li 2018), keeping secondary alignments: every candidate locus of every gene. Candidates must cover --min-coverage of the transcript at --min-identity, and span at most twice the reference gene plus 10 kb (a spurious long intron would swallow neighbours). Genes whose transcript does not align at all are rescued by aligning their protein with miniprot (Li 2023), when it is installed; its alignments give the CDS directly.
  2. Synteny. Genes are ordered along the reference chromosomes. A gene with a single clear candidate (coverage and identity at least 0.9, and the next candidate scoring less than 90% of it) is an anchor. For every other gene, each candidate is scored by how many of the gene's nearest anchored neighbours (up to --flank genes on each side) map to the same target chromosome within --max-distance bp, and the candidate with most support (then the best alignment) is chosen. Duplicated genes, tandem copies and gene families are thereby placed by their neighbourhood, where alignment scores alone cannot decide.
  3. Overlaps. Genes are placed in order of confidence (anchors, then syntenic, then the rest); a candidate sharing more than 10% of the shorter CDS (in coding bases, so genes nested in another's intron do not clash) with one already placed on the same strand gives way to the gene's next candidate.
  4. Reading frames. The CDS is projected through the alignment (from the aligned bases nearest its ends, so a partial alignment gives a partial model), spliced from the target and checked: start codon, stop codon, length a multiple of three, no premature stop. A missing stop codon is repaired by extending the last exon to the next in-frame stop (up to 300 bp). Each gene is reported intact or with its defects (no_start, no_stop, frameshift, premature_stop).
  5. Several references. Each reference is transferred on its own; the models are then grouped by overlapping CDS on the same strand, and each group keeps one model, in order of preference: intact reading frame, syntenic placement, coverage x identity, reference order. Genes missing from one reference are recovered from another, so the union of the references is transferred.
  6. Extra copies (--copies): further candidates at coverage and identity of at least --copy-identity that do not overlap a placed gene are added as copies (_copy<N>).

Writes <prefix>.gff3 (gene, mRNA, exon and CDS features; attributes give the reference, reference gene, coverage, identity, synteny and reading-frame status), the MCscan3 inputs <prefix>.bed, .cds and .pep, and <prefix>.transfer.tsv (one line per reference gene: where it went, or why not):

mcscan3 annotate transfer target.fa --ref japonica.fa,japonica.gff3 --ref glaberrima.fa,glaberrima.gff3 \
    -o indica --cpus 8

docs.text: Argument Description TARGET Target assembly to annotate (FASTA, may be gzipped).

(default: 4) --min-coverage Least share of a transcript aligned. (default: 0.5) --min-identity Least identity of an alignment. (default: 0.5) --flank Anchored neighbours used on each side to place a gene. (default: 10) --max-distance A neighbour supports a locus within this many bp. (default: 1000000) --max-intron Longest intron (bp). (default: 50000) --copies Also add extra copies of genes. --copy-identity With --copies: least coverage and identity. (default: 0.95)

docs.text: New in MCscan3. Anchors (--anchors a.b.anchors, or a two-column pairs file): precision is the share of anchor pairs that are positional homologs (orthologs, or ohnologs of a polyploidy event); recall is the share of all positional homolog pairs of the two genomes that are anchors. Pairs between tandem copies of a positional homolog count as correct for precision ("tandem" column) but are not required for recall.

docs.title: mcscan3 bench simulate
docs.text:
Simulate the evolution of gene-annotated genomes along a species tree.

Group bench · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 bench simulate [OPTIONS] TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Benchmarks of synteny, orthology, WGD and ancestral-genome methods need a known answer, which real genomes rarely give. The simulator evolves an ancestral genome (chromosomes of protein-coding genes with codon sequences) along a rooted species tree whose branch lengths are in synonymous substitutions per synonymous site (Ks). It writes each extant genome as MCscan3 input (<species>.bed, .cds and .pep) and the truth in truth/.

Sequences. Each gene is a run of sense codons. Over a step of length dt, each codon is proposed one point mutation with probability 1 - exp(-3 dt) (a random position, a random other base). Stop codons are rejected, synonymous changes are accepted, and non-synonymous ones are accepted with the gene's ω (Ka/Ks, drawn from a gamma distribution with mean --omega). The synonymous changes per synonymous site then equal the branch length, so a pair's Ks recovers twice the time since it split.

Genome changes, as Poisson processes along every branch (rates per unit Ks):

  • inversions (--inversions, lengths geometric with mean --inversion-genes);
  • reciprocal translocations of chromosome ends (--translocations);
  • fusions and fissions of chromosomes (--fusions, --fissions);
  • tandem duplications, next to the copied gene (--tandem, per gene);
  • dispersed duplications, to a random place (--dispersed, per gene);
  • losses of single genes (--loss, per gene).

Polyploidy is given as events on branches (--event N2:wgd:0.5 puts a WGD halfway along the branch above node N2; wgt is a triplication; allo is an allotetraploid whose two subgenomes had diverged by --allo-divergence Ks before they merged). After an event, each gene set from it loses copies at rate --fractionation. The copy lost is chosen with weights 1, --bias, --bias\ :sup:2 for subgenomes 1, 2, 3 (biased fractionation).

Truth (truth/):

  • genealogy.tsv: every gene copy ever made, with its parent, how it arose (root, speciation, wgd, tandem, dispersed), the event and the node where it arose;
  • genes.tsv: the extant genes and their genealogy ids;
  • events.tsv: the polyploidy events, their branch and time;
  • ancestors/<node>.bed: the genome at every internal node (the true ancestral gene orders);
  • species.nwk: the tree with node names, and config.json.

mcscan3 bench score compares results with this truth:

mcscan3 bench simulate "((A:0.3,B:0.3)N2:0.5,C:0.8)N1;" --event N2:wgd:0.4 -o sim

docs.text: Argument Description TREE Rooted species tree (Newick text or file), branch lengths in Ks.

docs.title: Options

(default: 6) --genes Genes of the root genome. (default: 3000) --protein-length Mean protein length (aa). (default: 300) --omega Mean Ka/Ks. (default: 0.2) --inversions Inversions per unit Ks. (default: 20) --inversion-genes Mean inversion length (genes). (default: 15) --translocations Reciprocal translocations per unit Ks. (default: 4) --fusions Chromosome fusions per unit Ks. (default: 1) --fissions Chromosome fissions per unit Ks. (default: 1) --tandem Tandem duplications per gene per unit Ks. (default: 0.02) --dispersed Dispersed duplications per gene per unit Ks. (default: 0.01) --loss Gene losses per gene per unit Ks. (default: 0.02) --fractionation Losses per polyploid gene set per unit Ks. (default: 2.0) --bias Fractionation bias between subgenomes. (default: 1.5) --allo-divergence Ks between the progenitors of an allo event. (default: 0.15) --seed Random seed. (default: 666)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the CNE scan of CNEr (Tan G et al. 2019, Bioinformatics 35:4467) and the conserved non-coding sequences of plants (Haudry A et al. 2013, Nat Genet 45:891). CNEs lie in the gene deserts and introns of syntenic regions, so only syntenic regions are compared:

  1. regions: every block of the anchors file between the two genomes gives a region of each genome, from its first to its last gene, widened by --flank bp on each side;
  2. masking: exons and coding sequences of the GFF3 files (--mask), repeats (soft-masked, lower-case bases; --keep-repeats keeps them) and Ns are masked;
  3. alignment: all regions of one genome are aligned to all regions of the other in a single LAST run (Kielbasa et al. 2011, Genome Res 21:487) and reduced to one-to-one alignments in both genomes (last-split, swapped, last-split again): each base of either genome is aligned at most once, which plays the part of CNEr's two-way scan and removes paralogous and repeated hits. Alignments between regions of different blocks are discarded;
  4. scan: along each alignment, every window of --window columns with at least --identity x window identical bases (gaps and masked bases count as differences) is conserved; overlapping conserved windows are merged, trimmed to their first and last identical bases, and kept from --min-length bp.

The scan runs on whole alignments at once with cumulative sums (no per-window loop):

mcscan3 cne find ath.fa.gz brapa.fa.gz --gff ath.gff3.gz brapa.gff3.gz --bed ath.bed brapa.bed \
    --anchors ath.brapa.anchors -o ath.brapa

Writes <prefix>.cne.tsv (both coordinates, strand, length, identity, block) and one BED file per genome, <prefix>.<genome>.cne.bed.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FASTA_A Genome a (FASTA, soft-masked repeats in lower case). FASTA_B Genome b (FASTA).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --gff GFF3 of genome a, then of genome b (exons masked). --bed Genes of genome a, then of genome b (BED). --anchors Synteny blocks of genomes a and b (anchors file). --prefix, -o Output prefix. --flank Bases added on each side of every block. (default: 10000) --window Columns of the scanning window. (default: 50) --identity Least share of identical bases in a window. (default: 0.9) --min-length Shortest CNE (alignment columns). (default: 50) --mask GFF3 feature types masked (comma-separated). (default: exon,CDS) --keep-repeats Do not mask lower-case (repeat) bases. --cpus Threads of LAST (default: all). --path Directory of the LAST programs.

docs.title: mcscan3 cne grb
docs.text:
Genomic regulatory blocks from clusters of CNEs.

Group cne · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 cne grb [OPTIONS] CNES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the genomic regulatory blocks of Kikuta H et al. (2007, Genome Res 17:545) and their identification from CNE density in Harmston N et al. (2017, Nat Commun 8:441). A GRB is a region dense in CNEs whose order and synteny are kept, because its CNEs regulate a shared target gene from far away. From the CNEs of cne find of one reference genome against one or more others:

  1. clusters: per comparison, the CNEs along each reference chromosome are joined while the gap between neighbours is at most --max-gap bp and they lie in the same syntenic block (synteny kept);
  2. density test: a cluster of n CNEs over L bp is tested against the comparison's mean CNE density over its syntenic regions (one-sided Poisson; Benjamini-Hochberg over all clusters); clusters with at least --min-cnes CNEs and q at most --alpha are kept;
  3. GRBs: kept clusters of all comparisons that overlap are merged; the number of comparisons supporting each GRB is reported, so a GRB held across many lineages stands out.

The genes of the reference inside each GRB are listed, the one overlapping most CNE bases first (the likeliest host or target):

mcscan3 cne grb ath.brapa.cne.tsv ath.lyrata.cne.tsv --bed ath.bed -o ath

Writes <prefix>.grb.tsv (chromosome, start, end, CNEs, comparisons, density per 100 kb, q, genes), <prefix>.grb.bed and the CNE density in windows, <prefix>.density.tsv.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CNES CNE tables of cne find, all with the same genome a.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --bed Genes of genome a (BED): genes of each GRB. --max-gap Largest gap between neighbouring CNEs of a GRB (bp). (default: 50000) --min-cnes Fewest CNEs of a GRB in one comparison. (default: 5) --alpha Largest q of the density test. (default: 0.05) --window Window of the density table (bp). (default: 100000)

docs.title: mcscan3 cne plot
docs.text:
CNE density along the reference genome with GRBs.

Group cne · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 cne plot [OPTIONS] CNES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. One panel per reference chromosome (or the --chrom given, optionally a --region): CNE density per window for each comparison as a line, the GRBs of cne grb as shaded spans with their supporting comparisons, and the reference genes as ticks along the bottom, so the long gene-poor, CNE-rich GRBs around developmental genes stand out:

mcscan3 cne plot ath.brapa.cne.tsv --grb ath.grb.tsv --bed ath.bed -o ath.cne

(default: 100000) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 dup classify
docs.text:
Classify duplicated genes by how they arose.

Group dup · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 dup classify [OPTIONS] BLAST_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: a reimplementation of the classification of Qiao et al. (2019, Genome Biology 20:38; DupGen_finder), from the published description. Paralogous pairs come from an all-against-all BLAST of one genome. They are assigned, in this order of priority:

  • WGD: collinear pairs, i.e. anchors of syntenic blocks within the genome (whole-genome or segmental duplication);
  • tandem: adjacent genes on the same chromosome;
  • proximal: genes on the same chromosome separated by at most --proximal-max genes;
  • transposed: one copy at an ancestral locus (syntenic with the outgroup genome) and the other not (needs --outgroup);
  • dispersed: all other pairs.

Genes in no pair are singletons:

mcscan3 dup classify grape.grape.last --bed grape.bed \
    --outgroup grape.peach.last --outgroup-bed peach.bed -o grape

Writes <prefix>.<class>.pairs (gene1<TAB>gene2; for transposed pairs the transposed copy first, then its ancestral copy) and <prefix>.genes (each gene with its highest-priority class), and prints the counts to stderr. With --unique, a pair is dropped when either gene already belongs to a higher-priority class, so each gene is counted in one class only.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLAST_FILE All-against-all BLAST of one genome (tabular).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --bed BED of the genome's genes. --outgroup BLAST of the genome against an outgroup (for transposed). --outgroup-bed BED of the outgroup genome. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --evalue E-value cutoff for homologous pairs. (default: 1e-10) --top Best hits per gene used as pairs. (default: 5) --proximal-max Max genes between proximal duplicates. (default: 10) --dist Synteny: max gap (genes) between anchors. (default: 20) --min-size Synteny: min anchors per block. (default: 5) --intrabound Synteny: ignore blocks this close to the diagonal. (default: 300) --unique Count each gene in one class only.
