docs.title: mcscan3 expr counts
docs.text:
Expression matrices from quantification outputs.

Group expr · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 expr counts [OPTIONS] FILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Reads per-sample read counts and builds one gene-by-sample matrix, with TPM and CPM. Supported inputs (detected per file):

  • featureCounts tables (one or many samples; lengths from its Length column);
  • htseq-count output (__ summary lines dropped);
  • Salmon quant.sf (NumReads; lengths EffectiveLength) and kallisto abundance.tsv (est_counts; eff_length), transcript level: summed to genes with --tx2gene (two columns) or the transcript -> gene links of --gff;
  • RSEM *.genes.results (expected_count);
  • a ready matrix (gene column then one column per sample, TSV or CSV).

A sample sheet (--samples: sample, condition, optional file) names the samples and their conditions; without one every file is one sample named after the file, or a matrix keeps its column names (--condition-from takes the condition from sample names with a regular expression such as '(.+)_rep\d+'). Gene lengths for TPM come from the inputs, else from --gff (union of exons per gene). Writes <prefix>.counts.tsv, <prefix>.tpm.tsv, <prefix>.cpm.tsv and <prefix>.samples.tsv:

mcscan3 expr counts --samples samples.tsv --gff ath.gff3 -o ath.expr

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FILES Count files (featureCounts, htseq-count, Salmon, kallisto, RSEM, matrix).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output prefix. --samples Sample sheet: sample, condition, optional file. --gff Annotation: gene lengths, transcript -> gene links. --tx2gene Transcript -> gene table (Salmon/kallisto inputs). --condition-from Regex whose group 1 is the condition.

docs.title: mcscan3 expr de
docs.text:
Differential expression ranked by Bayes factors.

Group expr · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 expr de [OPTIONS] MATRIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after Hoerbst F, Sidhu GS, Tomkins M & Morris RJ (2025) What is a differentially expressed gene? (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.31.635902) and their Bayesian framework (bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.20.633909; github.com/Morris-Research-Group/bayexpress). Instead of a yes/no call from p-value and fold-change cut-offs, every gene is ranked by the evidence for a difference in expression between two conditions (log10 Bayes factor BF21, replicates pooled; see mcscan3.features.expr.bayes), with its inferred log2 fold change, its expression probabilities q per condition, and the evidence that its replicates disagree (BFk1 per condition). Calls (up/down) are made only for convenience, at --min-bf (log10 BF, default 1: a Bayes factor of 10, "strong" on Jeffreys' scale) and --min-fc (|log2 fold change|, default 0); the table keeps every gene with its rank.

Checks of the uncertainty, as in the paper:

  • --control N: N random splits of the first condition's replicates into two halves (wild type against wild type): genes called in a split are listed with how often, and the number of calls per split is reported as the expected false calls of the design;
  • --subsets N: consistently inconsistent genes (CIG) of each condition: replicates drawn N times (--subset-size, default half of them, at least 3); a gene is a CIG when BFk1 > 1 in every draw.

Contrasts come from --contrast TREATMENT:REFERENCE (repeatable) or every pair of conditions. Writes per contrast <prefix>.<treatment>_vs_<reference>.tsv (sorted by evidence), a volcano plot (log2 fold change against log10 BF) and an MA-like plot, <prefix>.summary.tsv and, for the first contrast, q-plots of the top genes (q per replicate):

mcscan3 expr de ath.expr.counts.tsv --samples samples.tsv --contrast heat:control \
    --control 50 --subsets 50 -o ath.de

docs.text: Argument Description MATRIX Count matrix (expr counts output, featureCounts or any gene x sample table).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output prefix. --samples Sample sheet: sample, condition (default: .samples.tsv). --contrast TREATMENT:REFERENCE (repeatable; default: all pairs). (default: []) --min-bf log10 Bayes factor for a call (1 = BF of 10). (default: 1.0) --min-fc --min-count Skip genes with fewer reads in the two conditions. (default: 0) --control Reference-vs-reference splits to estimate false calls. (default: 0) --subsets Replicate draws to find consistently inconsistent genes. (default: 0) --subset-size Replicates per draw (default: half, at least 3). (default: 0) --top Genes in the q-plot. (default: 12) --format Figure format. (default: pdf) --seed Random seed. (default: 1)

docs.title: mcscan3 expr homoeolog
docs.text:
Homoeolog expression bias and subgenome dominance.

Group expr · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 expr homoeolog [OPTIONS] MATRIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. --strip REGEX removes a part of the gene names (e.g. transcript suffixes \.\d+$) so they match the expression matrix. Groups of homoeologs (pairs, triads, ...) come from a table with one column per subgenome (the <prefix>.genes.tsv of subgenome fractionation, . for a lost copy), any table with a header of subgenome names (--columns picks some), or 1:1 anchors (--anchors FILE with --names A,B). For each condition (replicates pooled):

  • bias evidence: log10 Bayes factor that the homoeologs' shares of the group's reads differ from the expected shares (equal, or proportional to gene length with --length), flat Dirichlet against a fixed multinomial (see mcscan3.features.expr.bayes), after the Bayesian treatment of read counts of Hoerbst F et al. (2025, bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.01.31.635902);
  • shares of TPM (mean of replicates) and the category nearest to them (Euclidean distance): balanced, one homoeolog dominant, or (three or more) one suppressed, after the triad categories of Ramírez-González RH et al. (2018, Science 361:eaar6089); pairs are dominant when one homoeolog has at least --min-fold times (default 2) the other's TPM; groups with less than --min-tpm in total are not expressed. A category other than balanced is kept only with bias evidence of at least --min-bf (log10 BF, default 1), else balanced;
  • changes between conditions (pairs, with --contrast T:R or every pair of conditions): log10 Bayes factor that the first homoeolog's share differs between the two conditions (the two-sample Bayes factor on the pair's reads).

Per condition, a summary counts groups dominated by and suppressed in each subgenome, the median log2 ratio for pairs, and a sign test of dominance (are biased pairs more often towards one subgenome than half?). Writes <prefix>.groups.tsv, <prefix>.summary.tsv, <prefix>.changes.tsv (pairs) and a figure (ternary plot for triads, ratio histogram for pairs, category bars):

mcscan3 expr homoeolog ath.expr.counts.tsv --groups bnap.frac.genes.tsv -o bnap.heb

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description MATRIX Count matrix (expr counts output, featureCounts or any gene x sample table).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output prefix. --samples Sample sheet: sample, condition (default: .samples.tsv). --groups Homoeolog table (one column per subgenome). --columns Subgenome columns to use (repeatable). (default: []) --anchors 1:1 anchors as homoeolog pairs (with --names). --names Subgenome names of the --anchors columns. (default: A,B) --length Expected shares proportional to gene length. --min-tpm Least total TPM of a group to classify it. (default: 1.0) --min-bf log10 Bayes factor for a biased category. (default: 1.0) --min-fold Pairs: TPM fold between homoeologs for dominance. (default: 2.0) --strip Regex removed from homoeolog names (e.g. '.\d+$'). --contrast TREATMENT:REFERENCE for bias changes (pairs). (default: []) --format Figure format. (default: pdf)

docs.title: mcscan3 expr pairs
docs.text:
Expression similarity of gene pairs.

Group expr · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 expr pairs [OPTIONS] MATRIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Pairs come as named groups (--pairs NAME=FILE, repeatable: .pairs of dup classify, synteny .anchors, ortholog pairs or any two-column table). Each pair's profiles across conditions (mean log2(TPM + 1) of the replicates; CPM when no gene lengths) are compared by Pearson correlation, Spearman correlation and expression divergence (1 - Pearson); the breadth of expression of each gene is its tissue-specificity index tau (Yanai I et al. 2005, Bioinformatics 21:650). Pairs between species use a second matrix (--matrix2, genes of the second column), with conditions matched by name (only shared conditions are used). A baseline of random pairs is added (--strip REGEX removes transcript suffixes from the pair files' gene names) and each group is compared with it (one-sided Mann-Whitney test: are the pairs more similar than random?). Writes <prefix>.pairs.tsv, <prefix>.summary.tsv, <prefix>.tau.tsv and a box plot:

mcscan3 expr pairs ath.expr.counts.tsv --pairs wgd=ath.wgd.pairs --pairs tandem=ath.tandem.pairs \
    -o ath.dup.expr

(default: 2000) --strip Regex removed from pair gene names (e.g. '.\d+$'). --format Figure format. (default: pdf)

docs.title: mcscan3 fetch genome
docs.text:
Genomes and annotations by accession, species or URL.

Group fetch · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 fetch genome [OPTIONS] SPECS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each argument names a genome in a public database, and the genome sequence and its annotation are downloaded into a folder that mcscan3 pipeline run reads directly (<label>.dna.fa.gz and <label>.gff3.gz; --proteins adds protein and CDS files). Your own genomes can be mixed in as local files. Accepted names (LABEL= in front sets the species label used in file names and figures):

  • GCF_000001735.4, GCA_...: NCBI Assembly (NCBI Datasets, O'Leary NA et al. 2024, Sci Data 11:732). A GenBank assembly without annotation is replaced by its annotated RefSeq pair.
  • ncbi:Sorghum bicolor or just "Sorghum bicolor": that species' NCBI reference genome.
  • ensembl:zea_mays: Ensembl and Ensembl Genomes, all divisions, current release (Harrison PW et al. 2024, Nucleic Acids Res 52:D891; Yates AD et al. 2022, Nucleic Acids Res 50:D996).
  • GWHBPAH01000000: the Genome Warehouse of the China National Center for Bioinformation (Chen M et al. 2021, Genomics Proteomics Bioinformatics 19:584).
  • CNP0000111 or CNP0000111/CNA0000821: the CNGB Sequence Archive (Guo X et al. 2020, Database baaa055). An assembly accession alone cannot be looked up there; give its project.
  • a URL of a folder (the genome, annotation, protein and CDS files are recognised by name) or comma-separated file URLs; local files or a folder.

Downloads resume after interruptions and are kept in a cache shared by all runs ($MCSCAN3_FETCH_CACHE or ~/.cache/mcscan3/genomes). manifest.tsv records each genome's source, accession, assembly, annotation and URLs, and taxonomy.nwk the NCBI taxonomy tree of the species:

mcscan3 fetch genome ath=GCF_000001735.4 ensembl:vitis_vinifera GWHBPAH01000000 \
    mine=my_genome.fa,my_genes.gff3 -o genomes
mcscan3 pipeline run genomes -o run

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SPECS Genomes: NCBI accession (GCF_/GCA_), ncbi:SPECIES, ensembl:SPECIES, GWH accession, CNGB project (CNP... or CNA...), URL of a folder or files, or local files; LABEL=SPEC sets the name.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --outdir Folder for the genomes (ready for pipeline run). --proteins Also download protein and CDS files. --jobs Downloads at once. (default: 3) --unannotated Keep genomes without an annotation. --no-cache Download straight into the folder. --dry-run Only list what would be downloaded.

docs.title: Method and references
docs.text: New in MCscan3 (no JCVI equivalent). MCscan3: database clients with resumable, cached downloads, ready for the pipeline. Data from NCBI Datasets (O'Leary NA et al. 2024, Sci Data 11:732), Ensembl and Ensembl Genomes (Harrison PW et al. 2024, Nucleic Acids Res 52:D891; Yates AD et al. 2022, Nucleic Acids Res 50:D996), Genome Warehouse (Chen M et al. 2021, Genomics Proteomics Bioinformatics 19:584) and the CNGB Sequence Archive (Guo X et al. 2020, Database baaa055).

docs.title: mcscan3 fetch taxon
docs.text:
The best annotated genome of every species of a taxon.

Group fetch · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 fetch taxon [OPTIONS] NAME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Give a taxon name or NCBI taxid (Poaceae, Brassicaceae, Saccharomycetaceae, 4479). The taxon is looked up in NCBI Taxonomy (Schoch CL et al. 2020, Database baaa062); the annotated assemblies of NCBI (reference genomes; --all-assemblies for every one) and of the Ensembl division the taxon belongs to are listed, and the best assembly of each species is kept: annotated, most contiguous (complete > chromosome > scaffold > contig; --level sets the least), RefSeq before GenBank, then the highest BUSCO completeness of the annotation. --per-genus spreads the genomes over genera and --max keeps the best ones; --include and --exclude (regular expressions on species or accessions) and --add (any fetch genome name, e.g. your own genome) adjust the set.

Without -o the genomes are only listed. With -o they are downloaded as by fetch genome, and taxonomy.nwk joins them by their NCBI lineages: a rooted tree with internal nodes named by taxon (unbranched ranks collapsed). Taxonomy leaves polytomies where relationships are unresolved. pipeline run --taxon does all of this and then the whole analysis (orthology, synteny, networks, pan-genes, ancestral genomes, duplications, WGDs, report), comparing the taxonomy tree with the gene-based species trees:

mcscan3 fetch taxon Poaceae --per-genus 1 --max 12            # list
mcscan3 fetch taxon Poaceae --per-genus 1 --max 12 -o grasses  # download
mcscan3 pipeline run -o grasses_run --taxon Poaceae --taxon-max 8 --cpus 16 --ks

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description NAME Taxon name or NCBI taxid (e.g. Poaceae, Brassicaceae, 4479).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --outdir Folder for the genomes (omit to only list them). --source Databases to search: ncbi, ensembl (comma-separated). (default: ncbi,ensembl) --prefer When both have a species: ncbi or ensembl. (default: ncbi) --level Least assembly level: complete genome, chromosome, scaffold or contig. (default: chromosome) --all-assemblies NCBI: consider every assembly, not only reference genomes. --max At most this many genomes, the best first (0: all). (default: 0) --per-genus At most this many genomes per genus (0: any). (default: 0) --include Always keep species/accessions matching (regex, repeatable). (default: []) --exclude Leave out species/accessions matching (regex, repeatable). (default: []) --add Extra genomes (any fetch genome spec, repeatable). (default: []) --proteins Also download protein and CDS files. --jobs Downloads at once. (default: 3) --no-cache Download straight into the folder.

docs.title: mcscan3 filter best
docs.text:
Best BLAST hit(s) per query or subject (mcscan3 filter best; legacy formats.blast best).

Group filter · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 filter best [OPTIONS] BLASTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
As in the original, the BLAST file is first sorted in place (sort -k1,1 -k12,12gr: by query, then score descending; -k2,2 with --subject) unless --nosort. Writes <blastfile>.best (<blastfile>.subject.best with --subject):

mcscan3 filter best grape.peach.last -n 3 --subject

docs.text: Argument Description BLASTFILE BLAST tabular file (sorted in place unless --nosort).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -n Best N hits. (default: 1) --nosort Assume the file is already sorted. --hsps Get all HSPs for the best pair. --subject Best hits per subject instead of query.

docs.title: mcscan3 filter blastfilter
docs.text:
Filter a BLAST table for synteny detection (mcscan3 filter blastfilter; legacy compara.blastfilter).

Group filter · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 filter blastfilter [OPTIONS] BLAST_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Keeps one hit per gene pair (highest score first), then applies, in order:

  • --exclude: drop pairs present in an anchors file from a previous run;
  • C-score filter: keep hits whose score is more than --cscore times the best score of either gene;
  • local (tandem) duplicate filter: genes hitting the same partner within --tandem-nmax genes are collapsed onto the largest one.

Writes <blast_file>.filtered. With --tandems-only also writes <bed>.localdups and <bed>.nolocaldups.bed for each genome:

mcscan3 filter blastfilter grape.peach.last --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed --no-strip-names

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLAST_FILE BLAST tabular file (e.g. a.b.last).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --no-strip-names Do not strip alternative splicing (e.g. At5g06540.1 -> At5g06540). --tandems-only Also write .localdups and .nolocaldups.bed files. --tandem-nmax Merge tandem genes within this distance. (default: 10) --cscore Keep hits with C-score above this. (default: 0.7) --exclude Remove anchors from a previous run.

docs.text:

docs.title: mcscan3 filter cscore
docs.text:
C-scores of BLAST hits (mcscan3 filter cscore; legacy formats.blast cscore).

Group filter · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 filter cscore [OPTIONS] BLASTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
cscore(A, B) = score(A, B) / max(best score of A, best score of B) (sea anemone genome paper). A C-score of 1 is a reciprocal best hit. Reports query subject cscore (optionally percent identity) for pairs above --cutoff, sorted by pair:

mcscan3 filter cscore grape.peach.last --cutoff=0.7 --pct -o grape.peach.cscore

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLASTFILE BLAST tabular file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --cutoff Minimum C-score to report. (default: 0.9999) --pct Also include percent identity. --writeblast Also write .filtered.blast. --no-strip-names Do not strip alternative splicing (e.g. At5g06540.1 -> At5g06540). --outfile, -o Output file. (default: stdout)

docs.title: mcscan3 gff add
docs.text:
Add derived features to an annotation.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff add [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_add_introns, agat_sp_add_intergenic_regions, agat_sp_add_start_and_stop and UTR completion (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT):

  • --introns: intron features between the exons of each transcript;
  • --utrs: five_prime_UTR/three_prime_UTR from exons minus CDS where missing;
  • --intergenic: top-level intergenic_region features between consecutive genes of a sequence (genes on either strand; overlapping genes leave no gap), and from the sequence ends when --genome gives the sequence lengths;
  • --codons: start_codon and stop_codon at the ends of each CDS, split across exons when a codon is spliced, added only where the genome (--genome, required) shows ATG (or the --table start codons) and a stop codon.

Writes GFF3 (or GTF/BED by the extension of -o):

mcscan3 gff add ath.gff3 --introns --intergenic --codons --genome ath.fa -o ath.full.gff3

docs.title: Arguments

docs.title: mcscan3 gff compare
docs.text:
Compare two annotations of one genome.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff compare [OPTIONS] REFERENCE QUERY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_compare_two_annotations (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT) and the sensitivity/precision levels of gffcompare (Pertea G & Pertea M 2020, F1000Research 9:304). The first file is the reference. Genes overlapping on the same strand (by CDS when both are coding, else exons) form loci; each locus is identical (a transcript pair with the same CDS, or the same exons when non-coding), overlapping, reference only or query only, with its numbers of genes on each side (1:1, 1:n, n:1, n:m). Sensitivity and precision at the base (CDS or exon bases), exon (exact exon), intron (exact intron), intron chain (transcript) and gene (locus with an identical pair) levels. Writes <prefix>.loci.tsv and <prefix>.summary.tsv:

mcscan3 gff compare reference.gff3 new.gff3 -o ref_vs_new

docs.text:

docs.title: mcscan3 gff extract
docs.text:
Sequences of annotated features.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff extract [OPTIONS] GFF GENOME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_extract_sequences (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). From an annotation and its genome FASTA, one record per transcript (or per piece) of --type:

  • cds (spliced, 5' to 3', first phase trimmed) and protein (translated, --table genetic code, final stop removed; --keep-stop keeps it). A complete CDS (first phase 0) that opens with an alternative start codon of the table (CTG, TTG; GTG with table 11) begins with M, as the ribosome reads it;
  • mrna (spliced exons), gene (genomic span), exon and intron (each piece);
  • five_prime_UTR and three_prime_UTR (spliced per transcript);
  • upstream / downstream: --flank bp before the transcript start or after its end, on the transcript's strand (clipped at sequence ends).

--longest uses one transcript per gene. Headers are >ID gene=GENE seqid:start-end(strand); --name Name uses another attribute as the record name:

mcscan3 gff extract ath.gff3 ath.fa --type protein --longest -o ath.pep

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped). GENOME Genome FASTA.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output FASTA (default: stdout). (default: -) --type cds, protein, mrna, gene, exon, intron, five_prime_UTR, three_prime_UTR, upstream or downstream. (default: cds) --longest One transcript per gene (longest CDS). --flank Upstream/downstream length (bp). (default: 1000) --table Genetic code (NCBI table number). (default: 1) --keep-stop Proteins keep a final stop (*). --name Attribute used as the record name. (default: ID)

docs.title: mcscan3 gff filter
docs.text:
Select genes of a GFF3/GTF annotation.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff filter [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's filters (agat_sp_filter_feature_by_attribute_value, agat_sp_filter_by_ORF_size, agat_sp_filter_gene_by_length, ...; Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). A gene is kept with all its transcripts when it passes every test given:

  • --type: gene type (gene, ncRNA_gene, ...; repeatable);
  • --seqid: on these sequences; --region SEQ:START-END: overlapping the region;
  • --attr KEY=REGEX: an attribute of the gene or one of its transcripts matches (repeatable, all must match); --exclude KEY=REGEX: none matches;
  • --min-length/--max-length: gene span in bp;
  • --min-protein/--max-protein: longest protein (CDS length / 3, stop excluded) in amino acids; genes without CDS fail --min-protein;
  • --coding/--noncoding: with or without CDS;
  • --max-exons/--min-exons: exons of the longest transcript.

Writes the kept genes (-o) and, with --discarded FILE, the others:

mcscan3 gff filter ath.gff3 --min-protein 50 --exclude Note=transposable -o ath.f.gff3

docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --discarded Also write the genes that fail. --type Gene type to keep (repeatable). (default: []) --seqid Sequence to keep (repeatable). (default: []) --region SEQ:START-END: genes overlapping it. --attr KEY=REGEX that must match (repeatable). (default: []) --exclude KEY=REGEX that must not match (repeatable). (default: []) --min-length Smallest gene span (bp). (default: 0) --max-length Largest gene span (bp). (default: 0) --min-protein Shortest longest protein (aa). (default: 0) --max-protein Longest longest protein (aa). (default: 0) --coding Only genes with (or without) CDS. --min-exons Fewest exons (longest transcript). (default: 0) --max-exons Most exons (longest transcript). (default: 0)

docs.title: mcscan3 gff fix
docs.text:
Check and repair a GFF3/GTF annotation.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff fix [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the checks of AGAT (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT, doi:10.5281/zenodo.3552717). Repairs, each counted in the report:

  • types: GTF and common aliases (5UTR, three_prime_utr, ...) to Sequence Ontology names; a transcript with a CDS becomes mRNA;
  • IDs: every gene and transcript gets one (<type><n>); parts get <transcript>.<type><k>, all CDS lines of a transcript share <transcript>.cds; repeated gene/transcript IDs get a suffix;
  • missing parents: parts whose transcript is missing get a transcript (mRNA when it has a CDS) and a gene; transcripts without a gene get one; parts without any Parent are grouped by transcript_id, Name or gene_id (else one transcript each);
  • exons made from CDS and UTRs when a transcript has none; UTRs made from exons minus CDS;
  • CDS phases recomputed from the lengths of the CDS before them (5' to 3');
  • transcript and gene spans set to their parts and transcripts;
  • duplicated lines and identical isoforms (same exons, same CDS) removed.

Writes the repaired annotation (GFF3, or GTF/BED by the extension of -o) and <output>.report.tsv:

mcscan3 gff fix messy.gff3 -o clean.gff3

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --no-utr Do not add missing UTRs. --no-exon Do not add missing exons. --no-phase Keep the CDS phases as they are. --keep-duplicates Keep repeated lines and isoforms.

docs.title: mcscan3 gff merge
docs.text:
Merge annotations into one.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff merge [OPTIONS] GFFS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_merge_annotations (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). Annotations are read in order; a gene of a later file that overlaps a gene already present on the same strand (by CDS when both have one, else by exons; at least --min-overlap bp) joins it: its transcripts become isoforms of the earlier gene, except transcripts identical to one already there (same exons and CDS), which are dropped. Other genes are added; IDs that clash get the file's --tag (default the file name) as a prefix. --separate keeps overlapping genes as separate genes (only identical transcripts are dropped). Writes GFF3 (or GTF/BED by the extension of -o) and a summary:

mcscan3 gff merge braker.gff3 liftoff.gff3 -o merged.gff3

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFFS Annotations, in order of priority.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --tag Prefix for clashing IDs, one per file (default: file names). (default: []) --min-overlap Shared CDS/exon bases that join two genes. (default: 1) --separate Keep overlapping genes apart.

docs.title: mcscan3 gff rename
docs.text:
Systematic IDs for genes, transcripts and their parts.

Group gff · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 gff rename [OPTIONS] GFF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after AGAT's agat_sp_manage_IDs (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT). Genes are numbered along each sequence (sequences in natural order) with --template, whose fields are {prefix}, {seqid}, {chrom} (the last number in the sequence name, else the name) and {n} (the gene number, which grows by --step; --per-seqid restarts it on each sequence). Transcripts become <gene>.1, <gene>.2...; exons, UTRs and others <transcript>.<type><k>, and the CDS lines of a transcript share <transcript>.cds. Old IDs are kept as Alias (--no-alias drops them) and listed in <output>.ids.tsv:

mcscan3 gff rename ath.gff3 --prefix ATH --template "{prefix}{chrom}G{n:05d}" --step 10 \
    --per-seqid -o ath.renamed.gff3

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Annotation (GFF3 or GTF, optionally gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -o, --output Output (.gff3, .gtf, .bed or .bed6 sets the format; - for stdout). --prefix Value of {prefix} in the template. (default: GENE) --template Gene ID: {prefix}, {seqid}, {chrom}, {n}. (default: {prefix}{n:06d}) --step Increment of the gene number. (default: 1) --start First gene number (default: --step). --per-seqid Restart the numbers on each sequence. --no-alias Do not keep old IDs as Alias.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the statistics of AGAT (Dainat J et al., github.com/NBISweden/AGAT, doi:10.5281/zenodo.3552717). Per gene type (gene, ncRNA_gene, ...) and transcript type: numbers of genes, transcripts, exons, CDS, UTRs and introns; transcripts per gene; exons per transcript; mean, median and total lengths of genes, transcripts (spliced), exons, introns, CDS and UTRs; single-exon genes and transcripts; genes overlapping another gene; share of the genome covered (with --genome). --longest measures only the longest isoform of each gene. docs.title: mcscan3 go enrich
docs.text:
Gene Ontology enrichment of gene sets.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go enrich [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after GOATOOLS (Klopfenstein DV et al. 2018, Sci Rep 8:10872), reimplemented. Annotations (GAF, GPAD, gene2go, eggNOG-mapper, InterProScan or a table; see go docs) are propagated up the ontology (true-path rule: a gene annotated to a term is annotated to all its ancestors; --relationships part_of also follows those links). For every term annotated in the population, the study genes in it are compared with the population genes in it:

  • test: Fisher's exact test, two-sided by default (terms both enriched, e, and purified, p, in the study); --test greater tests enrichment only;
  • correction for the number of terms tested, per namespace (BP, MF, CC) or over all (--correct-by all): fdr_bh (default), fdr_by, bonferroni, holm, sidak, holm-sidak; several can be given and the first decides significance (--alpha);
  • the population is the given gene list or BED (--population), or the genes of the MCscan3 output the sets come from, or else every annotated gene; study genes outside it are ignored. --annotated-only restricts both to annotated genes (as many R packages do).

Gene sets come from a gene list (--study), a table of named sets (--sets: set<TAB>gene, as written by go sets), or straight from MCscan3 outputs (--from: duplicate classes, pan-gene categories, subgenome assignments, HOGs, synteny blocks, genes in SVs, introgressed segments, regulatory blocks; see go sets), and every set is tested against the same population.

Writes <prefix>.tsv (set, term, namespace, name, level, depth, e/p, study and population counts and ratios, fold enrichment, raw and corrected p values, study genes in the term), a dot plot of the top terms (<prefix>.dotplot.<format>: one set, terms by fold enrichment; several sets, a grid of sets and terms) and, for each set with significant terms, the significant part of the ontology graph with its ancestors (<prefix>.<set>.dag.<format>):

mcscan3 go enrich --obo go-basic.obo --annotations tair.gaf --study young.txt \
    --population genes.bed -o young
mcscan3 go enrich --obo go-basic.obo --annotations ath.emapper.annotations \
    --from ath.genes --bed ath.bed -o ath.dup

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --obo Gene Ontology (OBO, e.g. go-basic.obo; gzip ok). --annotations, -a GAF, GPAD, gene2go, eggNOG-mapper, InterProScan or gene-GO table. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --study Gene list or BED of a study set (repeatable; set named after the file). (default: []) --sets Named sets: setgene (from go sets). --from MCscan3 outputs to take sets from (see go sets; repeatable). (default: []) --bed Genes (BED) for region outputs (SVs, introgression) and the population. --population Population: gene list or BED (default: from the sets' source). --genome Genome column of pan-gene / microsynteny tables. --species Species of HOG tables. --ann-format auto, gaf, gpad, gpad2, gene2go, emapper, interproscan, table. (default: auto) --id-field GAF gene ids: id, symbol or synonym. (default: id) --evidence Keep only these evidence codes (repeatable). (default: []) --no-evidence Drop these evidence codes, e.g. IEA (repeatable). (default: []) --strip Regular expression removed from gene ids, e.g. '.\d+$'. --relationships Also propagate through these relations (part_of, regulates, all). (default: []) --test two-sided (enriched and purified) or greater. (default: two-sided) --method fdr_bh, fdr_by, bonferroni, holm, sidak, holm-sidak (repeatable; first decides). (default: ['fdr_bh']) --correct-by namespace or all. (default: namespace) --alpha Significance level of the corrected p value. (default: 0.05) --min-term Test terms with at least this many population genes. (default: 2) --max-term Test terms with at most this many population genes (0: any). (default: 0) --annotated-only Count only annotated genes in study and population. --all Write every tested term, not only significant ones. --top Terms in the dot plot. (default: 20) --no-dag Skip the ontology graph figures. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 go sets
docs.text:
Named gene sets from MCscan3 outputs, for enrichment.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go sets [OPTIONS] INPUTS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each input is recognised by its header or name, and gives sets named <kind>:<value> together with its population (all genes it classifies):

  • dup classify <prefix>.genes: one set per duplication class (dup:wgd, dup:tandem, dup:proximal, dup:transposed, dup:dispersed, dup:singleton);
  • dup classify / synteny pair files (*.pairs, *.anchors): the genes in pairs;
  • pan genes table: pan-gene categories (pan:core, pan:softcore, pan:dispensable, pan:private, ...) of the genes of one genome (--genome, default the first);
  • subgenome assign gene table: one set per subgenome (subgenome:<progenitor>);
  • ortholog hogs gene table: genes by the node of their oldest HOG (hog:origin:<node>; with --bed, genes in no HOG are hog:origin:<species>, the species-specific ones), for one species (--species); the HOG table: genes of HOGs from a duplication at each node (hog:duplicated:<node>);
  • OrthoFinder (or pipeline) Orthogroups.tsv and Orthogroups_UnassignedGenes.tsv, for one species (--species): og:core (orthogroups in every species), og:single-copy (one gene in every species), og:accessory (in some other species, not all), og:specific (only in this species, unassigned genes included), og:expanded / og:contracted (at least twice / at most half the median copy number of the other species that have the orthogroup, and a difference of two or more genes);
  • network clusters (net.clusters.tsv): genes of one species in clusters of that species only (network:specific), of every species (network:all) or of some (network:partial); with the network gainloss origins table, by the node where their cluster arose (network:origin:<node>);
  • synteny .anchors / .pairs with --bed: the genome's anchored genes (<file>:syntenic) and the others (<file>:non-syntenic);
  • micro blocks block table: genes in microsynteny blocks of each genome;
  • cne grb table: genes in regulatory blocks;
  • regions with --bed (genes overlapping them, at least --min-overlap of the gene): sv call tables and VCFs (sv:<type>, reference side unless --side qry) and introgress scan segments (introgress:<state>);
  • expr de contrast tables: genes called up or down (de:<contrast>:up, de:<contrast>:down), all ranked genes as the population;
  • expr homoeolog group tables: per condition, the dominant and suppressed homoeologs (heb:<condition>:dominant:<subgenome>, heb:<condition>:suppressed:<subgenome>) and the genes of balanced groups (heb:<condition>:balanced);
  • a set<TAB>gene table or a plain gene list (one set named after the file).

Writes set<TAB>gene rows, with the population as set _population (go enrich --sets reads it back):

mcscan3 go sets ath.genes ath.pan.tsv sv/col.ler.sv.tsv --bed ath.bed --genome ath -o ath.sets.tsv

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description INPUTS MCscan3 outputs (dup classify, pan genes, subgenome assign, hogs, ...).

docs.title: Options

docs.title: mcscan3 go similarity
docs.text:
Functional similarity of gene pairs from their GO terms.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go similarity [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Semantic similarity of terms by information content (IC = -ln of the share of annotated genes of the namespace annotated to the term, after propagation): Resnik (IC of the most informative common ancestor, MICA), Lin (2 IC(MICA) / (IC(a) + IC(b))) or Jiang-Conrath similarity (1 / (1 + IC(a) + IC(b) - 2 IC(MICA))). Two genes compare by the best-match average of their most specific terms in one namespace (--ns, default BP). After Resnik P (1995, IJCAI), Lin D (1998, ICML), Jiang JJ & Conrath DW (1997, ROCLING) and the semantic similarity of GOATOOLS (Klopfenstein DV et al. 2018, Sci Rep 8:10872).

Pairs come as groups (--pairs NAME=FILE, repeatable): the .pairs of dup classify (wgd, tandem, ...), synteny .anchors, ortholog pairs, or any two-column table. A baseline of random annotated gene pairs (--random) is added, and each group is compared with it (one-sided Mann-Whitney test: are the pairs more similar than random?). Writes <prefix>.pairs.tsv (group, gene pair, similarity), <prefix>.summary.tsv and a box plot:

mcscan3 go similarity --obo go-basic.obo --annotations ath.gaf \
    --pairs wgd=ath.wgd.pairs --pairs tandem=ath.tandem.pairs -o ath.dup.sim

docs.title: mcscan3 go slim
docs.text:
Gene annotations summarised on a GO slim.

Group go · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 go slim [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the slim mapping of GOATOOLS (Klopfenstein DV et al. 2018, Sci Rep 8:10872) and map2slim (GO Consortium). Each term of a gene maps to its direct slim ancestors: the slim terms among the term and its ancestors that have no other such slim term below them (--all-ancestors: every slim ancestor). mcscan3 go slim --obo go-basic.obo --slim goslim_plant.obo --annotations ath.gaf \
    --from ath.genes -o ath.dup.slim

docs.title: mcscan3 introgress scan
docs.text:
Introgression and haplotype-sharing scans with k-mers.

Group introgress · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 introgress scan [OPTIONS] TARGET

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the k-mer identity-by-state approach of KCFtools and IBSpy (k-mers of a reference window looked up in the k-mers of a sample, with no alignment or variant calling). A target genome (an assembly: its chromosomes give the coordinates) is cut into windows; each source (assemblies or read sets, plain or gzip FASTA/FASTQ) is reduced to its sampled k-mers (introgress k-mer sketches, FracMinHash with --scaled; read k-mers seen fewer than --min-count times are dropped as errors). For every window and source, the containment is the share of the window's k-mers found in the source: ~1 where the two are identical by state, about (1 - d)^k where they differ at a rate d (0.53 at 2% with k = 31).

Two ways to read the windows, both segmented with a Viterbi path (--switch penalises a change of state between neighbouring windows, so single noisy windows do not break blocks); every block boundary is then moved to the sampled k-mer where the k-mers on each side best agree with the two states, so breakpoints are placed to tens of bases rather than to a window:

  • --mode paint (default): every window goes to the source it matches best; with the parents (or candidate donors) as sources and a hybrid or introgression line as target, the blocks are its ancestry mosaic, like haplotype painting;
  • --mode identity: every source separately, windows are identical by state (containment at least --min-identity) or divergent; with a reference as target and samples (reads) as sources, divergent blocks are candidate introgressions from a distant donor, as KCFtools reports them.
mcscan3 introgress scan hybrid.fa --source parentA.fa --source parentB.fa -o hybrid
mcscan3 introgress scan ref.fa --source line1.fq.gz --source line2.fq.gz --mode identity --min-count 3 -o lines

Writes <prefix>.windows.tsv (window, k-mers sampled, containment in each source, state) and <prefix>.blocks.tsv (chromosome, start, end, state, windows, mean containment).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description TARGET Target assembly (FASTA): its chromosomes give the windows.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --source Source genome or reads (FASTA/FASTQ, gzip ok), optionally named as NAME=FILE; repeat. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --mode paint (best source per window) or identity (IBS per source). (default: paint) --window Window size (bp). (default: 50000) --k k-mer length (up to 31). (default: 31) --scaled Keep one k-mer in this many (FracMinHash). (default: 10) --min-count Read k-mers seen fewer times are errors (FASTQ only). (default: 2) --min-identity Identity mode: least containment of an IBS window. (default: 0.8) --switch Penalty of a change of state between windows. (default: 3.0) --min-kmers Windows with fewer sampled k-mers are not scored. (default: 50) --cpus Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype events
docs.text:
Trajectories from the ancestral karyotype to each genome, and shared events on the tree.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype events [OPTIONS] SEGMENTS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the chromosome evolution models used with AKRUP and WGDI (Wang X et al. 2015, Plant Cell 27:1953 on grasses; Murat F et al. 2017, Genome Biol 18:200; Sun P et al. 2022, Mol Plant 15:1841). Each extant chromosome painted by karyotype map is read as a row of segments of ancestral chromosomes, each with its ancestral span (0 and 1 are the two ends, the telomeres, of the ancestral chromosome) and copy. Neighbouring segments meet at junctions, which are classified:

  • EEJ (end-to-end joining), EEJ:A-B: both segments meet with their ancestral ends (within --end-tol of 0 or 1). One chromosome is lost.
  • NCF (nested chromosome fusion), NCF:B>A: segments of B sit between two parts of the same copy of A, and the two parts of A are complementary (their spans hardly overlap): B was inserted into A, usually at the centromere. One chromosome is lost.
  • RCT (reciprocal translocation), RCT:A/B: two junctions of A and B, on different chromosomes, at least one end within the chromosome rather than at its end. The number of chromosomes stays.
  • TRA (other translocation), TRA:A-B: an unpaired junction within a chromosome. When both sides are broken inside, the exchange left one more chromosome (its other product split).
  • FIS (fission), FIS:A: a copy of A is split over more chromosomes than its translocations explain. One chromosome is gained.
  • WGD, WGD:x2: overlapping copies of the ancestral chromosomes (the median number over ancestral chromosomes) are whole-genome duplications, not fissions. The chromosome number expected from the events, ancestral chromosomes x copies + FIS - EEJ - NCF (plus one per TRA broken on both sides), is set beside the observed one as a check: a gap means events the segments do not resolve.

Every event is a character, present or absent in each genome (<prefix>.characters.tsv). With a rooted species tree (--tree) the characters are mapped onto it by irreversible (Camin-Sokal) parsimony: an event can arise on several branches but never reverts, so independent whole-genome duplications and parallel fusions stay on their own branches and an ancestor carries only the events all its descendants share (--model dollo: one origin per event, losses elsewhere). The karyotype of every ancestor follows from the events it carries: which fusions it already had, and its chromosome number (ancestral chromosomes x WGD copies + FIS - EEJ - NCF, each event counted once; genomes keep their observed number). Shared EEJs and NCFs are how the ancestral karyotypes of grasses and eudicots were built (bottom-up); the events on the branches are the trajectory to each genome (top-down):

mcscan3 karyotype events eudicot.segments.tsv --tree species.nwk -o eudicot

Writes <prefix>.events.tsv (genome, type, event, chromosomes, detail), <prefix>.genomes.tsv (per genome: chromosomes, copies, counts of each event type, expected chromosomes), <prefix>.characters.tsv and, with --tree, <prefix>.nodes.tsv (per node: events gained on the branch above it, events carried, chromosome number) and the tree figure <prefix>.tree.<format>.

docs.text: Argument Description SEGMENTS Segments of karyotype map (.segments.tsv).

docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --tree Rooted species tree: events and ancestral karyotypes on it. --genomes Only these genomes (comma-separated). --end-tol Ancestral positions this close to 0 or 1 are ends. (default: 0.15) --min-genes Smaller segments are ignored (genes). (default: 50) --model irreversible (parallel gains, no reversals) or dollo (one gain). (default: irreversible) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype genome
docs.text:
The ancestral karyotype written out as a genome.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype genome [OPTIONS] ANCESTOR REF_BED

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the ancestral genome files of WGDI (-ak) and AKRUP (-ags). Every ancestral chromosome becomes a pseudo-chromosome holding the reference genes that carry it, in ancestral order (see mcscan3.features.karyotype.core). The protein (and coding) sequences of those genes make the ancestral genome a genome like any other: align it to extant genomes (align, synteny), draw dot plots against it, and use it as the reference of karyotype map, where every chromosome is its own ancestral chromosome:

mcscan3 karyotype genome anc.segments.tsv grape.bed --pep grape.pep --cds grape.cds -o AEK
mcscan3 karyotype map AEK.labels.tsv AEK.bed --target cacao.bed --anchors AEK.cacao.anchors -o AEK.map

--name prefixes the pseudo-chromosomes (default: none, the ancestral chromosome names) and --rename gives the genes new names <name><chromosome>g<number>, keeping the originals in the labels table. Writes <prefix>.bed (genes spaced --spacing bp apart), <prefix>.lens (chromosome, genes), <prefix>.labels.tsv (gene, ancestral chromosome, reference gene), and <prefix>.pep / <prefix>.cds when the sequences are given.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCESTOR Ancestral karyotype on the reference: segments, WGDI regions or genelabel. REF_BED Genes of the reference genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --pep Proteins of the reference. --cds Coding sequences of the reference. --copy Use only this copy (class) of a polyploid reference. --name Prefix of the pseudo-chromosomes. --rename New gene names g. --spacing Distance between genes in the BED (bp). (default: 10000)

docs.title: mcscan3 karyotype map
docs.text:
A known ancestral karyotype painted on another genome through synteny blocks.

Group karyotype · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 karyotype map [OPTIONS] ANCESTOR REF_BED

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the karyotype mapping of WGDI (Sun et al. 2022, Mol Plant 15:1841) and the event-related blocks of AKRUP (ancestral karyotype reconstruction pipeline, Wang lab). The reference genome carries the ancestral karyotype (see mcscan3.features.karyotype.core); an anchors file between the reference and the target gives the synteny blocks. Each block with at least --min-block anchors votes for the ancestral chromosome most of its reference genes carry:

  • every target gene between the block's first and last anchor gets one vote (the block covers it);
  • every anchor gets two more votes for the ancestral chromosome of its own reference partner.

Each target gene takes the ancestral chromosome with most votes; labels are smoothed along the chromosome (--window genes each side) and runs shorter than --min-run genes join their neighbours, as in ancestral karyotype. A segment's ancestral span comes from the ancestral positions of its anchors' partners (median of the first and of the last five) and its strand from their rank correlation. Segments of one ancestral chromosome holding the same ancestral positions (over half of the shorter one's, in 1% bins) are copies (from whole-genome duplication), numbered 1, 2, ... by size, as the classes of WGDI.

With --ks (the anchor-pair TSV of wgd ksd --anchors) and --ks-range lo,hi, only blocks whose median Ks falls in the range count: in a polyploid, the blocks of one duplication event (wgd peaks gives the range) paint the copies that event made, as the event-related blocks of AKRUP. Several targets are painted in one run:

mcscan3 karyotype map anc.segments.tsv grape.bed --target cacao.bed --anchors grape.cacao.anchors \
    --target peach.bed --anchors grape.peach.anchors -o eudicot

Writes <prefix>.segments.tsv (the ancestral karyotype columns, then ancestral span, strand, copy and anchors; karyotype events reads it), one WGDI-style region file per genome <prefix>.<genome>.regions.txt (chromosome, start, end, colour, class), the colours <prefix>.colors.tsv, and the figure <prefix>.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCESTOR Ancestral karyotype on the reference: segments, WGDI regions or genelabel. REF_BED Genes of the reference genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --target Genes of a genome to paint (BED); repeat. --anchors Anchors of the reference and each target, in order. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --copy Use only this copy (class) of a polyploid reference. --min-block Fewest anchors of a block that votes. (default: 5) --window Smoothing: genes on each side. (default: 5) --min-run Shorter runs join their neighbours (genes). (default: 20) --ks Anchor-pair Ks (TSV of wgd ksd --anchors). --ks-range Only blocks with median Ks in lo,hi (with --ks). --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 ks calc
docs.text:
Ks/Ka of sequence pairs (mcscan3 ks calc; legacy compara.ks calc).

Group ks · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ks calc [OPTIONS] FILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For consecutive pairs of CDS records (translated first unless a protein file is given):

  1. align the protein pair with ClustalW (default) or MUSCLE;
  2. back-translate the alignment to codons with PAL2NAL;
  3. run PAML yn00 for Yang-Nielsen and Nei-Gojobori Ks/Ka.

Writes name,yn_ks,yn_ka,ng_ks,ng_ka (-o). Needs clustalw2 (or muscle 3.8), pal2nal.pl and yn00 on PATH (or MCSCAN3_<TOOL>_PATH). Intermediate files are kept in <workdir>/syn_analysis as in the original:

mcscan3 ks calc grape.peach.cds.fasta -o grape.peach.ks --workdir=ksw

docs.text: Argument Description FILES [protein FASTA] CDS FASTA with consecutive pairs.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --longest Use the longest ORF (only without a protein file). --msa Protein aligner: clustalw or muscle. (default: clustalw) --workdir Work directory (default: current directory). --outfile, -o Output file. (default: stdout)

docs.title: mcscan3 ks gc3
docs.text:
Remove gene pairs with high GC3 from Ks results (mcscan3 ks gc3; legacy compara.ks gc3).

Group ks · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ks gc3 [OPTIONS] KSFILE CDSFILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
High-GC3 genes give unreliable Ks (the two estimates disagree strongly; Tang et al. 2010 PNAS), which is common in cereals. A pair is dropped when the mean GC content at the third codon position of its two genes is above 0.75. For two genomes, give both CDS files (or one concatenated file):

mcscan3 ks gc3 grape.peach.ks grape.cds peach.cds -o grape.peach.gc3.ks

The output is CSV with \r\n line ends, as the original's csv writer produced. The original crashed on every run (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.7). --plot also writes the GC3 values to <cdsfile>.gc3 and draws their histogram (needs plot histogram).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description KSFILE Ks file. CDSFILES CDS FASTA file(s): one, or one per genome (at most 2).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --plot Also plot the GC3 histogram (see plot histogram). --outfile, -o Output Ks file. (default: stdout)

docs.title: mcscan3 ks kaks
docs.text:
Ka, Ks and Ka/Ks of gene pairs with MCscan3's own estimators.

Group ks · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ks kaks [OPTIONS] PAIRS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, in the spirit of KaKs_Calculator: no external aligner or PAML. Each pair's proteins are aligned and threaded back onto the codons, then Ks and Ka are estimated with one or more methods (--method, comma-separated; see mcscan3.core.kaks):

  • ng86 (Nei & Gojobori 1986) and lpb93 (Li 1993; Pamilo & Bianchi 1993): counting methods, about 0.1 ms per pair after the alignment;
  • gy94: maximum likelihood under the Goldman & Yang (1994) codon model, as pairwise codeml (tens of ms per pair; parallel with --cpus).

Pairs come from a two-column file (gene1<TAB>gene2) or an anchors file; sequences from one or more CDS FASTA files:

mcscan3 ks kaks grape.grape.anchors --cds grape.cds --method lpb93,gy94 --cpus 8 -o grape.kaks.tsv

Writes gene1, gene2, codons, identity and, per method, <method>_ks, <method>_ka and <method>_kaks. Pairs below --min-identity (protein identity over the aligned codons) get empty values: maximum-likelihood Ks of near-random pairs is meaningless.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PAIRS Gene pairs: two columns, or an anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --cds CDS FASTA file(s) with the genes (repeatable). --outfile, -o Output TSV. --method ng86, lpb93, gy94 (comma-separated for several). (default: lpb93) --min-identity Leave pairs below this protein identity empty. (default: 0.0) --cpus Processes (useful for gy94). (default: 1)

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

Ka, Ks and Ka/Ks (Goldman-Yang maximum likelihood and Nei-Gojobori) of the syntenic pairs, with MCscan3's own estimators; also written as Ks tables.

cd core && cat grape.cds peach.cds poplar.cds > all.cds  && for p in grape.peach.lifted.1x1 grape.poplar.lifted.1x2 peach.poplar grape.grape; do
   mcscan3 ks kaks $p.anchors --cds all.cds --method gy94,ng86 --cpus $CPU -o ${p%%.lifted*}.kaks.tsv; done  && for p in grape.peach grape.poplar peach.poplar grape.grape; do awk -F'\t' 'NR==1{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++)c[$i]=i; print "name,yn_ks,yn_ka,ng_ks,ng_ka"; next} $c["gy94_ks"]!=""{print $1";"$2","$c["gy94_ks"]","$c["gy94_ka"]","$c["ng86_ks"]","$c["ng86_ka"]}' $p.kaks.tsv > $p.ks; done && wc -l *.ks && head -3 grape.peach.kaks.tsv

run time 10 min 25 s · data real · showcase step ks_kaks

Variables: $CPU threads.

docs.title: mcscan3 macro algs
docs.text:
Ancestral linkage groups from many genomes.

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro algs [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Ancestral linkage groups (ALGs) are sets of gene families that stayed together on one chromosome since a distant ancestor, e.g. the 24-29 bilaterian ALGs (Simakov et al. 2022, Science Advances 8:eabi5884) or the 17 ALGs of the metazoan ancestor. Here they are found without a reference. Each pair of families is weighted by the share of the genomes having both in which they sit on one chromosome; the families are then split into groups whose pairs share a chromosome in more than --resolution (default 0.4) of the genomes on average: the Constant Potts Model (Traag et al. 2011, Phys Rev E 84:016114) optimised by Leiden when igraph is installed, else MCL. Pairs below --min-link (default 0.2) are left out of the graph, for speed. Families are used when present in at least --min-genomes genomes (default: half, at least two); groups of fewer than --min-size families are dropped. Fusions in a few lineages do not merge two ALGs (they are on one chromosome in a minority of genomes), and fissions in a few do not split one. With a rooted species tree (--tree), genomes are weighted so that each clade below a node has an equal share: a rearrangement shared by a large, densely sampled clade then counts once against its sister lineage, and the outgroups decide what was ancestral (a tie is not a link).

With --reference, each ALG is named after the chromosome of that genome holding most of its families (ref:chr, letters when several ALGs share one), else ALG01, ALG02, ... by size. ALGs that are already known (e.g. the bilaterian ALGs on amphioxus genes) are given with --known gene<TAB>ALG; families then take the ALG of most of their genes in that table:

mcscan3 macro algs *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv -o metazoa --reference amphioxus
mcscan3 macro algs *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv -o metazoa --known bfl_blg.tsv

Writes <prefix>.algs.tsv (family, ALG) and <prefix>.alg_summary.tsv (per ALG: families and, per genome, the chromosome holding most of them and its share).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BEDS Genes of each genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --families Orthogroups.tsv or genefamily table. --known Known ALGs as geneALG (instead of finding them). --tree Rooted species tree: weight genomes by clade. --reference Name ALGs after this genome's chromosomes. --resolution Least mean co-location within an ALG. (default: 0.4) --min-link Family pairs co-located less are ignored. (default: 0.2) --min-genomes Families in fewer genomes are left out (default: half). --min-size Smallest ALG (families). (default: 10) --seed Random seed (Leiden). (default: 666) --min-genes Smallest chromosome kept (genes with a family). (default: 20) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 4)

docs.title: mcscan3 macro fusions
docs.text:
Fusions, fissions and mixing of ancestral linkage groups in each genome.

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro fusions [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. With ALGs from macro algs, every chromosome of every genome is tested for the ALGs it carries (one-sided Fisher test of chromosome x ALG gene counts, Benjamini-Hochberg; an ALG is carried with at least --min-genes genes). A chromosome carrying two or more ALGs is a fusion; an ALG carried by two or more chromosomes of a genome is split (fission).

After a fusion, intrachromosomal rearrangements gradually interleave the genes of the fused ALGs. Such fusion-with-mixing cannot be undone and so marks clades (Simakov et al. 2022, Science Advances 8:eabi5884; Schultz et al. 2023, Nature 618:110). Mixing is measured from the order of the ALG genes along the chromosome by the number of runs (blocks of consecutive genes of one ALG): k runs for k unmixed ALGs, about 1 + (n - 1)(1 - sum n_i(n_i - 1) / (n(n - 1))) for a random order. The mixing index scales the observed runs from 0 (unmixed) to 1 (random), and a permutation test (--permutations) gives the chance that a random order has as few runs: below --alpha, the ALGs are still in separate segments (fusion, A+B); otherwise they are mixed (fusion-with-mixing, A x B). Every pair of ALGs on a chromosome is scored the same way.

Each fused pair of ALGs (A+B, any mixing) and each mixed pair (A x B) is then a character present or absent in each genome (<prefix>.characters.tsv, a profile matrix). With a rooted species tree (--tree) the characters are mapped onto it, giving the branch on which each fusion happened: by irreversible (Camin-Sokal) parsimony by default, since fusions, and above all fusions with mixing, are not undone, while the same fusion can arise in parallel in two lineages; --model dollo places each fusion once, at the last common ancestor of the genomes having it:

mcscan3 macro fusions *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv --algs metazoa.algs.tsv -o metazoa --tree sp.nwk

Writes <prefix>.chromosomes.tsv (per genome and chromosome: genes, ALGs carried, state, runs, mixing index, p), <prefix>.alg_pairs.tsv (per genome, every pair of ALGs on one chromosome), <prefix>.splits.tsv (ALGs on several chromosomes), <prefix>.characters.tsv and, with --tree, <prefix>.gainloss.tsv / .origins.tsv / .gainloss.nwk.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BEDS Genes of each genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --algs ALGs from macro algs (.algs.tsv). --families Orthogroups.tsv or genefamily table. --tree Rooted species tree: map fusions onto it. --model irreversible (parallel fusions, no reversals) or dollo (one origin). (default: irreversible) --alpha Significance of carried ALGs and of unmixed order. (default: 0.05) --min-alg-genes Fewest genes of an ALG on a chromosome. (default: 10) --permutations Permutations of the mixing test. (default: 1000) --seed Random seed. (default: 666) --min-genes Smallest chromosome kept (genes with a family). (default: 20) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 4)

docs.title: mcscan3 macro plot
docs.text:
Macrosynteny figures.

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro plot [OPTIONS] PREFIX BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• oxford: an Oxford dot plot of two genomes, one dot per gene pair of a shared family at the genes' positions (gene ranks) along the concatenated chromosomes, coloured by ALG when ALGs are given. Chromosomes of the second genome are ordered by the chromosome of the first they are most enriched with (macro test), so homologous chromosomes line up on the diagonal; cells of significant chromosome pairs are shaded.
  • painting: every genome as a row of chromosome bars, each gene a thin stripe coloured by its ALG, so fusions (several colours on one bar), fissions (one colour on several bars) and mixing (interleaved stripes) are seen at a glance across many genomes.

docs.title: mcscan3 macro test
docs.text:
Which chromosomes of two genomes descend from the same ancestral chromosome.

Group macro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 macro test [OPTIONS] BED_A BED_B

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Between distantly related genomes (hundreds of millions of years), gene order is lost but genes stay on the chromosomes they came from: macrosynteny (Simakov et al. 2020, Nature Ecology & Evolution 4:820; Simakov et al. 2022, Science Advances 8:eabi5884). For every pair of chromosomes, the number of gene families with genes on both is compared with what the chromosome sizes alone would give by the one-sided Fisher exact test, and adjusted for the number of pairs (Benjamini-Hochberg; --adjust bonferroni|holm|none). Families come from an orthogroup table (--families) or from reciprocal best hits in a BLAST table (--hits):

mcscan3 macro test amphioxus.bed scallop.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv -o amph.scallop

Writes <prefix>.macro.tsv, one row per chromosome pair: shared families, expected, the ratio, p and adjusted q, and whether the pair is significant (q <= --alpha and at least --min-count families); prints the significant pairs. macro plot --kind oxford draws them.

docs.text: Argument Description BED_A Genes of the first genome (BED). BED_B Genes of the second genome (BED).

docs.title: Options

(default: bh) --alpha Largest adjusted p of a significant pair. (default: 0.05) --min-count Fewest shared families of a significant pair. (default: 3) --min-genes Smallest chromosome kept (genes with a family). (default: 20) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 4)

docs.title: mcscan3 micro blocks
docs.text:
Microsynteny blocks shared by many distant genomes.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro blocks [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the multi-species microsynteny of Simakov et al. (2013, Nature 493:526), Zimmermann et al. (2019, Nat Ecol Evol 3:1289, metazoan microsynteny) and Robert et al. (2022, BMC Genomics 23:143, syntenic density). Over hundreds of millions of years gene order decays to small groups of genes that stay together in any order: microsynteny. A block is found in four steps, all on integer arrays:

  1. co-location: in each genome, two genes of different families are co-located when at most --max-gap genes lie between them (all genes count, so the gap is in the genome's own units);
  2. conserved pairs: a pair of families co-located in at least --min-genomes genomes;
  3. family groups: the conserved pairs form a graph of families, weighted 0.5 + 0.5 x the share of genomes with the pair (so the blocks of one lineage still count). It is cut into groups of tightly co-located families by the Constant Potts Model (Leiden, --resolution: the least mean weight within a group). Unlike single linkage, this does not chain neighbouring blocks into whole chromosome arms in closely related genomes; in distant genomes the groups are the isolated blocks themselves;
  4. blocks: in each genome, the genes of a group form runs along the chromosome (at most --max-gap genes between neighbours); a run with at least --min-families families is the block in that genome. A family found in fewer than half the genomes having its group is a chance neighbour and is dropped (and the runs found again). Blocks found in at least --min-genomes genomes are kept; their core families are those in at least two genomes;
  5. significance: a block's E-value is the number of blocks as large (core families), as compact (median span) and as widespread (genomes) expected by chance in genomes of random gene order; blocks above --max-evalue are left out. Small loose blocks shared by two genomes arise by chance surprisingly often; micro density checks the rest by shuffling.

Each block is then present or absent in each genome (<prefix>.profile.tsv, the profile format of network), so micro nodes dates it on a species tree, and micro density measures how tightly packed it is:

mcscan3 micro blocks *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv -o metazoa

Writes <prefix>.blocks.tsv (block, genomes, families, core families), <prefix>.members.tsv (block, genome, chromosome, first and last gene rank, genes in the span, block genes, families) and <prefix>.profile.tsv.

docs.text: Argument Description BEDS Genes of each genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --families Orthogroups.tsv or genefamily table. --max-gap Most genes between neighbouring genes of a block. (default: 5) --min-genomes Fewest genomes sharing a co-located pair or a block. (default: 2) --min-families Fewest families of a block in a genome. (default: 3) --resolution Least mean co-location weight within a family group. (default: 0.5) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 8) --seed Random seed. (default: 666)

docs.title: mcscan3 micro coexpr
docs.text:
Co-expression of the genes of microsynteny blocks.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro coexpr [OPTIONS] MEMBERS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after Zimmermann et al. (2019, Nat Ecol Evol 3:1289; reimplemented from the paper and its published code, metazoan_synteny): genes kept together for hundreds of millions of years may be kept together because they are expressed together. For every block of micro blocks in a genome with an expression matrix (tissues, conditions or cell types as columns), MCscan3 measures:

  • co-expression: the mean Pearson correlation of all pairs of block genes over the conditions (averaged through Fisher's z) on log2(CPM + 1), each condition first centred over all genes (--no-center: not), so a tissue where nearly every gene is low (pollen, seed) does not make every set of genes look co-expressed;
  • against three kinds of random blocks with the same number of expressed genes, drawn --draws times each (default 10,000): shuffled (genes drawn from all block genes of the genome, so the gene content is shuffled among blocks), sampled (runs of neighbouring genes anywhere in the genome) and sampled orthologs (runs of neighbouring genes that have a family, so only genes with homologs elsewhere, as block genes are). The empirical P-value of a block is against the sampled runs; Q-values by Benjamini-Hochberg;

  • specificity: tau of each gene (Yanai et al. 2005, Bioinformatics 21:650) averaged over the block, and the condition bias: the condition holding the largest mean share of the block genes' expression, as a fold over an even spread; Random blocks are drawn --draws times for each number of expressed genes and shared by all blocks of that size. Blocks on organelle chromosomes (--skip-chroms: Pt, Mt, chrC, chrM...) are left out, as organelle genes are transcribed together as operons.

  • paralog share: genes of a block whose family has another gene in the same block;

  • gaps: the number of other genes between neighbouring block genes, with a negative binomial fitted by moments:
mcscan3 micro coexpr eudicots.members.tsv --expr ath=ath.counts.tsv --bed ath=ath.bed \
    --families Orthogroups.tsv -o eudicots.coexpr

Gene IDs of the blocks and of the matrix are matched as they are, then without a version suffix (--strip). Writes <prefix>.blocks.tsv (one line per block and genome), <prefix>.genomes.tsv (observed against random blocks, Mann-Whitney), <prefix>.gaps.tsv and the figures <prefix>.<fmt> (distributions), <prefix>.top.<fmt> (expression of the most co-expressed blocks) and <prefix>.bias.<fmt> (blocks by condition).

(default: []) --bed Genes of the genome, GENOME=BED (random runs and gaps). (default: []) --families Orthogroups.tsv or genefamily (homolog runs, paralogs). --by-sample Samples as columns instead of condition means. --min-cpm Genes below this CPM in every condition are left out. (default: 1.0) --min-genes Fewest expressed genes of a block. (default: 3) --draws Random blocks of each kind per block size. (default: 10000) --skip-chroms Chromosomes left out (organelles). docs.title: mcscan3 micro density
docs.text:
Syntenic density of microsynteny blocks, against shuffled genomes.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro density [OPTIONS] BEDS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the syntenic density of Robert et al. (2022, BMC Genomics 23:143: distinct density regimes and their transitions in early animal genomes). The density of a block in a genome is the share of the genes in its span that belong to it: 1 for a compact block, low when other genes have been inserted between its members. Per genome the command reports the blocks, the genes in them, the share of the genome they cover, and the median density and span.

False blocks. Some blocks arise by chance, more so with many genomes, large gaps and small blocks. Each genome in turn has its gene order shuffled (--shuffles times; the families and the other genomes stay as they are) and the blocks are found again: the blocks still found in the shuffled genome are chance blocks, and their mean over the shuffles, divided by the blocks found in the real genome, estimates the share of false blocks (FDR) at these settings.

Transitions. With --tree, every block is dated (micro nodes) and the density of the blocks arisen at each node is compared with that of the blocks of its parent (Mann-Whitney U, Benjamini-Hochberg): a shift marks a transition between density regimes:

mcscan3 micro density *.bed --families Orthogroups.tsv --tree species.nwk -o metazoa

Writes <prefix>.density.tsv (per genome), <prefix>.members.tsv with each block's density, <prefix>.transitions.tsv with --tree, and the figure <prefix>.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BEDS Genes of each genome (BED).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --families Orthogroups.tsv or genefamily table. --tree Rooted species tree: density transitions between nodes. --shuffles Shuffled copies of each genome (0: none). (default: 3) --max-gap Most genes between neighbouring genes of a block. (default: 5) --min-genomes Fewest genomes sharing a co-located pair or a block. (default: 2) --min-families Fewest families of a block in a genome. (default: 3) --resolution Least mean co-location weight within a family group. (default: 0.5) --max-copies Families with more genes in a genome are left out there. (default: 8) --seed Random seed. (default: 666) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 micro nodes
docs.text:
Microsynteny blocks dated on the species tree.

Group micro · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 micro nodes [OPTIONS] PROFILE TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after Simakov et al. (2013, Nature 493:526) and Zimmermann et al. (2019, Nat Ecol Evol 3:1289). The presence of each block of micro blocks in each genome is mapped onto a rooted species tree by Dollo parsimony (a block arises once, at the last common ancestor of the genomes having it, and may be lost): the blocks ancestral at each node (present there), the novel ones (arisen on the branch above it) and the lost ones:

mcscan3 micro nodes metazoa.profile.tsv species.nwk -o metazoa

Writes <prefix>.gainloss.tsv (per node: genomes below, novel, lost and ancestral blocks), <prefix>.origins.tsv (per block: node of origin and nodes of loss), <prefix>.gainloss.nwk and the figure <prefix>.<format>.

docs.title: mcscan3 network build
docs.text:
Build a synteny network from anchors files.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network build [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, following the synteny network approach of Zhao & Schranz (2017, PNAS; 2019, PNAS), reimplemented from the papers with MCscan3's synteny. Nodes are genes; edges are syntenic anchor pairs from all pairwise (and self) comparisons. The species of each gene comes from the anchors file name, <speciesA>.<speciesB>.anchors: the first column is A, the second is B:

mcscan3 network build *.anchors -o net

Pairs can also come as one table (--table): block, score, gene1, gene2 (or block, gene1, gene2), as written by other synteny-network tools. The species of each gene is then taken from the gene tables in --genes-dir (<species>.bed, BED or the MCScanX layout chr, gene, start, end`; a `<species>__` prefix on gene names is dropped, and `<species><gene><species> is also recognised):

mcscan3 network build --table blocks.tsv.gz --genes-dir genomes/ -o net

Writes <prefix>.edges.tsv (species1, gene1, species2, gene2, source, where the source is the anchors file and block) and prints the numbers of species, nodes and edges.

docs.title: mcscan3 network cluster
docs.text:
Cluster a synteny network.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network cluster [OPTIONS] EDGES

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the synteny-network work of Zhao & Schranz (2017, 2019). The network from network build is split into clusters of genes that are syntenic with one another, each usually one ancestral syntenic locus. Five methods are available:

  • mcl, Markov clustering (van Dongen 2000; default; --inflation), run on blocks of the matrix in parallel threads (--cpus);
  • leiden, the Leiden algorithm (Traag, Waltman & van Eck 2019, Scientific Reports 9:5233; --seed), which guarantees connected communities, unlike Louvain. By default it optimises the Constant Potts Model (--objective cpm): a cluster must be denser inside than --resolution (default 0.1), which finds small loci however large the network is. Modularity (--objective modularity, resolution 1) cannot see communities below a size that grows with the network (Fortunato & Barthélemy 2007, PNAS 104:36) and merges loci. Needs the optional igraph package (pip install mcscan3[network]);
  • infomap, communities that compress a random walk best (Rosvall & Bergstrom 2008, PNAS 105:1118; --trials), as used by the original synteny-network work; igraph;
  • louvain, modularity communities (Blondel et al. 2008; networkx, --seed);
  • components, connected components, which merges clusters joined by any edge.

mcl, leiden and infomap give similar locus-level clusters (network compare measures how similar):

mcscan3 network cluster net.edges.tsv -o net

Writes <prefix>.clusters.tsv (cluster, size, species, members, where members are species|gene, comma-separated), largest cluster first.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description EDGES Edge list from network build.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --method mcl, leiden, infomap, louvain or components. (default: mcl) --inflation MCL inflation. (default: 2.0) --objective Leiden: cpm (Constant Potts Model) or modularity. (default: cpm) --resolution Leiden resolution, larger: smaller clusters (default: 0.1 cpm, 1 modularity). --trials Infomap trials. (default: 10) --seed Random seed (leiden, infomap, louvain). (default: 666) --min-size Smallest cluster written. (default: 2) --cpus Threads for MCL, 0 = all. (default: 0)
