docs.title: mcscan3 network compare
docs.text:
How similar two clusterings of a synteny network are.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network compare [OPTIONS] FIRST SECOND

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Compares two network cluster results (e.g. MCL and Leiden, or two inflation values) on the genes that both cluster:

  • the adjusted Rand index (Hubert & Arabie 1985, J Classif 2:193): agreement on which pairs of genes are together, 1 for identical clusterings and about 0 for unrelated ones;
  • the normalised mutual information (arithmetic normalisation; Strehl & Ghosh 2002, JMLR 3:583; Danon et al. 2005);
  • clusters of the first that the second splits, and clusters of the second that merge clusters of the first:
mcscan3 network compare mcl.clusters.tsv leiden.clusters.tsv

Prints the comparison; --out writes, per cluster of the first, where its genes went.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FIRST Clusters from network cluster. SECOND Other clusters of the same network.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --out Write where the genes of each first cluster went.

docs.title: mcscan3 network gainloss
docs.text:
Where syntenic loci arose and were lost on the species tree.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network gainloss [OPTIONS] PROFILE_FILE SPECIES_TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each synteny cluster (a syntenic locus, network profile) is mapped onto a rooted species tree by Dollo parsimony (Farris 1977, Syst Zool 26:77): a locus arises once, on the branch above the last common ancestor of the species that have it, and is lost on as few branches as possible below it. A locus found in only some lineages is either young (a gain: a lineage- specific transposition or new gene arrangement) or old and lost; the synteny-based phylogenomics of Zhao et al. (2021, Nature Communications 12:3498) reads such presence/absence characters for the history of genome structure:

mcscan3 network gainloss net.profile.tsv species.nwk -o net

Writes <prefix>.gainloss.tsv (per branch, named by its node: leaves below, loci gained on it, loci lost on it, loci present at its end), <prefix>.origins.tsv (per cluster: the node where it arose and the nodes where it was lost) and <prefix>.gainloss.nwk (the tree with the node names used). Internal nodes without a name in the tree are named N1, N2, ... from the root. Species of the profile missing from the tree are an error; tree tips missing from the profile have no loci.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PROFILE_FILE Profile matrix from network profile. SPECIES_TREE Rooted species tree (Newick file or text).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix.

docs.title: mcscan3 network plot
docs.text:
Figures of a synteny network.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network plot [OPTIONS] PREFIX

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the figures of the synteny-network papers (Zhao & Schranz 2017, 2019) and Tree2GD. --kind selects one or more (comma-separated, or all):

  • heatmap: species x species synteny similarity (Jaccard of their syntenic clusters), ordered by the species tree. The lower triangle is the raw similarity; the upper triangle is phylogeny-corrected: the similarity each pair would have at the average tree distance (its residual from an exponential decay with tree distance, fitted to all pairs, added to the decay at the mean distance). Both halves are Jaccard similarities on one colour scale; pairs darker above than below kept more synteny than their divergence predicts;
  • profile: the phylogenomic profile in the layout of the synteny-network papers: species as rows (species tree on the left, a clade strip), the largest --max-clusters clusters as columns ordered by average-linkage clustering of their presence (dendrogram on top), presence dark (--profile-style binary) or shaded by copy number (copies). Shared and lineage-specific synteny show as blocks. Clades come from --clades (speciesclade) or are cut from the tree (best with a balanced, trusted tree);
  • graph: the species network, edges weighted by shared clusters (the strongest --top share of the pairs);
  • cluster: the gene network of one cluster (--cluster), force-directed, nodes coloured by clade.

    • The species tree (--tree) orders the figures; without it, the network tree (network tree) is used. Distances are patristic when the tree has branch lengths, else in nodes:

    mcscan3 network plot net --tree species.nwk --kind all -o net

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PREFIX Prefix of the network files (.profile.tsv, .clusters.tsv, ...).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --tree Species tree (Newick) (default: .tree.nwk). --kind heatmap, profile, graph, cluster (comma-separated) or all. (default: all) --cluster Cluster for --kind cluster (default: the largest). --max-clusters Profile: largest clusters shown. (default: 2000) --top Graph: share of the strongest species pairs drawn. (default: 0.3) --profile-style Profile: binary (presence) or copies. (default: binary) --clades speciesclade colours (default: cut from the tree). --edges Edge list for --kind cluster (default: .edges.tsv). --outfile, -o Output prefix (default: the network prefix). --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 network stats
docs.text:
Statistics of synteny clusters and the links between them.

Group network · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network stats [OPTIONS] EDGES CLUSTERS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. For each cluster from network cluster (a syntenic locus), with the network from network build:

  • size, species, copies: genes, species, the most genes of one species and the species with two or more (retained duplicates, e.g. after a whole-genome duplication);
  • density: edges inside the cluster over all possible (1 for a locus syntenic in every pair);
  • leaving: the share of its genes' edges that go to other clusters (low: a well-separated locus);
  • class, pan-synteny classes after pan-genome practice (e.g. Kaas et al. 2012, BMC Genomics 13:577): core (every species), softcore (at least --softcore, default 95%, of them), shell, cloud (under --cloud, default 15%) and private (one species).

Clusters joined by many edges are listed as links (<prefix>.links.tsv): syntenic loci that are adjacent or were duplicated together, the trace of segmental duplications, translocations and fusions in the network. The summary gives the modularity of the clustering (Newman & Girvan 2004, Phys Rev E 69:026113; higher: the clusters explain the network better) and the share of edges inside clusters:

mcscan3 network stats net.edges.tsv net.clusters.tsv -o net

Writes <prefix>.cluster_stats.tsv and <prefix>.links.tsv; prints the summary.

docs.text: Argument Description EDGES Edge list from network build. CLUSTERS Clusters from network cluster.

docs.title: Options

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 network tree [OPTIONS] PROFILE_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the phylogenomic synteny profiling of Zhao & Schranz (2019, PNAS). Species are compared by which synteny clusters they share: the Jaccard distance between their presence/absence profiles (--distance jaccard) or the fraction of differing clusters (hamming). A tree is built by neighbour joining (--method nj) or UPGMA:

mcscan3 network tree net.profile.tsv -o net --outgroup rice

Writes <prefix>.tree.nwk and <prefix>.distances.tsv. --outgroup roots the tree. For a maximum-likelihood tree, give the PHYLIP matrix of network profile --phylip to RAxML or IQ-TREE.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PROFILE_FILE Profile matrix from network profile.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --distance jaccard or hamming. (default: jaccard) --method nj or upgma. (default: nj) --outgroup Root the tree on this species.

Group ortholog · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog enrich [OPTIONS] OMGFILE GROUPSFILE NTAXA

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For each OMG family (genes<TAB>taxa from ortholog omg-parse) that lacks some of the ntaxa taxa, candidates are the other members of the first gene's group (groups file, one comma-separated group per line) from the missing taxa. docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog hogs
docs.text:
Hierarchical orthologous groups at every node of the species tree.

Group ortholog · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog hogs [OPTIONS] SPECIES_TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the bottom-up HOG inference of OMA and FastOMA (Altenhoff AM et al. 2013, PLoS One 8:e53786; Majidian S et al. 2025, Nat Methods 22:269), with synteny as extra evidence. A HOG at a node is the set of genes descending from one ancestral gene of that node. Within each gene family (--families; without it, the connected groups of the hits), HOGs are built from the leaves to the root:

  1. at a species, every gene is a HOG;
  2. at a node, every HOG of each child is linked to its best match among the HOGs of each other child (the highest bit score between their genes; matches within --ratio of the best count too). Bit scores of gene pairs in a synteny block (--anchors) are raised by --synteny-bonus (x 1.5 by default), so the positional copy wins among close paralogs. A syntenic pair whose two genes both lie in clearly stronger blocks (median bit score) of the same two genomes is set aside: after a duplication and differential loss, the weaker block pairs paralogs (pseudo-orthologs), the stronger one is where the orthologs were;
  3. links are taken from the strongest down and join HOGs into the node's HOGs, except that two HOGs of the same child are joined only when they are at least as similar to each other as the link (they are paralogs from a duplication after the node, in-paralogs); otherwise they come from a duplication before the node and stay in different HOGs;
  4. a HOG left alone is kept at the node only when its genes match genes outside the node (the gene was there and was lost in the other children); otherwise it arose in the child's lineage.

A node's HOGs are its ancestral genes. Two genes of two species are orthologs when they are in the same HOG at the species' last common ancestor; a HOG that holds two HOGs of one child marks a duplication on the branch to that child:

mcscan3 ortholog hogs species.nwk --bed-dir data --hits *.last --anchors *.anchors \
    --families Orthogroups.tsv -o eudicots

Writes <prefix>.hogs.tsv (node, HOG, parent HOG, species, genes), <prefix>.genes.tsv (the HOG of every gene at every node above it), <prefix>.orthoxml (OrthoXML 0.4, with ortholog and paralog groups) and <prefix>.summary.tsv (per node: HOGs, duplications, gains).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SPECIES_TREE Rooted species tree (Newick); leaves are .bed names.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --hits Homology hits (BLAST tabular / LAST m8), all species pairs. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --bed-dir Directory of the .bed files. (default: .) --anchors Synteny anchors files: links in blocks weigh more. --families Gene families to split (default: from the hits). --synteny-bonus Score factor of links inside synteny blocks. (default: 1.5) --ratio Least score, relative to a gene's best, of a kept link. (default: 0.9) --max-family Largest family split (larger ones are skipped). (default: 3000) --format Image format of the tree figure. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

Hierarchical orthologous groups at every node of the eudicot tree, guided by synteny.

mkdir -p hogs && H=() && A=() && for a in amborella grape ath poplar peach soybean; do for b in amborella grape ath poplar peach soybean; do [ -e $R/synteny/$a.$b.last ] && H+=(--hits $R/synteny/$a.$b.last);  [ $a != $b ] && [ -e $R/synteny/$a.$b.lifted.anchors ] && A+=(--anchors $R/synteny/$a.$b.lifted.anchors); done; done;  mcscan3 ortholog hogs $R/ancestral/species.nwk --bed-dir $R/data "${H[@]}" "${A[@]}" --families $R/orthology/orthofinder/Results_mcscan3/Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv -o hogs/eudicots

run time 1 min 34 s · data real · showcase step ortholog_hogs

Variables: $R the eudicot pipeline run (six genomes).

Inputs: a ploidy file (species ploidy per line, in taxon order), an anchors file and a BLAST file. docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog qc [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the orthogroup and genome checks of cogeqc (Almeida-Silva F & Van de Peer Y, Bioconductor), reimplemented with its own scores. Reads orthogroups from:

  • an OrthoFinder results folder (Orthogroups/Orthogroups.tsv, unassigned genes, duplications per species tree node, the rooted species tree), or Orthogroups.tsv / N0.tsv alone;
  • MCscan3 HOGs (ortholog hogs: <prefix>.genes.tsv; every gene in its topmost HOG, or the HOGs at --node);
  • a long table (group, species, gene) or one group per line (genes, with --pep/--bed for their species).

and reports, for every species: genes, genes in orthogroups, unassigned genes, orthogroups with the species, species-specific orthogroups and their genes, single- and multi-copy orthogroups, duplications (OrthoFinder); orthogroups shared by every pair of species; orthogroup sizes and copy numbers. With domains (--domains, any of the formats of mcscan3.core.domains, or --pfam Pfam-A.hmm to search the proteomes) every orthogroup gets:

  • homogeneity H: the mean Sørensen-Dice similarity 2|A∩B|/(|A|+|B|) of the domain sets of all pairs of its annotated genes (genes without domains are left out; up to --max-size genes, sampled beyond). H is also given within each species, and for orthogroups of the same sizes with the domain sets shuffled among genes (what chance gives);
  • dispersal D: for each domain, (groups holding it − 1) / (genes with it − 1), 0 when all its genes are in one orthogroup and 1 when every gene is alone; D of an orthogroup is the mean over its domains. Unassigned genes count as groups of one, so domains split by under-clustering raise D;
  • score H − D: high for orthogroups that are both internally consistent and not split.

With --busco (BUSCO or phylo busco runs) and --genome (assemblies) the genome table adds completeness, assembly length, N50/L50 of scaffolds and contigs, GC and gaps. --compare measures agreement with a second grouping (orthogroups kept exactly, split, merged; best Jaccard; adjusted Rand index):

mcscan3 ortholog qc --orthofinder Results_Oct26 --domains pfam.domtbl --busco ath=busco_ath -o qc

(default: []) --bed Annotation NAME=BED (gene species and counts; repeatable). (default: []) --domains Domains: gene/domain table, HMMER domtblout, pfam_scan or InterProScan (repeatable). docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog run
docs.text:
The one-command MCscan pipeline (mcscan3 ortholog run; legacy compara.catalog ortholog).

Group ortholog · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog run [OPTIONS] SPECIES_A SPECIES_B

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For species a and b (files a.bed, a.cds / a.pep, b.bed, ...):

mcscan3 ortholog run grape peach --cpus=8
  1. align a against b (LAST by default; --align-soft blast, diamond or mmseqs) -> a.b.last
  2. filter blastfilter -> a.b.last.filtered
  3. synteny scan with liftover from a.b.last -> a.b.anchors, a.b.lifted.anchors
  4. optionally quota align --quota on the lifted anchors
  5. dot plot a.b.pdf (unless --no-dotplot)

--full instead builds 1:1 blocks (quota 1:1), lifts them over, stacks them with synteny mcscan both ways and recruits reciprocal best hits: a.b.ortholog and b.a.ortholog. Steps whose outputs are newer than their inputs are skipped, as in the original.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SPECIES_A Species a (a.bed + a.cds/a.pep). SPECIES_B Species b.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --dbtype nucl (.cds) or prot (.pep). (default: nucl) --full Full 1x1 mode, including blocks and RBH. --tandem-nmax Merge tandem genes within distance. (default: 10) --cscore C-score cutoff. (default: 0.7) --dist Extent of flanking regions to search. (default: 20) -n, --min-size Minimum number of anchors in a cluster. (default: 4) --quota Quota align parameter, e.g. 1:2. --exclude Remove anchors from a previous run. --self-remove Self comparison: drop hits above this identity. (default: 98) --no-strip-names Do not strip alternative splicing. --liftover-dist Liftover distance (default: --dist // 2). --cpus Number of CPUs, 0 = all. (default: 0) --skipempty Dot plot: skip seqids without matches. --nochpf Dot plot: do not change the contig names. --nostdpf Dot plot: do not standardise contig names. --genomenames Dot plot axis names, e.g. "A_B". --grid-color Dot plot grid colour index (0-8; the original's --theme). --notex Dot plot: do not use TeX. --no-dotplot Do not make the dot plot. --ignore-zero-anchor Continue when no anchor is found. --align-soft last, blast, diamond (proteins) or mmseqs. (default: last) --out-format Also write the lifted anchors as mcscanx, wgdi, genespace, iadhore, synvisio, bedpe, tsv.

docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog soi
docs.text:
Keep orthologous synteny using the Orthology Index.

Group ortholog · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog soi [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: a reimplementation of the Orthology Index method (SOI; Zhang et al. 2025, Nucleic Acids Research) from its description. A syntenic block's Orthology Index (OI) is the fraction of its anchor pairs that an independent orthology inference also calls orthologs. Blocks from speciation (orthologous synteny) have a high OI. Blocks from older duplications (out-paralogous synteny) have a low one. Blocks with OI >= --cutoff (default 0.6) are kept:

mcscan3 ortholog soi grape.peach.anchors --orthologs grape_peach.orthologs.tsv

Orthologs come from one of:

  • --orthologs: a file of ortholog pairs (two columns), or an OrthoFinder Orthologues directory (Orthologues_<A>/<A>__v__<B>.tsv, all pairs within each row);
  • --blast: reciprocal best hits of the BLAST file (a quick stand-in when no orthology inference is available).

Writes <anchors prefix>.soi.anchors (the kept blocks) and <anchors prefix>.oi (one line per block: id, anchors, ortholog anchors, OI, kept), and prints a summary to stderr.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file of two genomes.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --orthologs Ortholog pairs (2 columns) or an OrthoFinder Orthologues directory. --blast Use reciprocal best hits of this BLAST file as orthologs. --cutoff Keep blocks with an Orthology Index at least this. (default: 0.6) --strip-names Match genes without transcript suffixes (.1, .t01). --outfile, -o Kept blocks (default: .soi.anchors).

docs.title: mcscan3 ortholog tandem
docs.text:
Tandem gene clusters (mcscan3 ortholog tandem; legacy compara.catalog tandem).

Group ortholog · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 ortholog tandem [OPTIONS] BLAST_FILE CDS_FILE BED_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
From a self BLAST (comment-free table), genes within --tandem-nmax genes of each other that align over at least --percent-overlap % of the shorter gene (e-value <= --evalue) are grouped. With --not-self the BLAST is between two gene sets and neighbouring homologs of similar length are grouped; --genefamily groups all homologs. Writes one comma-separated family per line; a summary goes to stderr:

mcscan3 ortholog tandem grape.grape.last.filtered grape.cds grape.bed -o grape.tandem

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLAST_FILE Self BLAST without comment lines (e.g. a.a.last.filtered). CDS_FILE CDS (or protein) FASTA, for gene lengths. BED_FILE BED of the genome.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --tandem-nmax Merge tandem genes within distance. (default: 3) --percent-overlap Tandem genes have >= x% aligned sequence. (default: 50) --evalue E-value cutoff. (default: 0.01) --not-self The BLAST is not a self comparison. --strip-gene-name Isoform separator; None to disable. (default: .) --genefamily Compile gene families by similarity. --outfile, -o Output file. (default: stdout)

docs.title: mcscan3 pad cluster
docs.text:
Segment chromosomes and cluster the segments (mcscan3 pad cluster; legacy compara.pad cluster).

Group pad · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pad cluster [OPTIONS] BLASTFILE ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Method of Tang et al. (2010) PNAS: chromosomes are cut at synteny block boundaries (blocks with at least --minsize anchors) into segments (<prefix>.pad.bed); the -log(P) of hit enrichment between every pair of segments is written to <q>.<s>.logmp.txt and clustered with CLUSTER 3.0 (Pearson correlation, average linkage) into .cdt/.gtr/.atr files.

Needs the CLUSTER 3.0 command-line program (--path or MCSCAN3_CLUSTER_PATH); note that Graphviz ships an unrelated program also called cluster.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLASTFILE Filtered BLAST file. ANCHORFILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED. --sbed Subject BED. --minsize Only segment using blocks >= this size. (default: 10) --path Directory containing the CLUSTER 3.0 cluster program.

docs.title: mcscan3 pan genes
docs.text:
Synteny-constrained pan-gene sets across genomes.

Group pan · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pan genes [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, following the idea of GENESPACE (Lovell et al. 2022, eLife), reimplemented from the paper with MCscan3's own synteny. Each pairwise anchors file (<a>.<b>.anchors, e.g. from ortholog run) links syntenic homologs. The connected groups of genes across all genomes are the pan-genes. Each pan-gene is placed on the reference genome by the position of its reference gene. A pan-gene without a reference gene takes the position of the nearest pan-gene (within --window genes, on the same genome) that has one:

mcscan3 pan genes grape peach poplar --ref grape -o pan

Genomes are named by their BED files (<genome>.bed). Anchors files are looked up in --anchors-dir for every pair, in either order (<a>.<b>.<suffix> or <b>.<a>.<suffix>). Writes <prefix>.pangenes.tsv: one line per pan-gene in reference order, with its reference position, category and genes per genome (comma-separated, . if absent). Categories are core (in all genomes), shell (in several) and private (in one). Prints counts per category and genome.

docs.title: mcscan3 pan run
docs.text:
Pan-genome of many genomes, gene-based and sequence-based.

Group pan · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pan run [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Two views of the same question (what every genome shares, what only some carry, and whether sampling more genomes keeps adding new content):

  • gene-based: pan-genes are the syntenic homologs linked across genomes (pan genes). Missing pairwise synteny is computed first (ortholog run on proteins or CDS). Genes found in no anchor are pan-genes of one genome;
  • sequence-based: each assembly is sketched by FracMinHash (k-mers kept with a hash below 2**64 / scaled, Irber et al. 2022), so no annotation or reference is needed. Each kept k-mer stands for scaled bp of distinct sequence.

Both give a presence/absence matrix, from which MCscan3 reports:

  • classes: core (in every genome), softcore (at least --softcore of them), shell (two or more) and cloud (one genome), in total and per genome;
  • accumulation curves: pan-genome and core genome size as genomes are added, over --permutations random orders (all orders when there are fewer);
  • Heaps' law: the new content added by the k-th genome fitted as kappa * k**-alpha; alpha < 1 means an open pan-genome that keeps growing, alpha > 1 a closed one (Tettelin et al. 2008, Curr Opin Microbiol 11:472);
  • similarity: shared content of every pair of genomes (Jaccard), and for sequences the containment both ways and the Mash identity estimate (Ondov et al. 2016, Genome Biol 17:132):
mcscan3 pan run dmel dsim dyak dpse --bed-dir insects --fasta dmel=dmel.fa ... -o flies

Writes <prefix>.<mode>.{pav,classes,frequency,curve,similarity}.tsv for gene and seq, <prefix>.gene.pangenes.tsv (the genes of each pan-gene), <prefix>.summary.tsv, <prefix>.json, the sketches (<prefix>.sketches/, reused) and four figures: <prefix>.curves, <prefix>.composition, <prefix>.similarity and <prefix>.pav.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names for the gene-based pan-genome (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --mode gene, sequence or both. (default: both) --fasta Assembly for the sequence-based pan-genome, NAME=FILE (repeatable; .gz read). (default: []) --ref Reference genome for pan-gene order (default: first). --bed-dir Directory of .bed and .pep (or .cds). (default: .) --anchors-dir Anchors files (default: --bed-dir). --suffix Anchors file suffix. (default: lifted.anchors) --align Compute missing pairwise synteny. --dbtype prot (.pep) or nucl (.cds) for missing synteny. (default: prot) --align-soft last, diamond, mmseqs or blast. (default: last) --k k-mer size of the sketches (at most 31). (default: 21) --scaled Keep one k-mer in this many (bp per sketch hash). (default: 1000) --min-length Leave out sequences shorter than this (bp). (default: 0) --softcore Share of genomes for the softcore class. (default: 0.9) --permutations Random genome orders for the curves. (default: 100) --seed Random seed. (default: 1) --cpus Processes for sketching and alignment. (default: 1) --format Figure format (pdf, png, svg). (default: pdf) --dpi Figure resolution. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo build
docs.text:
NJ and ML trees from CDS (mcscan3 phylo build; legacy apps.phylo build).

Group phylo · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo build [OPTIONS] FILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Steps, all with external programs:

  1. translate the CDS (unless a protein file is given) and align the proteins with MUSCLE (default) or ClustalW (--msa);
  2. back-translate to a codon alignment with PAL2NAL;
  3. remove poorly aligned blocks with Gblocks (--nogblocks to skip; then --synonymous or --fourfold keep only those sites);
  4. a bootstrapped neighbour-joining tree with EMBOSS PHYLIP (fseqboot, fdnadist, fneighbor, fconsense, ffitch; --noneighbor to skip);
  5. a maximum-likelihood tree with RAxML or PhyML (--ml=raxml|phyml).

Files go to <outdir>/alignment and <outdir>/tree (<cds prefix>.NJ.unrooted.dnd, <cds prefix>.ML.unrooted.dnd):

mcscan3 phylo build family0.cds --ml=phyml

--outgroup=<file> roots the trees on the first outgroup name (prefix) found; --SH=<tree> runs RAxML's SH test against a reference tree; --treefix (with --stree, --smap) runs TreeFix on the RAxML tree. Rooting and the NJ tree need the phylo extra (ete4).

Differences from the original (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.11): it crashed on Python 3 when reading Gblocks output, and did not find the -gb.fa file that current Gblocks builds write.

docs.text: Argument Description FILES [prot.fasta] cds.fasta

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --longest Use the longest ORF (no protein file, e.g. ESTs). --nogblocks Do not edit the alignment with Gblocks. --synonymous Keep synonymous sites only (with --nogblocks). --fourfold Keep fourfold degenerate sites (with --nogblocks). --msa Protein aligner: clustalw or muscle. (default: muscle) --noneighbor Do not build the NJ tree. --ml ML tree program: raxml or phyml. --outgroup File with outgroup names, in order of preference. --SH, --sh Reference Newick tree for the SH test. --shout SH output file name. (default: SH_out.txt) --treefix Rearrange the ML tree with TreeFix. --stree Species Newick tree (TreeFix). --smap gene_name_patternspecies_name file (TreeFix). --outdir Output directory. (default: .)

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo busco
docs.text:
Phylogenomics from single-copy BUSCO genes.

Group phylo · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo busco [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the BUSCO_phylogenomics workflow (McGowan J & Fitzpatrick DA; reimplemented from its description) and BUSCO itself (Manni M et al. 2021, Mol Biol Evol 38:4647), made faster:

  1. markers: annotated proteomes (--pep NAME=FILE) are searched directly with the lineage's profile HMMs in one hmmsearch per genome (seconds instead of a BUSCO run); a protein is a match above the lineage's score cutoff (and counts only for the BUSCO it matches best), complete when its HMM coverage reaches the expected length minus two standard deviations, else fragmented; one complete match is single, more scoring at least 85% of the best are duplicated (weaker ones are paralogs, not copies). Finished BUSCO runs (--busco NAME=DIR) are read instead when given;
  2. loci: single-copy BUSCOs present in at least --occupancy of the genomes;
  3. alignment of each locus in parallel (FAMSA, MAFFT or MUSCLE; cached), trimming of gappy columns (--max-gap) natively, and loci shorter than --min-length dropped;
  4. supermatrix with a partition file (RAxML-NG and NEXUS formats), and trees: a concatenated maximum-likelihood tree (IQ-TREE's fast search with SH-aLRT support by default; --partitioned for a model per locus, --bootstrap for ultrafast bootstrap; or FastTree), gene trees (FastTree or IQ-TREE, in parallel) and their coalescent summary (ASTRAL);
  5. gene concordance factors of every branch, natively (Minh et al. 2020, Mol Biol Evol 37:2727), and the Robinson-Foulds distance between the concatenated and coalescent trees:
mcscan3 phylo busco --pep scer=scer.pep --pep dmel=dmel.pep ... --manifest manifest.tsv \
    --outgroup ath -o tree/euk

--lineage is a BUSCO dataset name (diptera_odb10; downloaded once into --lineage-dir) or folder (hmms/, scores_cutoff, lengths_cutoff). With auto (the default) the species of the genomes are looked up in NCBI Taxonomy and the most specific lineage holding them all is chosen (--odb sets the dataset version). Species come from --species NAME=SPECIES (a name or taxid), from fetch manifests (--manifest), or from genome names that are species names (Saccharomyces_cerevisiae). Writes <prefix>.status.tsv (status of every BUSCO in every genome), <prefix>.summary.tsv (BUSCO scores), <prefix>.loci.tsv, <prefix>.supermatrix.faa, <prefix>.partitions.{txt,nex}, <prefix>.concat.nwk, <prefix>.genetrees.nwk, <prefix>.astral.nwk, <prefix>.species.nwk (rooted, with gCF), <prefix>.concordance.tsv and the figures <prefix>.tree, <prefix>.matrix and <prefix>.compare. Intermediate files go to <prefix>.work/.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --pep Proteome, NAME=FASTA (searched with the lineage HMMs; repeatable). (default: []) --busco Finished BUSCO/compleasm run, NAME=DIR (repeatable). (default: []) --lineage BUSCO dataset (diptera_odb10), its folder, or auto: chosen from NCBI Taxonomy. (default: auto) --species Species of a genome for --lineage auto, NAME=SPECIES --manifest Manifest of fetch genome/fetch taxon (species). (default: []) --odb OrthoDB version of the datasets for --lineage auto (10 or 12). (default: 10) --lineage-dir Where datasets are kept. (default: ~/.cache/mcscan3/busco) --occupancy Least share of genomes with a single-copy locus. (default: 0.8) --aligner famsa, mafft or muscle. (default: famsa) --max-gap Alignment columns with more gaps are trimmed. (default: 0.5) --min-length Loci shorter than this after trimming are dropped. (default: 50) --tree-tool Concatenated tree: auto, iqtree3, iqtree, FastTree. (default: auto) --gene-trees Gene trees: fasttree, iqtree or none. (default: fasttree) --model Model of the concatenated tree (IQ-TREE; MFP to select). (default: LG+G4) --bootstrap Ultrafast bootstrap replicates (full search; 0: none). (default: 0) --alrt SH-aLRT replicates for branch support (0: none). (default: 1000) --partitioned A model per locus (slower). --copy-ratio Least score of a second copy, share of the best. (default: 0.85) --outgroup Outgroup genome(s) (default: midpoint root). (default: []) --max-loci Use at most this many loci (0: all). (default: 0) --cpus Parallel jobs. (default: 1) --seed Random seed. (default: 1) --format Figure format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

A tree of fungi, insects and plants from single-copy BUSCO genes: the lineage (eukaryota_odb10) is chosen from NCBI Taxonomy, proteomes are searched directly, and the concatenated, gene and coalescent trees are compared with gene concordance. Duplicated BUSCOs show the whole-genome duplications of soybean and poplar.

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo draw
docs.text:
Draw Newick trees, alone or combined (mcscan3 phylo draw; legacy apps.phylo draw).

Group phylo · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo draw [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
--input is one Newick file or a directory holding only tree files. Each tree is drawn as it is rooted (use plot tree for rerooting and more annotations); node support above --scutoff is shown in red. --combine=RxC puts R x C trees on one page (trees<N>.<format>); otherwise each tree goes to <tree prefix>.<format> in --outdir:

mcscan3 phylo draw --input=tree/family0.ML.unrooted.dnd --format=png

--sh gives a file of tree_file<TAB>SH p-value lines (as written by phylo build --SH). --trunc-name shortens names (headN, oheadN, tailN, otailN). Needs the phylo extra.

The original crashed on Python 3 (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.12). Its --barcode and --leafcolorfile options had no effect and are accepted but ignored.

docs.title: mcscan3 phylo prepare
docs.text:
Per-family CDS files from MCscan output (mcscan3 phylo prepare; legacy apps.phylo prepare).

Group phylo · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 phylo prepare [OPTIONS] MCSCANFILE CDSFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Each row of an MCscan table (synteny mcscan output: one column per genome, . for none, comma-separated tandem genes) with more than three genes becomes <outdir>/<first gene>.cds, ready for phylo build:

mcscan3 phylo prepare families.mcscan all.cds --outdir=sequences

--addtandem=<tandem file> first replaces anchors by their tandem clusters (the file must cover all genomes) and merges rows that overlap within 10 rows. --writecolors writes leafcolors.txt (gene, R,G,B of its column) for phylo draw.

Differences from the original (docs/DEVIATIONS.md): it crashed on Python 3 (A.10), and wrote each family in hash-seed-dependent order; MCscan3 writes genes in column order.

docs.text: Argument Description MCSCANFILE MCscan table (synteny mcscan output). CDSFILE CDS FASTA of all genomes.

docs.title: Options

docs.title: mcscan3 pipeline inputs
docs.text:
Find and prepare the genomes of a project directory (mcscan3 pipeline inputs; first step of pipeline run).

Group pipeline · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pipeline inputs [OPTIONS] DIRECTORY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each species is the file-name prefix before the first dot (grape.gff3.gz, grape.dna.fa.gz, grape.cds, ...). FASTA files are classified by name (cds, pep/protein/prot/faa, dna/genome/genomic/fna) and otherwise by content: protein, short nucleotide records (CDS), or long nucleotide records (genome). A species can be given as any of:

  • gff + genome: the longest coding transcript per gene, CDS spliced from the genome and translated (prep genome);
  • gff + cds [+ pep]: the longest transcript per gene from the GFF (the attribute that matches the FASTA names is found automatically), with the CDS and protein subset to it;
  • bed + cds [+ pep], or bed + pep: already processed. Names are checked and the protein is translated from the CDS when missing. The .bed may also be an MCScanX gene table (chr, gene, start, end); it is converted to BED.

--samples (TSV: species, gff, genome, bed, cds, pep; empty cells allowed) overrides the detection. Prepared files are <outdir>/<species>.bed, .cds (if any) and .pep, with clean IDs (transcript: and similar prefixes removed) and one record per BED gene.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description DIRECTORY Directory with genome files (gff, genome, bed, cds, pep).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outdir, -o Also prepare the files into this directory. --samples Sample sheet to use instead of detection.

docs.title: mcscan3 pipeline run
docs.text:
Everything from a directory of genomes, in one command.

Group pipeline · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 pipeline run [OPTIONS] DIRECTORY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Point it at a directory of raw or processed genome files (see pipeline inputs) and it runs, resuming where it stopped:

  1. inputs: one clean <species>.bed/.cds/.pep per species;
  2. orthology: OrthoFinder (orthogroups, orthologues, rooted species tree) when installed, else MCscan3's own orthogroups (DIAMOND + MCL, reciprocal best hits);
  3. synteny: ortholog run for every pair of species (and each species against itself), with dot plots;
  4. orthologous synteny: every pairwise block is scored by its Orthology Index against the orthologues (ortholog soi), so blocks from older duplications are set aside;
  5. pan-genes: the new part. Pan-genes are linked only by anchors that are orthologous synteny and fall in the same orthogroup, so they hold syntenic orthologues and not out-paralogues. Each pan-gene is then completed with the other members of its orthogroups (up to 40 genes), marked separately (like GENESPACE's non-syntenic orthologues), and placed on the reference. A riparian plot follows;
  6. network: a synteny network of all pairwise (and self) anchors, its clusters, profiles and a synteny-based species tree, to set against the orthology species tree;
  7. ancestral genomes on the species tree (CARs at every node), with each genome painted by the root's CARs;
  8. duplications: duplicate-gene classes per species (an outgroup gives transposed copies);
  9. WGD (--ks, slower): anchor-pair Ks (yn00), block medians and mixture models per species;
  10. Gene Ontology (--go-obo and --go-annotations): enrichment of every gene set the run produced, per species: duplication classes, pan-gene categories, orthogroup classes (core, single-copy, accessory, species-specific, expanded, contracted), synteny-network clusters, and genes syntenic or not with the reference (go enrich on go sets);
  11. report: report.html, everything on one page.

Example:

mcscan3 pipeline run genomes/ -o results --ref grape --cpus 8 --ks

Output directory: samples.tsv (what was found), data/ (prepared files), orthology/ (OrthoFinder results or MCscan3's own), synteny/ (ortholog run per pair; with --synteny-format also synteny/formats/: the blocks as MCScanX, WGDI, i-ADHoRe, BEDPE, ... files), soi/ (Orthology Index per block and *.soi.anchors), pan/ (pangenes.tsv, riparian.png), network/ (net.*), ancestral/ (CARs per node, anc.summary.tsv, paintings), dup/, wgd/ (with --ks) and report.html. Steps that fail are listed in the report's notes and the others still run. OrthoFinder with only three species cannot root its species tree reliably: give --tree when the rooting matters (ancestral genomes).

The genomes can also be downloaded first: --fetch takes accessions or species from NCBI, Ensembl, the Genome Warehouse, CNGB or URLs (as fetch genome; repeatable) and --taxon the best annotated genome of each species of a taxon (as fetch taxon; --taxon-max, --taxon-per-genus, --taxon-level). They go to <outdir>/genomes together with the files of the directory, if one is given, so your own genomes can be compared with public ones. The NCBI taxonomy tree of the species is compared with the gene-based species trees (a taxonomy group missing from a tree counts as a conflict; unresolved taxonomy does not), and is used for ancestral genomes when it is fully resolved and OrthoFinder gave no tree:

mcscan3 pipeline run -o grasses --taxon Poaceae --taxon-max 8 --cpus 16 --ks
mcscan3 pipeline run my_genomes -o run --fetch GCF_000001735.4 --fetch ensembl:vitis_vinifera

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description DIRECTORY Directory with genome files (see pipeline inputs); optional with --fetch or --taxon.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outdir, -o Output directory (re-running resumes). --samples Sample sheet to use instead of detection. --ref Reference genome for pan-gene positions (default: first). --cpus CPUs for aligners and Ks. (default: 1) --orthofinder auto, yes or no. (default: auto) --tree Rooted species tree (Newick) (default: OrthoFinder's). --soi-cutoff Orthology Index of orthologous blocks. (default: 0.6) --ks Also anchor/block Ks and WGD mixtures per species (slower). --search Homology search: pairwise (LAST per pair, CDS) or one search of all proteomes with mmseqs or diamond. (default: pairwise) --gpu With --search mmseqs: MMseqs2-GPU (NVIDIA GPU). --jobs Genome pairs processed at once (synteny step); at most --cpus. (default: 1) --steps Comma-separated steps to (re)run (default: all). Steps: orthology, synteny, formats, soi, pan, network, ancestral, dup, wgd, wgd-consensus, go, report. --go-obo Gene Ontology (OBO): enables the GO enrichment step. --go-annotations GO annotations: FILE for every species, or SPECIES=FILE (repeatable). (default: []) --go-strip Regular expression removed from annotated gene ids. --synteny-format Also write every pair's synteny blocks as: anchors, mcscanx, wgdi, genespace, iadhore, synvisio, bedpe, tsv (comma-separated) in synteny/formats/. --fetch Genome to download first: accession, ncbi:/ensembl:SPECIES, GWH, CNGB, URL (repeatable). (default: []) --taxon Download the best annotated genome of each species of a taxon. --taxon-max --taxon: at most this many genomes (0: all). (default: 10) --taxon-per-genus --taxon: genomes per genus (0: any). (default: 1) --taxon-level --taxon: least assembly level. (default: chromosome) --taxon-source --taxon: databases (ncbi, ensembl). (default: ncbi,ensembl)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot blastplot
docs.text:
Dot plot of a BLAST table (mcscan3 plot blastplot; legacy graphics.blastplot).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot blastplot [OPTIONS] BLASTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Hits are placed by base-pair position along the concatenated sequences. --qsizes/--ssizes (two-column sizes files) set the sequence borders and order; --qbed/--sbed place gene hits at their gene positions (a <bed prefix>.sizes file is written when no sizes file is given). At least one of the two options is needed for each genome:

mcscan3 plot blastplot grape.peach.last.filtered --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed

--dotstyle is dot, circle or line (hit extents); --qh/--sh highlight BED regions; --proportional scales the figure height to the genome size ratio.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLASTFILE BLAST table (-m8 / outfmt 6).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qsizes Query sizes file (seqidlength). --ssizes Subject sizes file. --qbed Query BED: place hits at gene positions. --sbed Subject BED. --qselect Minimum size of query sequences to show. (default: 0) --sselect Minimum size of subject sequences to show. (default: 0) --qh BED of query regions to highlight. --sh BED of subject regions to highlight. --dotstyle dot, circle or line. (default: dot) --proportional Figure height:width = genome size ratio. --stripnames, --strip-names Remove trailing .N from gene names. --nmax Plot at most N dots (random subset). --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 8x8) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 150) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... (default: pdf) --font Font: Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Palatino, Schoolbook, Arial. (default: Helvetica) --style Axes background: darkgrid, whitegrid, dark, white, ticks. (default: dark) --diverge Contrasting colour scheme (ColorBrewer diverging name). (default: PiYG) --cmap Matplotlib colour map. (default: jet) --notex Do not use LaTeX (MCscan3 uses LaTeX only when installed). --chinese Render Chinese labels (implies --notex). --seed Random seed when assigning colours. --theme classic (original look) or mcscan3. (default: classic)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot chromosome
docs.text:
Paint features onto chromosomes (mcscan3 plot chromosome; legacy graphics.chromosome).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot chromosome [OPTIONS] BEDFILE MAPPINGFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Features in a BED file are painted onto vertical chromosome glyphs, coloured by class. The optional id_mappings file maps feature ids to classes (id<TAB>class[<TAB>color]); without it each feature id is its own class. A feature named centromere marks a centromere. Chromosome lengths come from --sizes (else the last feature end):

mcscan3 plot chromosome peach.bed peach.idmap --sizes=peach.sizes --seed=666

Class colours are random unless given in the mapping file (--seed for reproducible colours). --gauge draws a Mb ruler; --imagemap also writes an HTML image map (<prefix>.map) of --winsize windows; --mergedist merges nearby regions of the same class.

(default: 0) --empty Legend label for unpainted regions. --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 6x6) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). docs.title: mcscan3 plot circos
docs.text:
Circular synteny plot of several genomes.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot circos [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the circular genome plots of Circos (Krzywinski et al. 2009, Genome Research). The chromosomes of every genome sit on one circle, each genome on its own arc (equal arcs by default, or arcs in proportion to genome size with --scale bp). An outer track shows gene density along the chromosomes; inside, every syntenic block between two genomes is a ribbon through the centre, coloured by the chromosome of the reference genome it touches, or traced to it through the other blocks:

mcscan3 plot circos dmel dyak dpse agam --ref dmel --suffix lifted.anchors -o insects.circos.pdf

Genomes are named by their BED files (<genome>.bed); anchors files between pairs of genomes are looked up as <a>.<b>.<suffix> or <b>.<a>.<suffix>. --pairs ref (default) draws the blocks of the reference with each other genome, --pairs ring those of neighbouring genomes around the circle and --pairs all every pair with an anchors file.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names, clockwise from the top (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference genome: ribbons are coloured by its chromosomes. --outfile, -o Output figure (PDF, PNG or SVG). (default: circos.pdf) --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix. (default: anchors) --pairs Blocks drawn: ref (reference with each genome), ring or all. (default: ref) --scale fit (equal arc per genome) or bp (arcs by genome size). (default: fit) --labels Display names, comma-separated. --min-block Do not draw blocks with fewer anchors. (default: 10) --min-frac Leave out chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction (scaffolds). (default: 0.005) --no-density Leave out the gene density track. --size Figure width in inches. (default: 8.0) --dpi Dots per inch (PNG). (default: 300) --title Figure title.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot depth [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Two bar charts side by side: for each genome, the percentage of its genes covered by 0, 1, 2, ... syntenic blocks of the other genome. The bars up to the peak depth (where 90% of genes are reached, or --quota) are highlighted and the pattern is shown in the title, e.g. 1:2. Saved as <anchors prefix>.depth.pdf:

mcscan3 plot depth grape.poplar.anchors --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=poplar.bed

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --xmax X-axis maximum. --title Title (a \n separates the two lines). --quota Force this pattern, e.g. 1:2. --theme classic (the original figure) or mcscan3. (default: classic) --outfile, -o Output image (mcscan3 theme; default .depth.pdf). --figsize mcscan3 theme: width x height in inches. (default: 6.4x2.6)

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text: Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

docs.text:

mkdir -p plots/depth && cd plots/depth && mcscan3 plot depth ../../core/grape.poplar.anchors --qbed ../../core/grape.bed  --sbed ../../core/poplar.bed && ls

docs.title: mcscan3 plot dot3d
docs.text:
Three-genome dot plot in 3D.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot dot3d [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. A gene of the reference genome A that is syntenic to a gene of B and to a gene of C is one point (A, B, C) in a cube whose axes are the three genomes, laid out chromosome after chromosome in base pairs. Collinear blocks shared by the three genomes become lines in space; a whole-genome duplication in one genome doubles the lines along its axis.

The three walls of the cube carry the pairwise dot plots: the floor A x B, the back wall A x C and the side wall B x C (from <B>.<C>.anchors when given, otherwise the projection of the three-way points). Points are coloured by the reference chromosome:

mcscan3 plot dot3d dmel dyak dpse --suffix lifted.anchors -o flies.dot3d.pdf --html flies.html

--html also writes a self-contained interactive page (drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, hover for gene names, click a chromosome in the legend to hide it). Genomes are named by their BED files (<genome>.bed); anchors files are looked up as <a>.<b>.<suffix> or <b>.<a>.<suffix>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Three genome names, the reference first (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outfile, -o Output figure (PDF, PNG or SVG). (default: dot3d.pdf) --html Also write an interactive HTML page (rotate, zoom, hover). --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix. (default: anchors) --labels Display names of the three genomes, comma-separated. --views Viewing angles elevation,azimuth; several separated by ';' (one panel each). (default: 22,-58) --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. --dpi Dots per inch (PNG). (default: 300) --min-frac Leave out chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction (scaffolds). (default: 0.005) --max-copies Syntenic copies per reference gene and genome. (default: 2) --reorder Order and flip chromosomes of the other genomes after the reference. --title Figure title.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text: Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

mcscan3 plot dot3d grape peach poplar --bed-dir core --anchors-dir core --suffix lifted.anchors  --labels "V. vinifera,P. persica,P. trichocarpa" -o kingdoms/plants.dot3d.pdf --html kingdoms/plants.dot3d.html

docs.title: Method and references
docs.text: New in MCscan3 (no JCVI equivalent). MCscan3: genes syntenic in a reference and two other genomes placed in a cube of the three genome coordinates (base pairs), chromosomes ordered and flipped after the reference, pairwise anchors projected on the walls; static (matplotlib) and self-contained interactive HTML renderings.

docs.title: mcscan3 plot dotplot
docs.text:
Dot plot of anchors or Ks values (mcscan3 plot dotplot; legacy graphics.dotplot).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot dotplot [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Each anchor pair is a dot at (rank of the query gene, rank of the subject gene); chromosome boundaries are drawn as grid lines:

mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.anchors --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed -o grape.peach.pdf

A third column (e.g. Ks) colours the dots when --cmaptext is given (values outside --vmin..--vmax are dropped); a .ks file is converted to anchors first. Blocks can be coloured by class (--colormap: block_id<TAB>class, 1-based ids) or by orientation (--colororientation). --synteny boxes the blocks found by a quick synteny scan. At most --nmax dots are drawn (a random subset). --grid-color is the Set1 colour index of the grid lines (the original's --theme).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file (or .ks file) of gene pairs.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --synteny Run a fast synteny scan and box the blocks. --cmaptext Colour dots by the 3rd column; label of the colour bar. --vmin Minimum value in the colour map. (default: 0) --vmax Maximum value in the colour map. (default: 2) --nmax Maximum number of dots (random subset) (default: 10000; all with --theme mcscan3). --minfont Do not draw labels smaller than this. (default: 4) --colormap block_idclass file: colour blocks by class. --colororientation Colour blocks by orientation. --nosort Do not sort the seqids along the axes. --nosep Do not draw chromosome grid lines. --title Title of the dot plot. --skipempty Skip seqids without matches. --nochpf Do not change the contig names. --nostdpf Do not standardise contig names. --genomenames Axis names as qname_sname, e.g. "Vitis vinifera_Oryza sativa". --grid-color Set1 colour index (0-8) of the grid lines. (default: 2) --outfile, -o Output image (default: .); a .html name makes an interactive dot plot (zoom, pan, genes on hover). --order Subject chromosomes: name, or auto (follow the query, flip reversed ones) [default: auto with --theme mcscan3]. --oi ortholog soi .oi table: grey out low Orthology Index blocks. --oi-cutoff Orthology Index of orthologous blocks. (default: 0.6) --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 9x9) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 90) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... (default: pdf) --font Font: Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Palatino, Schoolbook, Arial. (default: Helvetica) --style Axes background: darkgrid, whitegrid, dark, white, ticks. (default: dark) --diverge Contrasting colour scheme (ColorBrewer diverging name). (default: PiYG) --cmap Matplotlib colour map. (default: copper) --notex Do not use LaTeX (MCscan3 uses LaTeX only when installed). --chinese Render Chinese labels (implies --notex). --seed Random seed when assigning colours. --theme classic (original look) or mcscan3. (default: classic)

docs.text:
Exon structures of genes from GFF (mcscan3 plot gene-structure; legacy graphics.glyph gff).

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot gene-structure [OPTIONS] GFFILES...

docs.title: Description

Each GFF file holds one gene; its mRNA is drawn as a thin bar and its CDS parts as boxes, one gene per row on a common scale, to exons.pdf:

docs.title: mcscan3 plot histogram
docs.text:
Histogram of numbers (mcscan3 plot histogram; legacy graphics.histogram).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot histogram [OPTIONS] NUMBERFILES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Input files hold one number per line (--col picks another whitespace-separated column, --skip skips header lines). Only values within --vmin..--vmax are counted; summary statistics go to stderr:

mcscan3 plot histogram ks.values --vmax=3               # ks.values.pdf
mcscan3 plot histogram ks.values --vmax=3 --ascii       # text histogram on stderr
mcscan3 plot histogram a.txt b.txt --tags=A,B --facet   # a_b.pdf, one panel per file

--base=2|10 bins by powers of the base (log axis). --quick plots a file of value<TAB>count pairs as bars with the counts written above them.

The original drew figures with R/ggplot2; MCscan3 draws the same kind of figure with matplotlib (no R needed), so figures differ in look but not in content. The text mode is unchanged.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description NUMBERFILES Files with one number per line.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --skip Skip the first several lines. (default: 0) --col Use the n-th column (0-based). (default: 0) --vmin Minimum value, inclusive. (default: 0) --vmax Maximum value, inclusive (default: data maximum). --bins Number of bins. (default: 20) --xlabel Label on the X-axis. (default: value) --title Title (default: first file name). --tags Comma-separated names of the input files. --ascii Print a text histogram (stderr) instead of a figure. --base Logarithmic bins with base 2 or 10; 0 to disable. (default: 0) --facet One panel per input file. --fill Bar colour. (default: white) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --quick Input is value<TAB>count (already binned). --noprintstats With --quick: no statistics on the plot. --plain Text mode: print the title and no rich markup (fix).

docs.title: mcscan3 plot karyotype
docs.text:
Macrosynteny between genomes drawn as chromosome tracks (mcscan3 plot karyotype; legacy graphics.karyotype).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot karyotype [OPTIONS] SEQIDSFILE LAYOUTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
seqids lists the chromosomes of each track, one track per line (comma-separated; a trailing - draws a chromosome reversed; # starts a comment). The layout file describes each track, then the edges (syntenic wedges from .simple block files):

# y, xstart, xend, rotation, color, label, va, bed[, label_va]
.6, .1, .4, 0, m, Grape, top, grape.bed, center
.4, .3, .6, 60, k, Athaliana, top, athaliana.bed, center
# edges
e, 0, 1, athaliana.grape.4x1.simple[, samearc]

mcscan3 plot karyotype seqids layout -o karyotype.pdf

Chromosome lengths are in genes (--basepair: base pairs). Track colours are random when not given (--seed). --shadestyle curve or line, --chrstyle auto, rect or roundrect, --keep-chrlabels keeps full names in the circles, --nocircles drops them.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SEQIDSFILE Chromosomes of each track, one track per line, comma-separated (not with --genomes). LAYOUTFILE Track layout, then e, i, j, blocks.simple edge lines (not with --genomes).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outfile, -o Output image. (default: karyotype.pdf) --basepair Use base-pair positions instead of gene ranks. --keep-chrlabels Keep full chromosome labels. --nocircles Do not draw chromosome circles. --shadestyle Wedges: curve or line. (default: curve) --chrstyle Chromosomes: auto, rect or roundrect. (default: auto) --genomes Genomes top to bottom, comma-separated: layout made automatically. --bed-dir With --genomes: directory of .bed. (default: .) --anchors-dir With --genomes: directory of . anchors. (default: .) --anchors-suffix With --genomes: anchors file suffix. (default: anchors) --min-frac With --genomes: drop chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction. (default: 0.005) --auto-order Order and flip chromosomes to follow the track above (default: on with --genomes). --color-by Ribbon colours: none, chr (first track's chromosome), car (--cars) or labels (--labels) [default: chr with --theme mcscan3, else none]. --cars CARs TSV from ancestral genomes (for --color-by car). --families Gene families used for the CARs (for --color-by car). --labels genelabel table (for --color-by labels). --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 8x7) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 300) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... (default: pdf) --font Font: Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Palatino, Schoolbook, Arial. (default: Helvetica) --style Axes background: darkgrid, whitegrid, dark, white, ticks. (default: darkgrid) --diverge Contrasting colour scheme (ColorBrewer diverging name). (default: PiYG) --cmap Matplotlib colour map. (default: jet) --notex Do not use LaTeX (MCscan3 uses LaTeX only when installed). --chinese Render Chinese labels (implies --notex). --seed Random seed when assigning colours. --theme classic (original look) or mcscan3. docs.title: mcscan3 plot ks
docs.text:
Ks distribution figures (mcscan3 plot ks, mcscan3 ks multireport, ks report --pdf).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot ks [OPTIONS] KSFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The distribution of Nei-Gojobori Ks values (within --vmin..--vmax) is drawn as the percentage of gene pairs per bin, as a line with markers (--fill: a filled area; --kde: a smoothed curve):

mcscan3 plot ks grape.peach.ks                  # Ks_plot.pdf
mcscan3 ks multireport ks.layout -o Ks_plot.png # several Ks files in one figure

--fit adds a log-normal mixture of --components peaks fitted to log(Ks), with the peak positions labelled. The original shelled out to an external gmm-bic program for the fit; MCscan3 fits the mixture itself (expectation-maximisation), so no extra program is needed.

The multireport layout file lists Ks file, ncomponents, label, color, marker per line (# lines are comments); a missing colour or marker is assigned at random (--seed). If the layout file does not exist, a template listing the *.ks files below the current directory is written first.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description KSFILE Ks file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outfile, -o Output figure. (default: Ks_plot.pdf) --components Number of components (peaks) for --fit. (default: 1) --vmin Minimum value, inclusive. (default: 0.0) --vmax Maximum value, inclusive. (default: 3.0) --bins Number of histogram bins. (default: 60) --fit Add a fitted log-normal mixture (peaks labelled). --kde Smooth the distribution (Gaussian KDE). --legendp Legend position (matplotlib loc). (default: upper right) --fill Draw the distribution as a filled area. --title Title of the plot. (default: *Ks* distribution) --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 5x5) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 300) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... (default: pdf) --font Font: Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Palatino, Schoolbook, Arial. (default: Helvetica) --style Axes background: darkgrid, whitegrid, dark, white, ticks. docs.title: mcscan3 plot locus
docs.text:
Microsynteny of one locus across genomes, in several styles.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot locus [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Give a gene (--gene) or region (--region chr:start-end) of the reference genome (the first one named) and the anchors between the reference and every other genome; the syntenic regions are found automatically (the largest runs of anchor partners, up to --copies per genome, for duplicated genomes; --copies scer=2 for one genome) and drawn in one of four styles:

ribbons gene arrows on one track per region, homologous genes joined by ribbons between neighbouring tracks; arrows tracks aligned on the focal gene (base pairs from it, regions flipped so that it points the same way), homologs in one colour per reference gene; matrix one row per region and one column per reference gene: kept in the same orientation, inverted or missing (compact for many genomes); dots a local dot plot per region (reference genes against the region's genes).

Several styles at once (--style ribbons,matrix or all) write one figure each:

mcscan3 plot locus dmel dsim dyak dpse agam --gene rna-NM_079260.3 --suffix lifted.anchors \
    --style all -o adh

Colours (--color-by): homolog (one colour per reference gene, default), strand or focal (only the focal gene and its homologs). --layout middle puts the reference in the middle of the ribbons tracks (the two copies of a duplicated genome on either side), --scale bp draws ribbons tracks to scale (default: genes evenly spaced), --highlight marks more genes, --gene-labels names the reference genes.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names, the reference first (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --gene Focal gene of the reference: ID or symbol (with --names). --region Or a region of the reference, chr:start-end. --outfile, -o Output prefix: .

docs.title: mcscan3 plot microsynteny
docs.text:
Local synteny of gene-level tracks (mcscan3 plot microsynteny; legacy graphics.synteny).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot microsynteny [OPTIONS] BLOCKSFILE BEDFILE LAYOUTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Draws the regions of an MCscan blocks file (one column per track, from synteny mcscan) as gene tracks, with wedges between syntenic genes:

mcscan3 plot microsynteny micro.blocks all.bed micro.layout

The layout file has one line per track, x, y, rotation, ha, va, color[, ratio[, label[, fontsize]]] (a leading * hides the track), then e, i, j[, color[, samearc]] lines for the wedges between tracks i and j. ha is left, right, leftalign, rightalign, center or empty; va is top, bottom, center or empty. Saved as <blocks prefix>.<format>.

Options: --switch renames seqids (two columns); --tree draws trees below the tracks; --extra adds features (BED, e.g. repeats); --genelabels/--genelabelsize label genes; --glyphstyle box or arrow; --glyphcolor orientation or orthogroup; --scalebar.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLOCKSFILE MCscan blocks file (one column per track). BEDFILE BED of all genes in the blocks. LAYOUTFILE Layout: one line per track, then e, i, j wedge lines.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --switch Rename seqids with this two-column file. --tree Trees to display below the tracks. --extra Extra features (BED), e.g. repeats. --genelabels Label only these genes (comma-separated). --genelabelsize Gene label font size (0: no labels). (default: 0) --genelabelrotation Gene label angle (anti-clockwise). (default: 25) --scalebar Add a scale bar. --vpad Gap between a track's name and its coordinates (axes units). (default: 0.015) --glyphstyle Gene glyphs: box or arrow. (default: box) --glyphcolor Colour genes by orientation or orthogroup. (default: orientation) --shadestyle Wedges: curve or line. (default: curve) --outputprefix Prefix of the output file. --noprune Keep extra features under 0.1% of the region. --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 8x7) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 300) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... (default: pdf) --font Font: Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Palatino, Schoolbook, Arial. (default: Helvetica) --style Axes background: darkgrid, whitegrid, dark, white, ticks. (default: darkgrid) --diverge Contrasting colour scheme (ColorBrewer diverging name). (default: PiYG) --cmap Matplotlib colour map. docs.title: mcscan3 plot phylo
docs.text:
Tree figures.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot phylo [OPTIONS] TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: publication tree figures without a separate tree package (the features people reach for ete3 or iTOL for), in the MCscan3 house style:

  • rectangular (phylogram or --cladogram) or --layout circular trees, rooted on --outgroup or at the midpoint (--midpoint), ladderized;
  • support values from the node labels (--min-support: only those below), or pies of the share (--pies: node labels such as gCF 95/62 give the second number);
  • clades shaded and labelled (--highlight "NAME1,NAME2=label": the smallest clade holding the names) and tips coloured by group (--groups FILE: tipgroup);
  • a table aligned to the tips (--data FILE, tip in the first column): numeric columns drawn as a heatmap (--data-style heatmap) or stacked bars (stacked);
  • a tanglegram against a second tree (--tangle OTHER.nwk), with the Robinson-Foulds distance:
    • mcscan3 plot phylo species.nwk --outgroup scer --highlight "dmel,agam=Diptera" --data busco.tsv -o tree

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description TREE Newick tree.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --outgroup Outgroup tip(s) to root on (repeatable). (default: []) --midpoint Root at the midpoint. --layout rect or circular. (default: rect) --cladogram Ignore branch lengths. --min-support Show support values only below this. --pies Pies from node labels (last number, e.g. gCF of 95/62). --highlight Shade a clade: 'TIP1,TIP2=label' (repeatable). (default: []) --groups tipgroup: tip label colours. --data Table aligned to the tips (tip in the first column). --data-style heatmap or stacked. (default: heatmap) --tangle Second tree: draw a tanglegram. --italic Italic tip labels (species names). --title Figure title. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 plot ribbon
docs.text:
Shared identity between aligned chromosomes as ribbons (mcscan3 plot ribbon; legacy graphics.ribbon).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot ribbon [OPTIONS] BLOCKSFILE BEDFILE LAYOUTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Each track is a chromosome range; ribbons join the aligned intervals of a blocks file (one column per track; the intervals are BED features):

mcscan3 plot ribbon alignment.blocks alignment.bed ribbon.layout --reorient=F,R

The layout has one line per track, then e, i, j edge lines:

# x, y, rotation, ha, va, color, ratio, label, chrmName, rStart, rEnd, chrmMax
0.5, 0.6, 0, top, center, g, 1, Spp 1 Chrm 8, Chromosome_08, 2000000, 2108098, 2108098

--reorient flips tracks (F/R per track). --paintbystrand colours ribbons by relative orientation (--strandcolors), --paintbyscore sets their transparency from the BED score (0-100; --scalealpha rescales 50-100 to 0.1-0.9). --annotations and --extra-annotations draw feature tracks above and below each chromosome (BED columns 7-9: colour, offset and height multipliers); --annotation-boxes frames regions. Saved as <blocks prefix>.<format> (or --outfile).

The original crashed without --reorient, with --annotations, --scalebar or --tree, and with 11-column layout lines (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.13, A.22).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLOCKSFILE Alignment blocks file (one column per track). BEDFILE BED of the aligned intervals. LAYOUTFILE Layout: one line per track, then e, i, j edge lines.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outfile Output prefix (default: blocks prefix). --annotations Feature annotations (BED; col 7-9: colour, offset, height). --extra-annotations Extra annotations, below the chromosome. --annotation-boxes Regions to frame (BED; col 7: colour). --noprune Keep annotations under 0.1% of the region. --reorient F or R per track, comma-separated (R flips the track). --tree Trees to display below the tracks. --scalebar Add a scale bar. --paintbyscore Ribbon transparency from the BED score (0-100). --paintbystrand Ribbon colour by relative orientation. --plothits Also draw the ribbon intervals on the tracks. --strandcolors Colours of forward,inverted ribbons. --annotcolor Colour of the annotation track. (default: g) --scalealpha Rescale score alpha from 50-100 to 0.1-0.9. --transparent Transparent background. --noline No outline on ribbons. --shadestyle Ribbons: curve or line. (default: curve) --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 20x20) --dpi Physical dot density (dots per inch). (default: 300) --format Image format: pdf, png, svg, eps, ps, ... (default: pdf) --font Font: Helvetica, Liberation Sans, Palatino, Schoolbook, Arial. (default: Helvetica) --style Axes background: darkgrid, whitegrid, dark, white, ticks. docs.title: mcscan3 plot riparian
docs.text:
Riparian (braid) plot of synteny across several genomes.

Group plot · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot riparian [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the riparian plots of GENESPACE (Lovell et al. 2022, eLife). Each genome is a row of chromosomes, with lengths in genes (--basepair: base pairs). Syntenic blocks between neighbouring rows are drawn as braids, coloured by the reference chromosome they descend from. The colours spread from the reference row to the others through the blocks:

mcscan3 plot riparian grape peach poplar --ref grape -o riparian.pdf

Genomes are named by their BED files (<genome>.bed). Anchors files between neighbouring genomes are looked up as in pan genes (<a>.<b>.anchors or <b>.<a>.anchors). Braids that cannot be traced to a reference chromosome are grey. Small scaffolds (--min-frac) are left out and the other genomes' chromosomes are ordered and flipped to follow their neighbour (--no-reorder keeps the natural order).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genome names, top to bottom (.bed each).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference genome: braids are coloured by its chromosomes. --outfile, -o Output figure. (default: riparian.pdf) --bed-dir Directory of the BED files. (default: .) --anchors-dir Directory of the anchors files. (default: .) --suffix Anchors file suffix. (default: anchors) --basepair Chromosome lengths in base pairs, not genes. --figsize Figure size widthxheight in inches. (default: 10x6) --dpi Dots per inch (PNG). (default: 300) --min-frac Leave out chromosomes with fewer genes than this fraction (scaffolds). (default: 0.005) --reorder Order and flip chromosomes after the neighbouring genome. --min-block Do not draw blocks with fewer anchors. (default: 10) --labels Display names, comma-separated (... for italics). --title Figure title.

docs.title: mcscan3 plot tree
docs.text:
Plot a Newick tree (mcscan3 plot tree; legacy graphics.tree).

Group plot · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 plot tree [OPTIONS] NEWICK

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The tree is rerooted at the midpoint (or --outgroup; --noreroot keeps the given root) and drawn with leaf names, node support and a scale bar, to <tree prefix>.<format>:

mcscan3 plot tree tree.nwk --outgroup=rice

Annotations: --leafinfo (CSV name,color,new_name) recolours or renames leaves; --groups names the leaf colour groups to the right of the tree; --wgdinfo (CSV node,divergence,name,color,style) marks whole-genome duplications; --geoscale draws a geological time scale (branch lengths in 100 million years; 95% HPD intervals in the Newick are drawn as bars); --gffdir draws each gene's exon structure (<gene>.gff) and --sizes its protein length. Needs the phylo extra (ete4).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description NEWICK Newick tree file (or demo).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outgroup Outgroup taxa to root on, comma-separated. --noreroot Keep the root of the input tree. --rmargin Blank margin to the right. (default: 0.2) --gffdir Directory of .gff files: draw exon structures. --sizes FASTA or sizes file: show protein lengths. --sh, --SH SH test p-value to print. --leafcolor Font colour of the leaves. (default: k) --leaffont Font size of the leaves. (default: 12) --leafinfo CSV of leaves: name,color,new_name. --scutoff Show node support above this value (0-100). docs.title: mcscan3 prep bed-uniq
docs.text:
Remove overlapping BED features (mcscan3 prep bed-uniq; legacy formats.bed uniq).

Group prep · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 prep bed-uniq [OPTIONS] BEDFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Chooses the set of non-overlapping features with the largest total weight (weighted interval chaining). The weight is the feature span (--mode span, default), the BED score (--mode score) or the sequence length from a --sizes file. docs.title: mcscan3 prep fasta-format
docs.text:
Reformat FASTA and clean up sequence IDs (mcscan3 prep fasta-format; legacy formats.fasta format).

Group prep · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 prep fasta-format [OPTIONS] INFASTA OUTFASTA

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Used in the MCscan tutorial to normalise CDS/protein files before alignment:

mcscan3 prep fasta-format grape.cds.fa.gz grape.cds

Records are re-written with Biopython (60 columns per line). The ID is the first word of the header unless changed by the options; the rest of the header is kept unless --nodesc.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description INFASTA Input FASTA (may be .gz). OUTFASTA Output FASTA.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --pairs Add trailing /1 and /2 for interleaved pairs. --sequential Sequential IDs: replace, prefix or suffix. --sequentialoffset Sequential IDs start at. (default: 0) --pad0 Zero-pad sequential IDs to this width. (default: 0) --gb For GenBank IDs, keep the accession. --sep Split the header by this string ... --index ... and use the i-th field as ID. (default: 0) --noversion Remove the trailing .version. --prefix Prepend to IDs. --suffix Append to IDs. --template template=a dir=x library=m -> m-a/x. --switch Two-column file mapping old to new IDs. --annotation Two-column file with descriptions. --ids Write the ID conversion table here. --upper Upper-case sequences. --nodesc Drop the description after the ID. --minlength Minimum sequence length to keep. (default: 0) --chrom-names IDs from the chromosome names of the descriptions (NC_001133.9 -> chrI).
