docs.title: mcscan3 prep genome
docs.text:
Longest-isoform BED, CDS and protein from a genome GFF3 + FASTA.

Group prep · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 prep genome [OPTIONS] GFF FASTA

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. One step from a raw genome annotation to the MCscan inputs: for every gene, the transcript with the longest coding sequence is kept (ties: the first listed); its CDS is spliced from the genome (reverse-complemented on the minus strand, honouring the phase of the first CDS part) and translated. Writes <prefix>.bed, <prefix>.cds and <prefix>.pep:

mcscan3 prep genome grape.gff3.gz grape.dna.fa.gz --prefix grape

IDs are cleaned: prefixes such as transcript: or gene: (Ensembl) are removed. --name gene names each record by its gene instead of its transcript. Transcripts without a CDS (non-coding) are skipped, as are genes whose CDS is shorter than --min-length codons. The GFF and FASTA may be gzip-compressed.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF Genome annotation (GFF3, may be .gz). FASTA Genome sequence (FASTA, may be .gz).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -p, -o Output prefix: .bed, .cds, .pep. --name Name records by transcript or gene. (default: transcript) --min-length Skip genes with a CDS shorter than this (codons). (default: 0) --table Genetic code (NCBI translation table). (default: 1) --types GFF feature types of transcripts. (default: mRNA,transcript) --chrom-names Name chromosomes as in the FASTA descriptions (NC_001133.9 -> chrI). --symbols Also write .names.tsv: gene symbols of the GFF, for figures.

docs.title: mcscan3 prep gff2bed
docs.text:
Convert GFF features to BED (mcscan3 prep gff2bed; legacy formats.gff bed).

Group prep · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 prep gff2bed [OPTIONS] GFF_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Typical MCscan preparation keeps one transcript per gene:

mcscan3 prep gff2bed --type=mRNA --key=transcript_id --primary-only grape.gff3.gz -o grape.bed

primary_only keeps the first transcript listed for each gene (original behaviour). longest (MCscan3 addition) instead keeps the transcript with the longest total CDS length (the transcript span if it has no CDS); ties keep the first listed.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GFF_FILE GFF3/GFF2 file (may be .gz).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --type Feature types, comma-separated; all for all. (default: gene) --key Attribute used as the BED name. (default: ID) --accn Use this fixed name in column 4. --source Only these GFF sources (comma-separated). --span Use the feature span as the score. --score-attrib Attribute used as the score. --append-source Prefix the name with the GFF source. --append-ftype Prefix the name with the feature type. --append-attrib Append this attribute to the name. --nosort Keep GFF order instead of sorting. --primary-only Keep the first transcript per gene. --longest Keep the transcript with the longest CDS per gene. --parent-key Attribute grouping transcripts into genes. (default: Parent) --human-chr Only 1-22,X,Y,MT; add chr prefix. --ensembl-cds Name CDS as transcript_name.exon_number. --outfile, -o Output file (default: stdout). (default: stdout)

docs.text:

docs.title: mcscan3 quota align
docs.text:
Quota alignment (mcscan3 quota align; legacy compara.quota).

Group quota · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 quota align [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Selects the set of synteny blocks with the largest total score such that every gene of genome X is covered by at most a blocks and every gene of genome Y by at most b blocks (--quota=a:b), by 0/1 integer programming (Tang et al., BMC Bioinformatics 2011). Blocks may overlap by up to --Nm genes. Writes the selected block ids to <anchors prefix>.<a>x<b> and, with --screen, the selected blocks to <anchors prefix>.<a>x<b>.anchors:

mcscan3 quota align grape.poplar.anchors --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=poplar.bed --quota=1:2 --screen

For a 1:2 pattern (one grape region, two poplar regions after the Salicoid WGD) use 1:2.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --quota Blocks per gene allowed in genome X:genome Y, e.g. 1:2. (default: 1:1) --nm Tolerated overlap between two blocks (genes). (default: 10) --self Self comparison (screening paralogous blocks). --verbose Show verbose solver output. --screen Also write the screened anchors file. --solver MIP solver: ortools (default), highs, scip, glpk. (default: ortools)

docs.text:

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold contacts
docs.text:
Hi-C contacts between and within contigs.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold contacts [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Read pairs come from a 4DN .pairs file (plain or gzip), from SAM/BAM (one line per pair is used: the first read, with its mate's position; samtools reads BAM), or straight from Hi-C reads, mapped here with bwa mem -5SP (the Hi-C mode of BWA, Li H 2013, arXiv:1303.3997). Pairs with a mapping quality below --min-mapq are dropped. Positions are binned (--resolution, 1 kb by default) and identical bin pairs counted, so a dataset of a hundred million pairs becomes a sparse matrix of a few million cells, kept as .npz.

The matrix gives every later step its numbers: links between contigs (for grouping), their positions (for ordering and orientation), contacts within contigs (for the distance-decay law and for finding misjoins), and the contact map figures. Restriction sites per contig (--enzyme, e.g. GATC for MboI/DpnII, AAGCTT for HindIII, GATC,GANTC for Arima) normalise link counts (cf. Zhang X et al. 2019, Nat Plants 5:833):

mcscan3 scaffold contacts contigs.fa --pairs hic.pairs.gz -o asm
mcscan3 scaffold contacts contigs.fa --reads hic_R1.fq.gz --reads hic_R2.fq.gz --enzyme GATC -o asm

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTIGS Contigs (FASTA) the Hi-C reads were mapped to.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --pairs Hi-C pairs (4DN .pairs, gzip ok). --bam Hi-C reads mapped to the contigs (SAM/BAM, e.g. bwa mem -5SP). --reads Hi-C reads (R1 and R2), mapped here with bwa. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --resolution Bin size (bp). (default: 1000) --enzyme Restriction motif(s), e.g. GATC or GATC,GANTC. --min-mapq Least mapping quality of both reads (SAM/BAM). (default: 1) --threads Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold hic
docs.text:
Hi-C scaffolding of contigs into chromosomes, haplotype- and allele-aware.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold hic [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3; the steps follow ALLHiC (Zhang X et al. 2019, Nat Plants 5:833: prune allelic links, partition, rescue, optimise, build), with ideas of HapHiC (Zeng X et al. 2024, Nat Plants), YaHS (Zhou C et al. 2023, Bioinformatics 39:btac808) and 3D-DNA (Dudchenko O et al. 2017, Science 356:92), reimplemented:

  1. break (--break): within every contig, the contacts spanning each position at short range are counted; where they fall below break_ratio of the contig's median (away from the ends), the contig is a misjoin and is cut there.
  2. prune: links between allelic contigs (alleles.py) are removed, and of the links from a contig to several alleles of one region only the strongest is kept (the others come from reads mapped to the wrong allele).
  3. partition: contigs of at least min_length are clustered by average link density (links per restriction site, or per kb, of both) into groups clusters (chromosomes x ploidy for haplotype-resolved assemblies), never joining clusters that share allelic sequence (cannot-link); then every contig is moved to the group it links to most densely, as long as that adds no allele to the group, until nothing moves. With a reference (place), contigs first go to their reference chromosome and each chromosome is split into ploidy haplotypes the same way.
  4. rescue: shorter and unassigned contigs join the group they link to most densely, when that group clearly beats the next (rescue_ratio) and holds none of their alleles.
  5. order and orient: contact probability falls with distance as d^-a, so the layout that maximises the likelihood of the links minimises the sum of log distances of all links. The links of every contig pair are compressed, per relative orientation, into a few weighted distance quantiles, so a layout is scored in microseconds. A greedy join of contig ends (strongest close links first) gives the start; a local search over flips, moves and segment reversals (batched evaluation of all candidates of a contig) improves it to a local optimum. With a reference, its order is the start.

Outputs <prefix>.agp and <prefix>.fa (scaffolds, 100 N gaps), <prefix>.groups.tsv (contig pieces with group, order, orientation) and statistics on stderr:

mcscan3 scaffold hic contigs.fa --pairs hic.pairs.gz --groups 40 --alleles auto -o asm
mcscan3 scaffold hic contigs.fa --bam hic.bam --ref mono.fa --ploidy 8 -o sugarcane

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTIGS Contigs (FASTA).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --contacts Contacts of scaffold contacts (.npz). --pairs Hi-C pairs (4DN .pairs, gzip ok). --bam Hi-C reads mapped to the contigs (SAM/BAM). --reads Hi-C reads (R1 and R2), mapped here with bwa. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --groups Number of groups: chromosomes x ploidy (without --ref). --ref Reference: contigs grouped by its chromosomes, Hi-C splits haplotypes. --ploidy Haplotypes per chromosome (with --ref, and to name homologs). (default: 1) --alleles Allele table: auto (self-alignment when --ploidy > 1), none, or a file. (default: auto) --break Cut misjoined contigs where Hi-C contacts drop. --min-length Contigs shorter than this are only rescued. (default: 20000) --resolution Bin size (bp) when reading pairs. (default: 1000) --enzyme Restriction motif(s) for normalisation. --min-mapq Least mapping quality (SAM/BAM). (default: 1) --gap Ns between joined pieces. (default: 100) --threads Threads (default: all). --plot Draw the contact map of the result.

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold hicmap
docs.text:
Hi-C contact maps of an assembly.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold hicmap [OPTIONS] CONTACTS_ AGP

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. The contacts of scaffold contacts (in contig coordinates) are lifted through an AGP (scaffold hic/ref/map output, or any AGP of the contigs) onto scaffold coordinates and binned into a square map, whole genome or selected scaffolds, drawn on a log scale with scaffold borders. A correct assembly shows strong squares along the diagonal (chromosomes) with contacts fading away from it; misjoins, inversions and wrongly placed contigs show as off-diagonal blocks and bow ties:

mcscan3 scaffold hicmap asm.contacts.npz asm.agp -o asm.map --format png
mcscan3 scaffold hicmap asm.contacts.npz asm.agp --scaffold chr1_hap1 --scaffold chr1_hap2 -o chr1

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold map
docs.text:
Scaffolding with genetic maps.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold map [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after Chromonomer (Catchen J et al. 2020, G3 10:4115: markers anchor, split and order scaffolds) and ALLMAPS (Tang H et al. 2015, Genome Biol 16:3: several maps at once, scaffold order and orientation maximising the markers in map order), reimplemented:

  1. markers: per map a table of contig, position (bp), linkage group and cM (tab or comma separated, header optional); each map has a weight (--map maps/f2.tsv:2). Linkage-group names of later maps are matched to those of the first (most markers x weight) by the contigs they share, and their direction turned to agree with it.
  2. split: along every contig, markers fall into runs of one linkage group; where two runs of at least min_markers markers of different groups meet, the contig is cut between them (where at least min_maps maps agree).
  3. assign and order: every piece goes to the group with most (weighted) markers; within a group, pieces start in the order of their weighted median map position and are oriented by the trend of cM along them.
  4. optimise: a local search over flips, moves and segment reversals maximises the sum over maps (times weight) of the longest run of markers in map order (increasing or decreasing), the ALLMAPS objective, so a few misplaced markers do not move a piece.

Writes AGP and FASTA, <prefix>.markers.tsv (every marker with its scaffold position) and a summary per group (markers placed, Spearman rho of physical vs genetic position per map):

mcscan3 scaffold map contigs.fa --map f2.tsv --map ril.tsv:2 -o asm

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --map Markers: contig, position, linkage group, cM; path:weight; repeat. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --min-markers Markers of a linkage group needed on each side of a cut. (default: 3) --min-maps Maps that must agree on a cut. (default: 1) --format Image format of the marker plot. (default: png)

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold ref
docs.text:
Reference-guided correction and scaffolding of contigs.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold ref [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the approach of RagTag (Alonge M et al. 2022, Genome Biol 23:258: correct, then order and orient by alignment to a related genome, then merge solutions), reimplemented with these differences:

  • evidence from several references at once: every reference adds weighted adjacencies between contig ends to one scaffold graph (in a single step), and the scaffolds are its best paths (strongest adjacencies first, no cycles), so references that disagree are outvoted rather than run one after another; other evidence (Hi-C join scores) enters the same graph;
  • correction by collinear chains: alignments of a contig are chained (same chromosome and strand, collinear within max_gap); a contig is cut between two chains of at least min_chain bp that go to different chromosomes or far-apart places, at the middle of the unaligned stretch between them, and only where at least min_refs references agree (so a rearrangement of one reference does not break a correct contig);
  • haplotigs: contigs whose reference span lies inside a longer contig's span are allelic copies and are left unplaced (--keep-contained places them as alternate scaffolds);
  • gaps are the reference distance between neighbours (100 N when unknown or overlapping).

Alignment by minimap2 (Li H 2018, Bioinformatics 34:3094):

mcscan3 scaffold ref contigs.fa --ref close.fa --ref other.fa:0.5 -o asm --correct

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTIGS Contigs (FASTA).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference FASTA, optionally path:weight; repeat. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --correct Cut misjoins supported by the alignments. --min-refs References that must agree on a cut. (default: 1) --preset minimap2 preset: asm5, asm10 or asm20. (default: asm10) --keep-contained Place haplotigs inside other contigs too. --threads Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold review
docs.text:
Interactive Hi-C contact map for reviewing and curating an assembly.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold review [OPTIONS] CONTACTS_ AGP

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: one self-contained HTML page (contacts embedded as binary arrays, map drawn on a <canvas>; no server, no install). The .assembly layout format follows Dudchenko O et al. 2018, bioRxiv 254797 (see also Durand NC et al. 2016, Cell Syst 3:99):

  • the contact map of the scaffolds, with scaffold (blue) and contig piece (green) outlines; scroll to zoom, drag to pan, hover for positions and counts, a slider for the colour range;
  • curation: click a piece to select it (shift-click for a range), then invert (I), move (M, then click where it goes), cut (C, then click where to cut), mark as debris (D), split/join scaffolds at a piece boundary (B, then click), undo (Z); every edit redraws the map from the new layout at once;
  • export of the curated assembly as AGP and as an .assembly layout; scaffold apply turns either back into AGP and FASTA. .assembly layouts from other Hi-C review tools load here too:
mcscan3 scaffold review asm.contacts.npz asm.agp -o asm.review.html
mcscan3 scaffold apply contigs.fa asm.review.assembly -o asm.curated

docs.title: mcscan3 scaffold run
docs.text:
Scaffolding with all evidence at once: references, genetic maps and Hi-C.

Group scaffold · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 scaffold run [OPTIONS] CONTIGS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each kind of evidence proposes cuts (misjoins) and adjacencies between contig ends:

  • references: collinear-chain misjoins and neighbours along every reference chromosome (scaffold ref);
  • genetic maps: linkage-group switches and neighbours in the map order (scaffold map); joins to pieces the maps cannot orient count half;
  • Hi-C: contact-drop misjoins (scaffold hic) and, for every contig end, its best partner by close contacts when the choice is mutual, weighted by how clearly it beats the second best.

All cuts are made (nearby cuts of different sources merged), all adjacencies go into one scaffold graph with their weights (--ref x.fa:w, --map m.tsv:w, --hic-weight), and the scaffolds are its best paths (strongest first, no cycles). Adjacencies proposed but not used with at least half the weight of the chosen join are reported as conflicts, with their sources:

mcscan3 scaffold run contigs.fa --ref close.fa --map f2.tsv --pairs hic.pairs.gz -o asm

Writes AGP, FASTA, <prefix>.joins.tsv (every join and the sources supporting it) and <prefix>.conflicts.tsv.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CONTIGS Contigs (FASTA).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref Reference FASTA, optionally path:weight; repeat. --map Genetic map markers, optionally path:weight; repeat. --contacts Hi-C contacts (.npz). --pairs Hi-C pairs (4DN .pairs). --bam Hi-C reads mapped to the contigs (SAM/BAM). --hic-weight Weight of Hi-C joins. (default: 1.0) --groups Chromosomes, for the Hi-C layout (default: from --ref or --map). --prefix, -o Output prefix. --correct Cut misjoins. --min-refs References that must agree on a cut. (default: 1) --preset minimap2 preset. (default: asm10) --threads Threads (default: all).

docs.title: mcscan3 subgenome assign
docs.text:
Assign the chromosomes of a polyploid to subgenomes by homology to progenitors.

Group subgenome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 subgenome assign [OPTIONS] POLY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. In an allopolyploid each subgenome descends from a different parent, so its genes are closest to the genes of that parent's living relative (the progenitor-like diploid). Given anchors between the polyploid and each progenitor-like genome (e.g. ortholog run):

  1. gene votes: every polyploid gene with a syntenic partner votes for the progenitor whose partner is closest: the highest anchor score (third column of the anchors, a BLAST score), or the lowest Ks when --ks NAME=FILE gives the pairs' Ks (wgd ksd TSV, gene1, gene2, ks columns). Votes closer than --margin (relative score difference) abstain;
  2. segments: votes are smoothed along each chromosome (sliding majority, --smooth genes each side) and runs shorter than --min-run genes are merged, as in ancestral karyotype;
  3. chromosomes: each chromosome gets the subgenome of most of its genes, with the share as a confidence (homoeologous exchanges show as mixed chromosomes):
mcscan3 subgenome assign bnapus --bed-dir data --progenitor brapa=bnapus.brapa.anchors \
    --progenitor bole=bnapus.bole.anchors -o bnapus

Writes <prefix>.genes.tsv (gene, chromosome, vote, scores), <prefix>.segments.tsv, <prefix>.chromosomes.tsv (chromosome, subgenome, share, votes per progenitor) and the figure <prefix>.<format>: the polyploid's chromosomes coloured by subgenome.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description POLY Polyploid genome name (.bed in --bed-dir).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --progenitor NAME=ANCHORS: anchors between the polyploid and a progenitor-like genome. --bed-dir Directory of .bed. (default: .) --prefix, -o Output prefix. --ks NAME=FILE: Ks of the pairs (wgd ksd TSV) instead of scores. --margin Votes with a smaller relative score gap abstain. (default: 0.02) --smooth Sliding-majority window (genes each side). (default: 15) --min-run Shortest segment (genes; at least 1% of a chromosome). (default: 40) --min-frac Leave out sequences with fewer genes than this fraction (0: keep all scaffolds). (default: 0.005) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 subgenome fractionation
docs.text:
Biased fractionation of a polyploid against an unduplicated relative.

Group subgenome · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 subgenome fractionation [OPTIONS] ANCHORS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the analyses of Thomas et al. (2006), Schnable et al. (2011, PNAS, maize) and Cheng et al. (2012, PLoS ONE, Brassica rapa). After a polyploidy, duplicated genes are lost (fractionated). When one parental subgenome keeps more genes than the other, fractionation is biased: a sign of allopolyploidy and of subgenome dominance.

Input: anchors between a reference genome that did not share the polyploidy (ref) and the polyploid (poly), e.g. from ortholog run --quota 1:2 for a tetraploid. Each block of the polyploid covers an interval of the reference:

  1. retention of a block: the share of reference genes in its interval that have a partner in the block (the genes kept by that copy);
  2. ranks: at every reference gene, the covering blocks (at most --copies) are ranked by retention: LF (least fractionated), MF1, MF2...;
  3. windows: the retention of each rank along every reference chromosome (--window reference genes, centred on each gene with any copy);
  4. bias test: ranking by retention alone makes LF look better than MF even without bias. The null keeps every reference gene's number of kept copies but shuffles which copies keep them (--permutations), and re-ranks. The p-value is the share of shuffles whose LF - MF1 retention difference is at least the observed one:
mcscan3 subgenome fractionation ath.brapa.anchors --ref-bed ath.bed --poly-bed brapa.bed --copies 3 -o brapa

Writes <prefix>.genes.tsv (reference gene, then the polyploid gene or . for each rank), <prefix>.blocks.tsv (block, polyploid and reference intervals, retention, majority rank), <prefix>.windows.tsv and the figure <prefix>.<format>; prints the summary.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORS Anchors between the reference and the polyploid.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --ref-bed BED of the unduplicated reference. --poly-bed BED of the polyploid. --prefix, -o Output prefix. --copies Copies expected per reference region (2 tetraploid, 3 hexaploid). (default: 2) --window Window (reference genes) of the retention curves. (default: 100) --permutations Shuffles for the bias test (0: no test). (default: 200) --seed Random seed. (default: 666) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 sv call
docs.text:
Structural rearrangements and small variants between two assemblies.

Group sv · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sv call [OPTIONS] PAF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the approach of SyRI (Goel M et al. 2019, Genome Biol 20:277): first find what is syntenic, then explain everything else relative to it. From the alignments of wga align (minimap2 with base-level CIGAR), on every pair of homologous chromosomes:

  1. syntenic path (SYN): the highest-scoring collinear chain of forward alignments (dynamic programming over the whole chromosome; score: aligned bp minus overlaps);
  2. inversions (INV): chains of reverse alignments that sit in the same place on both genomes relative to the syntenic path (as many syntenic alignments before them on the reference as on the query) and do not overlap it, accepted from the best down;
  3. translocations and duplications: the remaining alignments, on any chromosome pair, are chained into blocks (--min-size aligned bp). A block whose reference region is new and whose query region is new is a translocation (TRANS; inverted: INVTR); a block whose reference region is already syntenic, inverted or translocated is an extra copy in the query (DUP gain; inverted: INVDP), and one whose query region is already used is a copy lost from the query (DUP loss). Blocks are accepted from the best down, so nested candidates collapse;
  4. gaps of the syntenic path: between neighbouring syntenic alignments, sequence on the reference only is a deletion (DEL), on the query only an insertion (INS), on both a highly diverged region (HDR); neighbours overlapping on the reference mark a tandem duplication in the query (DUP gain), overlapping on the query one lost from it (DUP loss); long indels inside alignments are reported as INS and DEL;
  5. not aligned (NOTAL): reference sequence left in none of the above;
  6. small variants: SNPs and indels shorter than --min-size from the CIGAR of the syntenic, inverted, translocated and duplicated alignments, written as VCF.
mcscan3 wga align col.fa ler.fa -o col.ler --preset asm5
mcscan3 sv call col.ler.paf --ref col.fa --qry ler.fa -o col.ler

Writes <prefix>.sv.tsv (type, reference and query coordinates, strand, sizes), <prefix>.vcf (small variants, and SVs as symbolic alleles), <prefix>.summary.tsv (per type: count, reference bp, query bp) and, with sv plot, the rearrangement figure.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PAF Alignments (PAF with cg:Z CIGAR) of wga align.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --ref Reference assembly (FASTA): SNPs and indels. --qry Query assembly (FASTA): SNPs and indels. --min-size Smallest structural variant (bp); shorter go to the VCF. (default: 50) --min-block Smallest inversion, translocation or duplication. (default: 1000) --min-identity Alignments below this identity are ignored. (default: 0.0)

docs.title: mcscan3 sv merge
docs.text:
Merge the structural variants of many genomes against one reference.

Group sv · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sv merge [OPTIONS] CALLS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the multi-genome use of SyRI and plotsr (Goel M & Schneeberger K 2022, Bioinformatics 38:2922) and pan-genome SV catalogues (Jiao WB & Schneeberger K 2020, Nat Commun 11:989). From the sv call tables of every query against the same reference:

  1. merging: events of the same kind (inversion, translocation, duplication, deletion, insertion, diverged region) found in several genomes are one pan-SV when their reference spans overlap reciprocally by --overlap (insertions: positions within 100 bp and sizes within a factor of two); clusters are built by single linkage along the reference;
  2. presence: each pan-SV is present (1) or absent (0) in every genome, which gives its frequency, the frequency spectrum of each kind and a presence matrix for association studies;
  3. core and variable genome: every reference base is counted in the genomes that align to it (syntenic or rearranged): aligned in all of them it is core, in some variable, in none private to the reference.
mcscan3 sv merge col.ler.sv.tsv col.cvi.sv.tsv -o two --names ler,cvi

Writes <prefix>.pansv.tsv (pan-SV, kind, reference span, median size, frequency, genomes), <prefix>.presence.tsv (pan-SV x genome), <prefix>.core.tsv (per reference chromosome: core, variable and private bp), <prefix>.summary.tsv and the figure <prefix>.<format> (size spectra, frequency spectra, core and variable genome).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CALLS Tables of sv call, all against the same reference.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --names Genome names, comma-separated (default: from the tables). --overlap Least reciprocal overlap of one event in two genomes. (default: 0.5) --min-size Smallest event (bp). (default: 50) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 sv pan
docs.text:
Structural-variant pipeline over many assemblies.

Group sv · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 sv pan [OPTIONS] FASTAS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Aligns every query assembly to the reference (wga align), calls its variants (sv call) and merges them into pan-SVs with their presence in each genome and the core and variable reference genome (sv merge); with --stack each genome is also aligned to the previous one for a stacked rearrangement plot (sv plot). Alignments and calls already in <prefix>.work are reused, so an interrupted run resumes:

mcscan3 sv pan col.fa ler.fa cvi.fa eri.fa kyo.fa sha.fa -o arabidopsis --stack

Writes the outputs of sv merge under <prefix>, the pairwise tables in <prefix>.work and, with --stack, <prefix>.stack.<format>.

docs.title: Options

(default: asm5) --cpus Threads (default: all). --stack Also align each genome to the previous one: stacked plot. --overlap Least reciprocal overlap of one event in two genomes. (default: 0.5) --min-size Smallest event (bp). (default: 50) --plot-min-size Smallest event in the stacked plot (bp). (default: 10000) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, in the style of plotsr (Goel M & Schneeberger K 2022, Bioinformatics 38:2922): each genome is a row of chromosomes laid end to end, top to bottom in the order given, and the output of sv call between each pair of neighbouring genomes is drawn as ribbons: syntenic regions in grey, inversions, translocations and duplications in colour. Chromosomes of each lower genome are ordered after their homologues above. Small events (--min-size) are left out so that large rearrangements stand out:

mcscan3 sv plot col.ler.sv.tsv ler.cvi.sv.tsv -o stack --min-size 10000

docs.title: mcscan3 synfind run
docs.text:
Syntenic region of every gene (mcscan3 synfind run; legacy compara.synfind).

Group synfind · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synfind run [OPTIONS] BLASTFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
For each query gene, BLAST hits within a window (--window genes, centred on the gene) are chained by single linkage into candidate regions, scored by the number of anchors (--scoring collinear keeps the longest collinear chain). Output per region:

query  anchor  S|G|F  score  flank_dist  orientation  qnote  snote

S = syntelog found; G/F = gray gene (no match; region marked by the closest (flanking) gene). Both directions are reported unless it is a self comparison. --sqlite writes a database instead. With --scoring density orientation is reported as . (the original crashed; docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.5).

docs.title: Arguments

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny anchor
docs.text:
Synteny-constrained anchors between two genomes.

Group synteny · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny anchor [OPTIONS] HITS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the synteny method of GENESPACE (Lovell et al. 2022, eLife 11:e78526), reimplemented from the paper. Its premise: in a syntenic region, homologs should be single copy between two genomes (or as many copies as their ploidy). So copy-number noise is removed before chaining, and syntenic hits are recovered around the chains afterwards:

  1. Tandem arrays. On each chromosome, genes of one orthogroup (--orthogroups; without them, genes with the same best hit in the other genome) less than --array-jump genes apart form an array. Its representative is the gene nearest the array's median position (ties: the longest gene).
  2. Candidate anchors. Hits between representatives, of one orthogroup when orthogroups are given, that are among the --hits best of both genes (default 2; 4 for a genome against itself). Keeping more than the single best hit lets the copies of a polyploid all form chains; on simulated genomes it raised recall against a diploid from 0.97 to 0.999 at a precision cost below 0.001.
  3. Gene-rank coordinates. Each candidate gene's position is its rank among the candidate genes of its chromosome, so lost, unannotated and tandem copies do not open gaps.
  4. Chains. Collinear chains in those coordinates, on both strands: consecutive anchors at most --max-gaps ranks apart on both genomes; chains of at least --block-size anchors are kept (a dynamic program over the candidates, best chains first).
  5. Buffer. Every hit within --buffer genes of an anchor on both genomes is syntenic (<prefix>.syntenic.tsv). Each block's anchors are then extended with its block-local best hits (among its syntenic hits with a C-score of at least 0.5, of one orthogroup when given, within the --hits best of both genes) and with the hits between tandem copies of its anchored pairs. The C-score (score over the better of the two genes' best scores) keeps out weak hits of genes whose syntenic partner was lost.
  6. Secondary blocks (--secondary N, default 3, for polyploids and old WGDs). The syntenic hits found so far are masked, and steps 2-5 are rerun on the rest without the orthogroup constraint and with twice the gaps, until no block is found or N rounds. Blocks with most anchors less than --mask-buffer (100) genes from earlier ones are dropped (GENESPACE uses 500; with fusions, copies of a region can lie closer than that on one chromosome).

Writes <prefix>.anchors (blocks in the MCscan format: ### then gene1 gene2 score) and <prefix>.syntenic.tsv (every syntenic hit, with its block and whether it is an anchor):

mcscan3 synteny anchor grape.peach.last --qbed grape.bed --sbed peach.bed \
    --orthogroups Orthogroups.tsv -o grape.peach

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description HITS BLAST tabular hits (LAST, DIAMOND, MMseqs2 or BLAST), e.g. a.b.last.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --prefix, -o Output prefix (default: a.b from the hits file). --orthogroups Orthogroups (OrthoFinder Orthogroups.tsv or genegroup). --hits Best hits per gene kept as candidates (default: 2; 4 for a genome against itself). --block-size Fewest anchors in a block. (default: 5) --max-gaps Most genes skipped between consecutive anchors (gene ranks). (default: 5) --buffer Hits within this many genes of an anchor are syntenic. (default: 100) --array-jump Most genes between two members of a tandem array. (default: 50) --secondary Rounds of secondary blocks (masking the syntenic hits found). (default: 3) --mask-buffer Secondary blocks this close to earlier ones are dropped. (default: 100) --out-format Also write: mcscanx, wgdi, genespace, iadhore, synvisio, bedpe, tsv (comma-separated).

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny breakpoint
docs.text:
Breakpoints where collinearity ends (mcscan3 synteny breakpoint; legacy compara.synteny breakpoint).

Group synteny · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny breakpoint [OPTIONS] BLASTFILE BEDFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
blastfile maps markers (query) to scaffolds (subject); bedfile gives marker positions in the related genome. Collinear marker runs are found per scaffold and the gaps between them are printed as BED intervals. As in the original, the BLAST hits are first written to <blastfile>.bed (sorted in place like sort -k1,1 -k2,2n -k3,3n -k4,4).

Note (original behaviour): markers are matched by the BLAST query name up to its last ., so names such as gene.t01 do not match a BED that uses the full name.

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny convert
docs.text:
Synteny blocks in the format of your choice (mcscan3 synteny convert, --out-format).

Group synteny · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny convert [OPTIONS] BLOCKS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Blocks of anchors (MCscan .anchors, MCScanX .collinearity or WGDI collinearity files; read automatically) are written in one or more formats, with the gene coordinates of the two BED files:

  • anchors: MCscan .anchors (### between blocks, gene1 gene2 score);
  • mcscanx: MCScanX .collinearity (## Alignment k: score=... e_value=... N=... chr1&chr2 plus|minus` then `k- i: gene1 gene2 value`) and its four-column `.gff (chromosome, gene, start, end) for both genomes, the inputs of MCScanX's downstream tools and SynVisio;
  • wgdi: WGDI collinearity (# Alignment k: score=... pvalue=... N=... chr1&chr2 plus|minus then gene1 order1 gene2 order2 direction), a block table (blockinfo.csv: id, chromosomes, start and end orders, p value, length, Ks columns filled from --ks when given, the anchor orders block1/block2 and anchor densities density1/density2; the columns homo1-homo5 and tandem_ratio are left empty as they come from WGDI's own BLAST ranking) and WGDI's .gff and .lens for each genome;
  • genespace: GENESPACE's syntenic hits (<g1>_vs_<g2>.synHits.txt.gz: anchors with genome-wide gene orders, isAnchor TRUE and the block id) and syntenicBlock_coordinates.csv (block extents in base pairs and gene orders, first and last genes, orientation);
  • iadhore: i-ADHoRe multiplicons.txt and anchorpoints.txt (gene positions 0-based);
  • synvisio: the MCScanX pair (.collinearity and a .gff of both genomes) named for SynVisio's upload page;
  • bedpe: one line per block, the two block extents in base pairs, name, anchors, strands;
  • tsv: one line per anchor with block, both genes and their coordinates, score and strand.

Block scores follow MCScanX's defaults (50 per anchor, -1 per gene of gap on the longer side); the p value (MCScanX's e_value, WGDI's pvalue) is MCscan3's: the chance of as many anchors in the block's gene-rank box if the anchors of the chromosome pair were spread uniformly (Poisson). MCScanX writes BLAST e-values in its third column; MCscan3 writes the anchor's score there. Formats after MCScanX (Wang Y et al. 2012, NAR 40:e49), WGDI (Sun P et al. 2022, Mol Plant 15:1841), i-ADHoRe 3.0 (Proost S et al. 2012, NAR 40:e11) and SynVisio (Bandi V, Gutwin C 2020) and GENESPACE (Lovell JT et al. 2022, eLife 11:e78526):

mcscan3 synteny convert grape.peach.anchors --qbed grape.bed --sbed peach.bed \
    --to mcscanx,wgdi,bedpe -o grape.peach
mcscan3 synteny anchor grape.peach.last --out-format mcscanx,wgdi

(default: mcscanx) --prefix, -o Output prefix (default: the input without extension). --from Input format: auto, anchors, mcscanx or wgdi. (default: auto) --ks Ks of gene pairs (for WGDI's block table). --names Genome names, e.g. grape,peach (default: from the BED files).

MCscan3: blocks of .anchors, MCScanX or WGDI collinearity files written as MCScanX (Wang Y et al. 2012, NAR 40:e49), WGDI (Sun P et al. 2022, Mol Plant 15:1841), i-ADHoRe 3.0 (Proost S et al. 2012, NAR 40:e11), SynVisio, GENESPACE (Lovell JT et al. 2022, eLife 11:e78526), BEDPE or a long table, with gene coordinates from the BED files.

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny decay
docs.text:
Decay of synteny with divergence across many genome pairs.

Group synteny · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny decay [OPTIONS] ANCHORS...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. For each pair of genomes (one anchors file each), the divergence of the pair is measured as the median protein (or DNA) identity of its anchor genes, and the state of its synteny by the number of blocks, their N50 (anchors) and the share of the first genome's genes inside blocks. Plotted against each other, pairs from different kingdoms show how fast gene order erodes as sequences diverge:

mcscan3 synteny decay fungi=fungi/scer.klac.lifted.anchors insects=insects/dmel.dpse.lifted.anchors \
    -o decay

GROUP=FILE puts a pair in a group (one colour each). Each anchors file <a>.<b>.<suffix> needs <a>.bed and <b>.bed (--bed-dir, default: next to it) and the alignment it came from, <a>.<b>.last next to it (or --blast-suffix), for the identities.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORS Anchors files .., as GROUP=FILE to colour by group.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix: .tsv and the figure. (default: decay) --bed-dir Directory of the BED files (default: next to each file). --blast-suffix Alignment next to each file: ... (default: last) --min-block Leave out blocks with fewer anchors. (default: 0) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300) --title Figure title.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

Synteny decays with divergence: block N50 and the share of genes in blocks against the identity of anchor genes, for plant, yeast and insect genome pairs.

mcscan3 synteny decay plants=core/grape.peach.lifted.anchors plants=core/grape.poplar.lifted.anchors \
 fungi=kingdoms/fungi/scer.klac.lifted.anchors fungi=kingdoms/fungi/klac.egos.lifted.anchors fungi=kingdoms/fungi/scer.egos.lifted.anchors \
 fungi=kingdoms/fungi/klac.kmar.lifted.anchors fungi=kingdoms/fungi/egos.esin.lifted.anchors \
 insects=kingdoms/insects/dmel.dsim.lifted.anchors insects=kingdoms/insects/dmel.dyak.lifted.anchors insects=kingdoms/insects/dmel.dpse.lifted.anchors \
 insects=kingdoms/insects/dmel.agam.lifted.anchors insects=kingdoms/insects/dpse.agam.lifted.anchors -o kingdoms/decay && cat kingdoms/decay.tsv

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny depth
docs.text:
Synteny depth of each genome (mcscan3 synteny depth; legacy compara.synteny depth).

Group synteny · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny depth [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Layers the blocks onto each genome (in gene ranks) and reports, to stderr, the fraction of genes covered by 0, 1, 2, ... blocks. A 1:2 pattern (e.g. grape vs poplar) shows most genes of the first genome at depth 2. --depthfile writes gene<TAB>depth for every gene; the --histogram plot is the plot depth feature.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --depthfile Write genedepth here. --histogram Plot depth histograms (see plot depth). --xmax Histogram x-axis maximum. --title Histogram title. --quota Histogram: force this quota, e.g. 1:2. --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed).

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny layout
docs.text:
Order query seqids by their synteny to subject seqids (mcscan3 synteny layout; legacy compara.synteny layout).

Group synteny · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny layout [OPTIONS] SIMPLE_FILE QSEQIDS SSEQIDS

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Both seqid lists are given on the command line, comma-separated. Each block of the .simple file adds its score to the pair (subject seqid, query seqid); a seeded genetic algorithm then finds the order of the query seqids that maximises the heaviest collinear chain of those scores:

mcscan3 synteny layout grape.peach.anchors.simple Vv06,Vv08 Pp06 --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed

Progress (Current iteration N: max_score=...) is printed every 20 generations, then the query seqids in the new order. The original crashed when the first generation did not improve the score (docs/DEVIATIONS.md A.3); MCscan3 fixes this.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SIMPLE_FILE Blocks in .simple format (query/subject). QSEQIDS Query seqids to order, comma-separated. SSEQIDS Subject seqids in their fixed order, comma-separated.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --cpus Number of CPUs to use, 0 = all (at most 32). (default: 0)

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny liftover
docs.text:
Recruit extra anchors near existing ones (mcscan3 synteny liftover; legacy compara.synteny liftover).

Group synteny · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny liftover [OPTIONS] BLAST_FILE ANCHOR_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Every BLAST hit within --dist genes (L1 distance in rank space) of an anchor is added to that anchor's block, with its score suffixed by L. Anchors not present in the BLAST file are then dropped and scores corrected. Writes <anchors>.lifted.anchors (or -o):

mcscan3 synteny liftover grape.peach.last.filtered grape.peach.anchors \
    --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed --no-strip-names -o grape.peach.lifted.anchors

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLAST_FILE BLAST file. ANCHOR_FILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --no-strip-names Do not strip alternative splicing (e.g. At5g06540.1 -> At5g06540). --outfile, -o Output (default: .lifted.anchors). --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --dist Extent of flanking regions to search. (default: 10)

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny mcscan
docs.text:
Stack synteny blocks on a reference genome, MCscan style (mcscan3 synteny mcscan; legacy compara.synteny mcscan).

Group synteny · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny mcscan [OPTIONS] BEDFILE ANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The first column lists every gene of the reference BED in order; each further column is a "track": the best non-overlapping chain of blocks, then the next best among the remaining ones, up to --iter tracks. Each cell holds the syntenic gene or .:

mcscan3 synteny mcscan grape.bed grape.peach.lifted.anchors --iter=1 -o grape.peach.i1.blocks

The chain log (Chain 0: score=...) goes to stderr. --trackids writes the block ids of each track to <outfile>.tracks; --mergetandem replaces genes by their tandem cluster.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BEDFILE Reference BED. ANCHORFILE Anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --iter Maximum number of tracks (chains). (default: 100) --ascii Output x symbols rather than gene names. --nm Clip block ends to allow slight overlaps. (default: 10) --trackids Write block ids per track to .tracks. --mergetandem Merge tandem genes from this file. --outfile, -o Output file. (default: stdout)

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

cd core && mcscan3 synteny mcscan grape.bed grape.peach.lifted.anchors --iter 1 -o grape.peach.i1.blocks  && mcscan3 synteny mcscan grape.bed grape.poplar.lifted.anchors --iter 2 -o grape.poplar.i2.blocks && head -5 grape.poplar.i2.blocks

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny scan
docs.text:
Find syntenic anchors (mcscan3 synteny scan; legacy compara.synteny scan).

Group synteny · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny scan [OPTIONS] BLAST_FILE ANCHOR_FILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Single-linkage clustering of BLAST hits in gene-rank space: two hits are linked when both genomes' ranks differ by at most --dist genes; clusters with at least -n non-redundant anchors become blocks. Writes an anchors file and prints a summary to stderr:

mcscan3 synteny scan grape.peach.last.filtered grape.peach.anchors \
    --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed --no-strip-names

For self comparisons, hits within --intrabound genes of the diagonal are ignored. --liftover <blast> then runs synteny liftover on the result.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description BLAST_FILE Filtered BLAST file. ANCHOR_FILE Output anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description -n, --min-size Minimum number of anchors in a cluster. (default: 4) --intrabound Self comparison: ignore blocks this close to the diagonal. (default: 300) --liftover BLAST file to lift over extra anchors from. --liftover-dist Liftover distance (default: --dist // 2). --no-strip-names Do not strip alternative splicing (e.g. At5g06540.1 -> At5g06540). --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --dist Extent of flanking regions to search. (default: 20) --out-format Also write: mcscanx, wgdi, genespace, iadhore, synvisio, bedpe, tsv (comma-separated).

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
Run on real data in the MCscan3 showcase (all commands on published genomes, in workflow order). The command line, console output, output files and figures below are those of that run.

Syntenic anchors by single-linkage clustering of the filtered hits.

cd core && mcscan3 synteny scan grape.peach.last.filtered grape.peach.anchors --qbed grape.bed --sbed peach.bed --no-strip-names  && mcscan3 synteny scan grape.grape.last.filtered grape.grape.anchors --qbed grape.bed --sbed grape.bed --no-strip-names  && mcscan3 synteny scan grape.poplar.last.filtered grape.poplar.anchors --qbed grape.bed --sbed poplar.bed --no-strip-names

docs.title: mcscan3 synteny screen
docs.text:
Extract a subset of blocks from an anchors file (mcscan3 synteny screen; legacy compara.synteny screen).

Group synteny · status parity-verified

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 synteny screen [OPTIONS] ANCHORFILE NEWANCHORFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Filters: --ids (0-based block numbers, comma separated), --seqids (allowed chromosomes), --seqpairs (allowed chrA,chrB pairs), --minspan (genes spanned on both sides), --minsize (anchors), --intrabound (self comparisons: drop blocks near the diagonal). --simple also writes the .simple file of the result (tutorial usage):

mcscan3 synteny screen grape.peach.anchors grape.peach.anchors.new \
    --qbed=grape.bed --sbed=peach.bed --simple --minspan=30

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description ANCHORFILE Anchors file. NEWANCHORFILE Output anchors file.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --qbed Query BED (default: .bed from a file named a.b.*). --sbed Subject BED (default: .bed). --ids File with 0-based block IDs, comma separated. --seqids File with allowed seqids. --seqpairs File with allowed seqid pairs chrA,chrB. --intrabound Self comparison: drop blocks this close to the diagonal. (default: 300) --minspan Only blocks spanning >= this many genes. (default: 0) --minsize Only blocks with >= this many anchors. (default: 0) --simple Also write the .simple file.

docs.title: mcscan3 te age
docs.text:
Insertion history of LTR retrotransposons.

Group te · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 te age [OPTIONS] LTR_TABLE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
• ages: the two LTRs of an element are identical when it inserts, so their Kimura distance K dates the insertion: T = K / (2 r), with r the substitution rate per site per year (SanMiguel P, et al. (1998) Nat Genet 20:43; rice 1.3e-8, Ma J & Bennetzen JL (2004) PNAS 101:12404);
  • per clade: ages, recent insertions (younger than --young years) and the median of each superfamily and clade from te classify;
  • nesting chronology: an element inside another inserted after it, so it should be younger; the share of nested pairs whose molecular ages agree with that order checks the dating;
  • solo LTRs: an LTR left by recombination between the two LTRs of an element; a hit of an LTR sequence of the library (te annotate) that is not inside an intact element, has no internal region of the same superfamily within --solo-gap bp and passes the filter of Ou S & Jiang N (2018) Plant Physiol 176:1410 (alignment score 300 or more, 100 bp or longer); the solo:intact ratio of a clade measures how much of it has been removed by recombination (Vitte C & Panaud O (2003) Mol Biol Evol 20:528).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description LTR_TABLE te ltr table (.ltr.tsv, after te classify --ltr).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --annotation, -a te annotate table or RepeatMasker .out, for solo LTRs. --rate Substitutions per site per year. (default: 1.3e-08) --level Group by clade or superfamily. (default: clade) --young Insertions younger than this many million years are recent. (default: 1.0) --solo-gap An internal region this close (bp) means the LTR is not solo. (default: 500) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 te annotate
docs.text:
Whole-genome TE annotation with a library.

Group te · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 te annotate [OPTIONS] GENOME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The genome is masked with the library (te library) by RepeatMasker (Smit AFA, Hubley R & Green P, RepeatMasker Open-4.0, http://www.repeatmasker.org) with the settings of the EDTA benchmark (Ou S, et al. (2019) Genome Biol 20:275): -q -no_is -norna -nolow -div 40 -cutoff 225. Each hit keeps its CpG-adjusted Kimura divergence from the consensus (transitions at CpG sites counted as one, a single one as a tenth), the measure of TE landscapes. Overlapping hits are already resolved by RepeatMasker; the composition is counted on the union of the hits of each class, so a base is counted once per class and once in total.

Writes <prefix>.te.tsv (one row per hit), <prefix>.te.gff3, <prefix>.te.out (RepeatMasker table), <prefix>.te.summary.tsv (bp and share of the genome per class) and a JSON summary.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOME Genome FASTA (plain or gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --library, -l TE library (te library, or any name#Class/Superfamily FASTA). --prefix, -o Output prefix. --cpus Parallel RepeatMasker jobs. (default: 4) --repeatmasker RepeatMasker program or its folder. --from-out Use this RepeatMasker .out (and its .align) instead of masking. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 te classify
docs.text:
Classification of transposable elements by their protein domains.

Group te · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 te classify [OPTIONS] FASTA

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the domain-based lineage classification of TEsorter (Zhang RG et al. 2022, Hortic Res 9:uhac017) with the REXdb profiles (Neumann P et al. 2019, Mob DNA 10:1), written from the papers:

  1. every sequence is translated in six frames and searched with HMMER hmmsearch against the domain profiles (REXdb for plants or metazoa, or both; GyDB or any HMM library whose names are lineage/path:DOMAIN), in parallel chunks with a fixed database size so that E-values do not depend on the number of processes;
  2. for every sequence and domain type (GAG, PROT, INT, RT, RH, CHD, TPase, HEL...) the best hit covering --min-coverage of the profile is kept;
  3. the lineage is the deepest node of the REXdb tree on which the domains agree: from the root, the best-supported child (by summed bit score) is taken while it holds at least --agree of the support; otherwise the call stops at the parent and is marked mixed;
  4. the element is oriented by the strand of its domains, called complete when it has every core domain of its superfamily, and the order of the domains along it is checked against the superfamily (Ty1/copia GAG-PROT-INT-RT-RH; Ty3/gypsy GAG-PROT-RT-RH-INT).

Writes <prefix>.cls.tsv (sequence, order, superfamily, clade, lineage, support, complete, strand, domain order and its agreement, domains) and <prefix>.domains.tsv (every kept hit with its position on the sequence), and the classified FASTA (name#Order/Superfamily).

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FASTA TE sequences (library, elements of te ltr...).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --db rexdb-plant, rexdb-metazoa, rexdb (both), gydb, or an HMM file (lineage:DOMAIN names). (default: rexdb-plant) --cpus Parallel hmmsearch processes. (default: 4) --evalue Largest domain E-value. (default: 0.001) --min-coverage Least share of a profile covered by a hit. (default: 0.2) --agree Least share of domain support to go one lineage level deeper. (default: 0.75) --ltr te ltr table to update with the calls (.ltr.tsv).

docs.title: mcscan3 te helitron
docs.text:
Helitrons, rolling-circle DNA transposons.

Group te · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 te helitron [OPTIONS] GENOME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: a native structural search written from the structure of the elements (Kapitonov VV & Jurka J 2001, PNAS 98:8714; Wicker T et al. 2007, Nat Rev Genet 8:973) and the approach of HelitronScanner (Xiong W, et al. 2014, PNAS 111:10263), which finds the conserved ends of a family at many insertion sites, without its code. A Helitron inserts between an A and a T without a target-site duplication, starts with 5'-TC and ends with 3'-CTRR a few bases after a GC-rich hairpin; most copies are non-autonomous and keep only the two ends.

  1. 3' ends: every CTRR followed by T, on both strands, is keyed by the two 16-mers before it; anchors sharing a key are one candidate family;
  2. sharp 3' boundary: a family needs copies at independent sites, where the bases after the end differ (copies of a larger repeat share them), and most copies need the hairpin (stem of --min-stem bp or more, loop of 3-15 bp, ending 2-12 bp before the CTRR);
  3. 5' ends: upstream of each copy, every A|TC within --max-len is keyed by the 16-mers after it; the key shared by the most copies at independent sites (the bases before it differ) is the 5' end of the family, and copies without the exact key are matched to its 32 bp consensus;
  4. filters: elements with a target-site duplication of 4 bp or more are not Helitrons; an element overlapping a better one is dropped unless nested inside it; --min-copies.

Engines. --engine native runs the search above. --engine helitronscanner runs an installed HelitronScanner (heads and tails of both strands in parallel) and MCscan3 filters its candidates: an A|T or T|T target site, no TSD, head plus tail score of 12 or more, a 3' end shared by copies at independent sites and a 5' 16-mer seen at least twice. both merges the two; auto uses HelitronScanner when it is installed. With --domains, calls with retrotransposon or TIR domains (REXdb) are dropped, and calls longer than --max-nonautonomous need the Rep/Hel protein.

Writes <prefix>.helitron.tsv, .gff3, .fa, <prefix>.helitronlib.fa (the longest copy of each family), a JSON summary and a figure.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOME Genome FASTA (plain or gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --min-len Shortest element (bp). (default: 150) --max-len Longest element (bp). (default: 40000) --min-stem Shortest hairpin stem before the 3' CTRR (bp). (default: 6) --min-copies Least copies at independent sites (2 or more). (default: 2) --engine native (MCscan3 search), helitronscanner (HelitronScanner candidates filtered by MCscan3), both, or auto (helitronscanner when installed, else native). (default: auto) --helitronscanner Folder of HelitronScanner.jar. --java Java runtime for HelitronScanner. --cpus Parallel HelitronScanner scans (up to 4). (default: 4) --mem Java memory per scan (GB). docs.title: Method and references
docs.text: New in MCscan3 (no JCVI equivalent). Native search for CTRR-T 3' ends keyed by the bases before them, shared by copies at independent insertion sites (edit distance of the flanks) with a hairpin before the end, then the A|TC 5' end shared upstream; structure after Kapitonov VV & Jurka J (2001) PNAS 98:8714 and the conserved-end approach of HelitronScanner (Xiong W, et al. (2014) PNAS 111:10263); no code reused. With --engine helitronscanner the installed HelitronScanner supplies candidates that MCscan3 filters for the AT|TT target site, end scores, shared 3' ends and repeated 5' ends; calls with non-Helitron domains (REXdb) are dropped.

docs.title: mcscan3 te lai
docs.text:
LTR Assembly Index.

Group te · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 te lai [OPTIONS] GENOME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The LAI measures how completely an assembly holds its LTR retrotransposons, after Ou S, Chen J & Jiang N (2018) Nucleic Acids Res 46:e126:

  • raw LAI = 100 x (bases in intact LTR retrotransposons) / (bases annotated as LTR sequence);
  • LAI = raw LAI + 2.8138 x (94 - mean LTR identity), set to 0 when the raw LAI is 0 or the correction makes it negative; the correction removes the effect of the age of the LTR families;
  • the mean LTR identity comes from comparing the sequences annotated as terminal repeats (library entries *_LTR; all LTR hits when the library does not split LTRs from internal regions) with each other, all against all: the copies sharing most sampled 15-mers with a sequence are searched on both strands (seeds of shared 11-mers, gapped X-drop extension, as a local search finds hits) and the identity of its top-scoring hit is kept; the identities are averaged;
  • regional LAI in 3 Mb windows moved by 300 kb; a window with less than 1% LTR sequence has its LAI scaled to a tenth; the whole-genome LAI is reliable when intact elements make up at least 0.1% and LTR sequence at least 5% of the genome;
  • draft (LAI < 10), reference (10 to 20) and gold (20 or more) quality.

Intact elements come from te ltr (or a LTR_retriever pass.list) and the LTR sequence from te annotate (or a RepeatMasker .out); nested elements are counted once.

docs.text: Argument Description GENOME Genome FASTA (plain or gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --intact Intact elements: te ltr table or LTR_retriever pass.list. --annotation, -a te annotate table or RepeatMasker .out (LTR hits are used). --prefix, -o Output prefix. --window Window for regional LAI (bp). (default: 3000000) --step Step between windows (bp). (default: 300000) --identity Mean LTR identity (%) instead of estimating it. --sample Estimate the identity from this many LTR sequences (0: all). (default: 0) --mono File of sequence names of one monoploid set (polyploids). --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 te ltr
docs.text:
Intact LTR retrotransposons.

Group te · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 te ltr [OPTIONS] GENOME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: a native, parallel search for full-length LTR retrotransposons, written from the structure of the elements as described for LTRharvest (Ellinghaus D et al. 2008, BMC Bioinformatics 9:18), LTR_FINDER (Xu Z & Wang H 2007, NAR 35:W265) and LTR_retriever (Ou S & Jiang N 2018, Plant Physiol 176:1410), without their code:

  1. seeds: k-mer minimizers of every chromosome chunk; k-mers that recur closer than the shortest LTR distance (tandem and satellite arrays) are dropped;
  2. direct repeats: pairs of identical seeds --min-dist to --max-dist apart are chained along their diagonal (indels allowed) into pairs of similar regions, then extended outward by an ungapped X-drop;
  3. boundaries: both ends are moved (by the same amount on the two LTRs) to the best combination of the 5'-TG...CA-3' terminal motif and an identical 4-6 bp target-site duplication (TSD) flanking the element; non-canonical motifs are kept when the TSD is found;
  4. LTR alignment: banded global alignment of the two LTRs gives identity and the Kimura two-parameter distance K; the insertion age is K / (2 x --rate);
  5. filters: LTR length, element length, LTR identity, internal region (length, N content), tandem arrays (a third copy at the same period, or an internal region that is half repeated k-mers, as in satellite and centromeric arrays), and the polypurine tract (PPT) and primer binding site (PBS, with --trna) to orient the element;
  6. overlaps: candidates for the same element are reduced to the best; elements inside the internal region or the LTR of another are kept as nested insertions (with their host).

Chromosomes are cut into overlapping chunks searched in parallel, so genome size and sequence names do not matter. Writes <prefix>.ltr.tsv (one row per element), <prefix>.ltr.gff3, <prefix>.ltr.fa (elements), <prefix>.ltrlib.fa (LTR and internal sequences of each element, for building the library) and figures.

docs.text: Argument Description GENOME Genome FASTA (plain or gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --cpus Parallel processes (chromosome chunks). (default: 4) --min-ltr Shortest LTR (bp). (default: 100) --max-ltr Longest LTR (bp). (default: 7000) --min-len Shortest element (bp). (default: 1000) --max-len Longest element (bp). (default: 25000) --max-dist Largest distance between the starts of the LTRs. (default: 20000) --min-identity Least identity of the two LTRs (0-1). (default: 0.85) --rate Substitutions per site per year (for ages). (default: 1.3e-08) --trna tRNA FASTA: primer binding sites orient elements. --passes Search passes (later passes find elements broken by nested insertions). (default: 3) --k Seed k-mer length. (default: 15) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 te simulate
docs.text:
Simulated genomes with transposable elements at known places (for tests and benchmarks).

Group te · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 te simulate [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Elements are inserted one after another into a random background, so later insertions can land inside earlier elements (nested insertions) exactly as in a real genome, and every coordinate is tracked. LTR retrotransposons get two LTRs of a chosen identity (substitutions with a transition:transversion ratio of 2, and small indels), 5'-TG...CA-3' ends and a 5 bp target-site duplication; decoys that trouble LTR finders are added as well: tandem segmental duplications, satellite arrays, solo LTRs and truncated elements.

DNA transposons with terminal inverted repeats (TIRs) follow the rules of their superfamily (Wicker T et al. 2007, Nat Rev Genet 8:973): Tc1-Mariner inserts at TA and duplicates it, hAT makes 8 bp target-site duplications, Mutator 9-10 bp with long TIRs, PIF-Harbinger 3 bp (TAA or TTA), CACTA 3 bp with 5'-CACTA...TAGTG-3' ends and PiggyBac TTAA. MITEs are short non-autonomous copies with the TIRs of a family. Helitrons insert between an A and a T without a duplication, start with 5'-TC and end with a hairpin a few bases before 3'-CTRR; most copies are shortened (non-autonomous) but keep both ends.

Elements are inserted one after another into a random background, so later insertions land inside earlier ones; LTR pairs diverge with age (transition:transversion 2:1, short indels) and each insertion duplicates its 5 bp target site; decoys: solo LTRs, truncated copies, tandem duplications and satellites.

docs.title: mcscan3 te tir
docs.text:
DNA transposons with terminal inverted repeats, and MITEs.

Group te · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 te tir [OPTIONS] GENOME

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: a native, parallel structural search written from the structure of the elements (Wicker T et al. 2007, Nat Rev Genet 8:973) and the superfamily rules used by TIR-Learner (Su W, Gu X & Peterson T 2019, Mol Plant 12:447) and MITE-Hunter (Han Y & Wessler SR 2010, NAR 38:e199), without their code:

  1. seeds: every k-mer of a chromosome chunk is paired with the reverse complement of the k-mers up to --max-len downstream (low-complexity and tandem k-mers left out);
  2. inverted repeats: seed pairs on one anti-diagonal (x + y constant, indels allowed) are chained, then extended outward and inward by a gapped X-drop, so each arm is a TIR;
  3. boundaries: the two ends are moved together to the best target-site duplication (TSD), so chance base pairs beyond the TIRs (the palindromic TA of Tc1-Mariner) are trimmed;
  4. filters: TIR length and identity (banded alignment of one TIR against the reverse complement of the other), element length, N content, tandem TIRs;
  5. superfamily: from the TSD and the ends, after Wicker et al.: TA (Tc1-Mariner, DTT), TTAA (PiggyBac, DTB), 3 bp TWA (PIF-Harbinger, DTH), 3 bp with 5'-CACT (CACTA, DTC), 5 bp (Transib, DTR), 8 bp (hAT, DTA), 9-11 bp (Mutator, DTM);
  6. families: elements sharing k-mers of their TIRs are one family; the superfamily of a family is the majority call of its copies, and --min-copies removes single copies (most false structural calls are single); copies up to --mite-max bp are MITEs.
  7. family ends: the 50 bp ends of each family are aligned back to the genome (11-mer seeds, banded alignment, identity 0.8 or more); a start and an end at the family's length with a TSD of its superfamily is another copy;
  8. domains: with --domains, elements over 2 kb are searched for protein domains (REXdb); elements with retrotransposon or Helitron domains are dropped, a transposase sets the superfamily, and long elements without one are dropped unless CACTA or Mutator.

Writes <prefix>.tir.tsv, <prefix>.tir.gff3, <prefix>.tir.fa and <prefix>.tirlib.fa (the longest copy of each family) and a figure.

docs.text: Argument Description GENOME Genome FASTA (plain or gzipped).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --cpus Parallel processes (chromosome chunks). (default: 4) --min-tir Shortest TIR (bp). (default: 10) --max-tir Longest TIR (bp). (default: 1000) --min-len Shortest element (bp). (default: 50) --max-len Longest element (bp). (default: 20000) --mite-max Elements up to this length are MITEs. (default: 800) --min-identity Least identity of the two TIRs (0-1). (default: 0.8) --min-copies Least copies of a family (1 keeps single copies). (default: 2) --no-tsd Keep elements without a target-site duplication. --k Seed k-mer length. (default: 11) --domains Protein domains of elements over 2 kb (hmmsearch): rexdb, rexdb-plant, rexdb-metazoa, an HMM file, none, or auto (rexdb when hmmsearch is installed). (default: auto) --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 view browse
docs.text:
Interactive genome browser of alignments, SVs, paintings and identity.

Group view · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 view browse [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. One self-contained HTML page (data embedded as JSON, drawn on a <canvas>; no server or network needed) along the chromosomes of a reference, with one track per input:

  • --paf: alignments of a genome (wga align, sv pan), coloured by strand, shaded by identity;
  • --sv: the calls of sv call (syntenic regions faint, rearrangements and indels coloured by type);
  • --pansv: pan-SVs of sv pan/sv merge with their frequency and carriers;
  • --blocks: blocks of introgress scan (painting by source);
  • --identity: per-window identity of view identity, one heat strip per genome.

Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, hover for details, click to zoom to a feature; the position box takes chrom:start-end and the address keeps it (page.html#Col4:1500000-3000000):

mcscan3 view browse --paf col.ler.paf --sv col.ler.sv.tsv --pansv ath.pansv.tsv \
    --identity ath.identity.tsv -o ath.browser.html

docs.title: mcscan3 view identity
docs.text:
Identity of genomes to a reference along its chromosomes.

Group view · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 view identity [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. For each window of the reference and each other genome, the sequence identity of the genome there, as a heatmap (genomes x windows, one panel per chromosome) and a table. Two ways to measure it:

  • from alignments (PAF of wga align or sv pan, with --eqx CIGAR): exact counts of matched, mismatched, inserted and deleted bases in each window, identity = matches / alignment columns (gaps included) and coverage = share of the window aligned. Every CIGAR run is placed with vectorised arithmetic, runs crossing window ends split exactly, so a 120 Mb reference with five genomes takes seconds;
  • from k-mers (--kmer, FASTA only, no alignment needed): the FracMinHash containment of the window's k-mers in the genome, turned into an identity estimate c^(1/k) (the containment ANI of Mash and sourmash: Ondov BD et al. 2016, Genome Biol 17:132; Hera MR et al. 2023, Genome Res 33:1061); no coverage.
mcscan3 view identity --paf col.ler.paf --paf col.cvi.paf -o ath.identity --format png
mcscan3 view identity --kmer col.fa --genome ler.fa --genome cvi.fa -o ath.kid

Writes <prefix>.tsv (chrom, start, end, then identity_ and coverage_) and the heatmap <prefix>.<format>.

docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Every genome (assembly or reads, plain or gzip FASTA/FASTQ) is reduced to a FracMinHash sketch of canonical k-mers (as in introgress scan); for every pair, the share of the smaller sketch found in the other (containment) gives the average nucleotide identity estimate c^(1/k) (containment ANI: Ondov BD et al. 2016, Genome Biol 17:132; Hera MR et al. 2023, Genome Res 33:1061), and the share of k-mers in both of their union the Jaccard index. Sorted sketches are intersected by merging, so 10 plant genomes take well under a minute. Genomes are ordered by average-linkage clustering of 1 - ANI and drawn as a heatmap with the tree:

mcscan3 view matrix col.fa ler.fa cvi.fa eri.fa kyo.fa sha.fa -o ath.ani --format png

Writes <prefix>.tsv (ANI matrix), <prefix>.pairs.tsv (every pair: shared k-mers, containment both ways, Jaccard, ANI) and the heatmap <prefix>.<format>.

(default: 2) --cpus Threads (default: all). --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 view tracks
docs.text:
Genome track figures from an INI file.

Group view · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 view tracks [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the track files of pyGenomeTracks (Lopez-Delisle L et al. 2021, Bioinformatics 37:422). Each [section] of the INI file is a track drawn from top to bottom, with file, title, height (cm), color and file_type (otherwise taken from the file extension). Track types:

  • genes (.bed BED6/BED12, .gff3/.gtf): transcripts with exons and coding parts (style = UCSC arrows on the intron lines, or flybase), stacked so they do not overlap (display = stacked or collapsed), names (labels = false hides them, fontsize), color / border_color; gene_rows limits the stacking;
  • bed: plain intervals (.bed with 3 to 9 columns; itemRgb colours when color = bed_rgb);
  • bedgraph (4 columns) and bigwig (needs the pyBigWig package): type = fill, line or points, min_value / max_value (or auto), number_of_bins, summary_method (mean, max, min);
  • links (chr1 start1 end1 chr2 start2 end2 [score]): arcs within the region, links_type = arcs or triangles, line_width;
  • synteny (MCscan3): ribbons between the genes of the gene track above and the gene track below, from an .anchors file (gene pairs), a .bedpe or a links file (two intervals per line). Together with a region = chr:start-end on each gene track (each track can show its own region, default the --region), this draws microsynteny across genomes;
  • vlines (.bed): dashed lines across every track at the feature starts;
  • x-axis (where = top or bottom) and spacer.

Common options: orientation = inverted (right to left), overlay_previous = yes (draw on the previous track), title. --region (repeatable) or --BED (one figure per region, named <output stem>_<chr>-<start>-<end>.<ext>) chooses what is shown; --width is in cm:

mcscan3 view tracks --tracks microsynteny.ini --region Chr1:1,000,000-1,200,000 -o result.pdf

docs.title: mcscan3 wga align
docs.text:
Whole-genome alignment of two assemblies.

Group wga · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wga align [OPTIONS] REF QRY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Aligns a query assembly to a reference with minimap2 (Li H 2018, Bioinformatics 34:3094) in assembly-to-assembly mode, keeping base-level CIGAR strings (--eqx: = match, X mismatch), so that sv call can place SNPs and short indels and wga chain can build DNA-level synteny. The chaining band is narrowed (-r 1000,2000) so that a translocated or duplicated segment gets an alignment of its own rather than becoming a long insertion inside the alignment around it. The preset follows the divergence of the two assemblies: asm5 (up to ~0.1%, accessions of a species), asm10 (~1%), asm20 (~5%, related species). Alignments of other tools in PAF (with cg:Z CIGAR tags, e.g. wfmash or AnchorWave converted to PAF) are read too:

mcscan3 wga align col.fa ler.fa -o col.ler --preset asm5

Writes <prefix>.paf (gzip if the name ends in .gz) and prints alignment statistics.

docs.text: Argument Description REF Reference assembly (FASTA). QRY Query assembly (FASTA).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --preset asm5 (same species), asm10 or asm20 (related species). (default: asm5) --cpus Threads (default: all). --path Directory of minimap2.
