docs.title: mcscan3 wga chain
docs.text:
DNA-level synteny: collinear chains of whole-genome alignments.

Group wga · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wga chain [OPTIONS] PAF

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, the annotation-free counterpart of gene-based synteny blocks, in the spirit of DEEPSPACE (J. T. Lovell, DNA-level synteny along pangenomes) and of the chaining of minimap2 and LAST. Alignments of wga align (or any PAF) on each pair of chromosomes and strand are chained by dynamic programming: an alignment can follow another when it starts after it on both genomes (small overlaps of --overlap bp tolerated and subtracted from the score) and the gap is at most --max-gap bp on both. The score of a chain is its aligned length; chains are taken from the best down, each alignment used once, and kept from --min-length bp. Every chain is a synteny block in base pairs, as gene-based blocks are in genes:

mcscan3 wga chain col.ler.paf -o col.ler --max-gap 100000 --min-length 10000

Writes <prefix>.blocks.tsv (block, reference and query chromosome, start, end, strand, aligned bp, identity, alignments) and a dot plot <prefix>.dotplot.<format>.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description PAF Alignments (PAF) of wga align or another aligner.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --max-gap Largest gap within a block (bp). (default: 100000) --min-length Smallest block (aligned bp). (default: 10000) --min-identity Alignments below this identity are left out. (default: 0.0) --format Image format of the dot plot. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 wga riparian
docs.text:
Riparian plot of DNA-level synteny along a chain of genomes.

Group wga · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wga riparian [OPTIONS] GENOMES...

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Genomes are rows of chromosomes; synteny blocks between neighbouring rows (from wga windows or wga chain, or computed here with --run) are braids. Every braid is phased by the reference genome: the reference's chromosomes are painted with their colours, and the paint is carried through the blocks row by row, both up and down the chain, so each braid shows which reference chromosome its sequence descends from, even several genomes away (grey: not traced). The painting is written as a table, <prefix>.paint.tsv (genome, chromosome, start, end, reference chromosome), a reference-phased map of every genome.

Rows other than the reference have their chromosomes ordered by the position of their synteny in the neighbouring row nearer the reference, and flipped when most of their synteny is reversed (--no-reorder keeps the natural order). Inversions are braids reversed relative to the orientation of their chromosomes as drawn; --inversions outline (default) outlines them, fill fills them with one colour, none leaves them alone. --scale bp draws every row on one base-pair scale (centred), --scale fit stretches each row to the full width. Blocks shorter than --min-block bp on either genome (default 50 kb) are left out, so that small moved repeat copies do not hide the large-scale picture. Density tracks (--track NAME=FILE, BED or GFF3; repeatable) are drawn as filled profiles above their genome's chromosomes. After the riparian plots of GENESPACE (Lovell JT et al. 2022, eLife 11:e78526) and DEEPSPACE (Lovell JT, github.com/jtlovell/DEEPSPACE):

mcscan3 wga riparian A=a.fa B=b.fa C=c.fa --ref B --run -o abc
mcscan3 wga riparian A=a.fa B=b.fa --blocks A,B=a.b.blocks.tsv --track B=b.genes.gff3 -o ab

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description GENOMES Genomes in plot order: NAME=FASTA (or NAME=lengths table).

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix. --ref Genome whose chromosomes colour the braids (default: the first). --blocks A,B=FILE: blocks between neighbouring genomes (A the reference side); repeatable. (default: []) --blocks-dir Directories with ..blocks.tsv files (default: the output directory). (default: []) --run Compute missing blocks with wga windows (FASTA genomes). --preset Preset of wga windows for --run. --n-windows Windows per genome for --run (default 500000). --cpus Threads for --run (default: all). --scale bp (one scale for all rows) or fit (rows fill the width). (default: bp) --inversions outline, fill or none. (default: outline) --track NAME=FILE: BED or GFF3 density drawn above a genome. (default: []) --min-frac Leave out sequences under this share of their genome. (default: 0.005) --min-block Leave out blocks shorter than this on either genome (bp). (default: 50000) --no-reorder Keep chromosomes in natural order, unflipped. --title Figure title. --format Image format. (default: pdf) --dpi Dots per inch. (default: 300)

docs.title: mcscan3 wga windows
docs.text:
Annotation-free synteny from windowed alignments.

Group wga · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wga windows [OPTIONS] REF QRY

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. One genome (the query) is cut into short windows that are mapped to the other (the reference) with minimap2; the best, non-repetitive window hits are chained into synteny blocks the way gene anchors are, with window ranks in place of gene ranks. No annotation is needed, and because each window maps on its own, repeats, rearrangements and duplicated copies do not disturb the chains of their neighbours. Method after DEEPSPACE (Lovell JT, github.com/jtlovell/DEEPSPACE) and GENESPACE (Lovell JT et al. 2022, eLife 11:e78526).

  1. Windows. Every query sequence of at least --min-chrom bp is cut into --window bp windows, one every step bp, where step spreads --n-windows windows over the genome (at least one window length apart is not required: windows may overlap or leave gaps). Windows with more than half N are skipped.
  2. Mapping. minimap2 without base-level alignment, chaining kept within the window (no long joins, no gap bandwidth), up to --max-hits hits per window within --min-ratio of the best, the most frequent --repeat-filter share of minimizers ignored.
  3. Hit filters. Hits below --min-mapq; hits with fewer matching bases than the lower decile of confidently mapped windows; windows whose best hit is tied more than --max-best times (repeats); hits beyond the --top best of their window; reference bins (two steps wide) hit far more often than the rest (above the 95th percentile and twice the median); and of hits of one window falling in one reference bin, all but the best.
  4. Chains. Hits are points in rank space: query window index and reference position in steps. On each pair of sequences and strand, a dynamic program finds collinear chains (successive hits at most reach ranks apart on both axes, a small penalty per rank of gap). A loose pass (5 x --max-gaps, half of --min-hits) finds anchors; hits within --radius ranks of an anchor (grid cells, so at most twice that) are kept, and a strict pass (--max-gaps, --min-hits) chains them into blocks.
  5. Blocks. Blocks spanning less than --min-span bp on either genome are dropped (small repeat copies). Neighbouring blocks of one pair and strand with nothing between them on the query are merged when less than --merge bp apart on both genomes, unless most of the reference gap between them is in other blocks (a segment moved elsewhere).

Presets (--preset, combinable with commas) set window and mapping parameters for the divergence of the genomes: close (500 bp windows), distant (5 kb windows, blocks of 5 hits), fast (fewer windows, k = 19 minimizers, more repeat filtering, MAPQ >= 12) and repeats (keep repetitive hits, for duplicated genomes). Writes <prefix>.blocks.tsv (the wga chain format), <prefix>.hits.tsv.gz (filtered window hits with their block) and a two-panel dot plot <prefix>.dotplot.<format>: all window hits, then syntenic hits by block:

mcscan3 wga windows col.fa ler.fa -o col.ler
mcscan3 wga windows ref.fa distant.fa -o ref.distant --preset distant,fast --cpus 8

docs.title: mcscan3 wgd blocks
docs.text:
Median Ks of each syntenic block.

Group wgd · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wgd blocks [OPTIONS] KSFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the segment-guided anchor Ks of wgd v2 (Chen, Zwaenepoel & Van de Peer 2024) and the block Ks of WGDI (Sun et al. 2022). All anchor pairs of a block descend from the same duplication, so the block's median Ks is a much steadier estimate than any single pair. It also stops long blocks from dominating the distribution. Reads the anchor-pair TSV of wgd ksd --anchors:

mcscan3 wgd blocks grape.anchor.ksd.tsv -o grape.blocks.tsv
mcscan3 wgd mix grape.blocks.tsv --model gmm --assign grape.blocks.assigned.tsv

Only pairs with --min-ks <= Ks <= --max-ks count (saturated Ks is dropped). Blocks with fewer than --min-pairs such pairs are skipped. With --bed, blocks whose two copies lie on the same chromosome less than --min-dist genes apart (median over the block's pairs) are skipped too: in a self comparison these are tandem arrays next to the diagonal, not whole-genome duplications. The output has the wgd ksd columns, so wgd mix and wgd peaks read it directly: one line per block, with Ks and Ka the medians and the weight 1 (--weight pairs: the number of pairs). The extra columns are pairs, ks_q1 and ks_q3.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description KSFILE Anchor-pair TSV of wgd ksd --anchors.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outfile, -o Output TSV (one line per block). --min-ks Pairs below this Ks are ignored. (default: 0.0) --max-ks Largest Ks used. (default: 5.0) --min-pairs Skip blocks with fewer pairs in range. (default: 3) --weight Block weight: one, or pairs (its number of pairs). (default: one) --bed BED of the genome: skip blocks next to the diagonal. --min-dist With --bed: min genes between a block's two copies. (default: 50)

docs.title: mcscan3 wgd consensus
docs.text:
Whole-genome duplications placed on a species tree by consensus of four lines of evidence.

Group wgd · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wgd consensus [OPTIONS] TREE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Each line of evidence places WGD events on the branches of a rooted species tree on its own; an event is called where at least --min-support of them agree:

  1. block ratio (synteny depth). Every gene of a reference genome is covered by as many syntenic blocks of a genome as the genome has copies of that region relative to the reference. The ratio is the largest depth reached by at least --depth-share of the covered genes. Against an in-group reference, orthologous synteny is used when --soi-dir gives it (ortholog soi): paralogous blocks from events the reference shares would inflate the depth;
  2. quota ratio. The quota alignment (quota align) of the genome against the reference is solved for 1:1, 1:2, ... 1:--max-ratio. Anchors kept grow until the ratio reaches the true one, then stop growing (gain below --quota-gain).

Copies of old events are too fragmented to count against a distant outgroup, so ratios are chained: the outgroup (--outgroup) has multiplier 1, and each genome is measured against its nearest genome (on the tree) of known multiplier that is not more duplicated than itself (multiplier = the reference's times the ratio), in passes until no multiplier changes.

For both, multipliers are split into prime factors (x2 duplication, x3 triplication). The factors shared by every genome of a clade are placed on the clade's stem branch (parsimony), the rest on the branches below; 3. Ks. The peaks of each genome's syntenic block Ks (wgd blocks, mixture models of wgd mix) are placed against its speciations with a rate correction: along the branch to the split from a sister clade T, with an outgroup O, the genome's own Ks since the split is (Ks(S, T) + Ks(S, O) - Ks(T, O)) / 2, from orthologous anchors. A paralog peak older than twice that value predates the split (the reasoning of ksrates, Sensalari et al. 2022); 4. gene trees (PUG, McKain et al. 2016): the syntenic paralogs of each Ks peak (the anchors of the genome's self synteny, each block labelled by the mixture component of its Ks) are placed on the species tree by where they coalesce in the gene trees (wgd tree-map --paralogs; e.g. OrthoFinder's resolved gene trees, rooted on the outgroup's genes). This places each event by itself, independently of rates. A peak whose pairs fall in few gene trees (fewer than --min-tree-rate per pair: tandem arrays or a few large families) is not a genome-wide event and gets no Ks vote either. A placement split between two adjacent branches is flagged as possible allopolyploidy. Without syntenic paralogs, the duplications of the reconciled gene trees are counted instead (Tree2GD, Chen et al. 2023): a node with at least --burst times the median number is a burst.

The number of WGDs called on a branch is the median count of the lines that saw events, with the Ks and gene-tree counts capped by the copy-number ratios when those saw events too (a mixture can split one peak in two; close peaks, less than 1.35 times apart, count once anyway).

Writes <prefix>.evidence.tsv (per genome: multipliers and Ks peaks), <prefix>.tsv (per branch: the events of each line of evidence, the support and the call), <prefix>.events.tsv (per Ks peak: its branch by Ks and by gene trees, votes, share and status) and the figure <prefix>.<format>: the tree with the called WGDs (squares) and triplications (triangles) on their branches, coloured by support, and the evidence beside it:

mcscan3 wgd consensus species.nwk --bed-dir data --anchors-dir synteny --cds-dir data \
    --blocks-dir wgd --outgroup amborella --gene-trees Resolved_Gene_Trees.txt -o wgd

docs.text: Argument Description TREE Rooted species tree (Newick).

docs.title: Options

docs.title: mcscan3 wgd correct
docs.text:
Correct a species-divergence Ks for rate differences.

Group wgd · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wgd correct [OPTIONS]

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Lineages evolve at different rates, so the ortholog Ks between a focal species F and a sister species S is not on F's own Ks scale, the scale of F's paranome peaks. With an outgroup O, the relative rate test splits the divergence (as in ksrates, Sensalari et al. 2022, and wgd v2):

Ks_F = (Ks_FS + Ks_FO - Ks_SO) / 2        the F branch since the F-S split
corrected Ks_FS = 2 * Ks_F                 the divergence on F's scale

Each ortholog Ks is the mode (highest peak of the density) of an ortholog Ks distribution (ks calc CSV or wgd ksd TSV) or a number. A 95% interval comes from bootstrapping the distributions:

mcscan3 wgd correct --fs grape.peach.ks --fo grape.rice.ks --so peach.rice.ks

A corrected divergence below a WGD peak of F means the WGD predates the F-S split.

docs.text: Argument Description

docs.text: Option Description --fs Focal-sister ortholog Ks (file or number). --fo Focal-outgroup ortholog Ks (file or number). --so Sister-outgroup ortholog Ks (file or number). --max-ks Largest Ks used. (default: 5.0) --bootstrap Bootstrap resamplings for the interval (0: none). (default: 200) --seed Random seed. (default: 666)

docs.title: mcscan3 wgd ksd
docs.text:
Whole-paranome or anchor-pair Ks distribution.

Group wgd · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wgd ksd [OPTIONS] CDSFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, following the approach of wgd (Zwaenepoel & Van de Peer 2019; wgd v2, Chen et al. 2024, Bioinformatics), reimplemented from the papers:

  1. Gene families. Paralogous BLAST hits (e-value at most --evalue) are clustered with Markov clustering (--inflation). Families larger than --max-family genes are skipped.
  2. Ks. Every pair within a family is aligned (protein alignment, back-translated to codons) and its Ks and Ka are estimated with PAML yn00, as in ks calc, or with pairwise maximum likelihood in PAML codeml (--method codeml, the method of wgd). MCscan3's own estimators need no external tool and are much faster: --method lpb93 (Li 1993, Pamilo & Bianchi 1993), ng86 (Nei & Gojobori 1986) or gy94 (maximum likelihood, as codeml); see mcscan3.core.kaks.
  3. Node weighting. In a family of n genes, n - 1 duplication events give rise to n(n - 1)/2 pairs. The pairs are clustered by average linkage on Ks. At each node, the pairs joining its two subclusters share a total weight of 1, so each duplication counts once.

With --anchors (from synteny scan of the genome against itself), only anchor pairs are used, each with weight 1: the Ks of syntenic, WGD-derived duplicates:

mcscan3 wgd ksd grape.cds --blast grape.grape.last -o grape.ksd.tsv --cpus 4
mcscan3 wgd ksd grape.cds --anchors grape.grape.anchors -o grape.anchor.ksd.tsv

The output TSV has the columns family, gene1, gene2, ks, ka, weight, node. Pairs for which yn00 failed are written with empty Ks and Ka and weight 0. Needs MUSCLE (default) or ClustalW, PAL2NAL and PAML yn00, as ks calc does.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description CDSFILE CDS FASTA of the genome.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --outfile, -o Output TSV. --blast All-against-all BLAST: whole-paranome Ks. --anchors Self-synteny anchors: anchor-pair Ks. --evalue E-value cutoff for family edges. (default: 1e-10) --inflation MCL inflation (larger: smaller families). (default: 2.0) --max-family Skip families larger than this. (default: 200) --msa Protein aligner: muscle or clustalw. (default: muscle) --method Ks estimator: yn00 or codeml (PAML), or MCscan3's own lpb93, ng86, gy94 (fast). (default: yn00) --cpus Parallel processes. (default: 1)

docs.title: mcscan3 wgd mix
docs.text:
Mixture models of a Ks distribution: GMM, ELMM and Bayesian GMM.

Group wgd · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wgd mix [OPTIONS] KSFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, following wgd v2 (Chen, Zwaenepoel & Van de Peer 2024), reimplemented from the paper. Ks values within --min-ks..--max-ks (weighted as in wgd ksd) are fitted with:

  • gmm: 1..--max-components log-normal components (a Gaussian mixture of ln Ks);
  • elmm: an exponential component for the background of small-scale duplicates, plus 0..--max-components log-normal WGD peaks. 0 peaks is the no-WGD null model;
  • bgmm: a Bayesian GMM with a Dirichlet-process prior that chooses the number of components itself (needs pip install 'mcscan3[stats]'). It is reported for comparison but only chosen with --model bgmm, because it is not a maximum-likelihood fit;
  • all (default): all of the above.

Every fit keeps the best of --n-init seeded starts. Log-likelihoods are on the Ks scale, so GMM and ELMM compete by --criterion (BIC, default, or AIC). The exponential starts at --min-ks, so cutting away the lowest Ks does not bias it. The best model's peaks get bootstrap 95% intervals (--bootstrap):

mcscan3 wgd mix grape.ksd.tsv --plot grape.mix.pdf
mcscan3 wgd mix grape.anchor.ksd.tsv --model gmm --assign grape.anchor.assigned.tsv

Prints one table: every model (label, log-likelihood, BIC, AIC; * marks the best) and its components (kind, weight, median and mode Ks, mean and sd of ln Ks or the exponential rate, interval). A peak close to --max-ks is flagged as probable Ks saturation. For whole-paranome Ks, ELMM is usually the right family. For anchor or segment Ks (wgd blocks), GMM is. --assign writes each pair's most probable component and its probability.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description KSFILE wgd ksd or wgd blocks TSV, or ks calc CSV.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --model gmm, elmm, bgmm or all. (default: all) --min-ks Smallest Ks used. (default: 0.05) --max-ks Largest Ks used. (default: 5.0) --max-components Largest number of log-normal peaks. (default: 4) --criterion Model choice: bic or aic. (default: bic) --n-init Seeded starts per fit (the best is kept). (default: 10) --bootstrap Resamplings for the peak intervals (0: none). (default: 100) --seed Random seed. (default: 666) --assign Write each pair with its most probable component. --plot Also draw the best model to this file. --log-plot Plot on the ln Ks scale.

docs.title: mcscan3 wgd peaks
docs.text:
Peaks of a Ks distribution.

Group wgd · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wgd peaks [OPTIONS] KSFILE

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3. Finds the modes of a (weighted) Ks distribution, e.g. from wgd ksd, as the peaks of a Gaussian kernel density estimate. Whole-genome duplications show up as such peaks. Only Ks within --min-ks..--max-ks are used. --log smooths log(Ks) instead, as is common for older, broader peaks. A peak counts when its prominence is at least --prominence of the highest density. Each peak gets a 95% interval from --bootstrap resamplings of the gene pairs:

mcscan3 wgd peaks grape.ksd.tsv --plot grape.peaks.pdf

Prints one line per peak (ks, ci_low, ci_high, density, prominence) and can draw the histogram, the density and the peaks.

docs.text: Argument Description KSFILE wgd ksd TSV or ks calc CSV.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --min-ks Smallest Ks used. (default: 0.05) --max-ks Largest Ks used. (default: 5.0) --log Smooth log(Ks) instead of Ks. --prominence Minimum peak prominence (fraction of the maximum). (default: 0.1) --bandwidth KDE bandwidth factor (default: Scott's rule). --bootstrap Bootstrap resamplings for the intervals. (default: 200) --seed Random seed. (default: 666) --plot Also draw the distribution and peaks to this file.

docs.title: mcscan3 wgd transcriptome
docs.text:
WGD signatures from a transcriptome assembly, without a genome.

Group wgd · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wgd transcriptome [OPTIONS] FASTA

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3, after the transcriptome workflows of WGDetector (Yang et al. 2019) and wgd (Zwaenepoel & Van de Peer 2019), reimplemented:

  1. ORFs: the longest open reading frame of each transcript on both strands (between stop codons; partial ORFs at the transcript ends are allowed, as assemblies are often fragmented), at least --min-aa codons, trimmed to the first ATG when one lies in its first third;
  2. redundancy: isoforms and alleles inflate the Ks distribution near zero. Proteins with at least --collapse identity over 80% of the shorter one are merged, keeping the longest;
  3. paranome: DIAMOND all-against-all of the proteins, MCL families and the node-weighted Ks of each family (as wgd ksd), with MCscan3's own estimators (--method, default lpb93; gy94 for maximum likelihood);
  4. WGD peaks: mixture models of the Ks distribution (wgd mix; ELMM by default, which models the small-scale duplicates near zero and the WGD peaks), with the best model by BIC.
mcscan3 wgd transcriptome trinity.fasta -o sample --cpus 8

Writes <prefix>.cds / .pep (one ORF per kept transcript), <prefix>.diamond.tsv, <prefix>.ksd.tsv (wgd ksd format), <prefix>.mix.tsv and the figure <prefix>.ks.<format>, and prints the peaks.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description FASTA Transcriptome assembly (FASTA, may be gzipped).

docs.title: mcscan3 wgd tree-map
docs.text:
Place gene duplications on a species tree from gene trees.

Group wgd · status new · new in MCscan3

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: mcscan3 wgd tree-map [OPTIONS] SPECIES_TREE GENE_TREES

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
New in MCscan3: the gene-tree / species-tree reconciliation approach of Tree2GD (Chen et al. 2023, Bioinformatics), reimplemented from the paper. It works in four steps:

  1. Species. Each gene is assigned to a species, either from --species-map (gene<TAB>species) or from its name (--sep/--field, e.g. Ath|AT1G01010).
  2. Rooting. Each gene tree is rooted on the branch that gives the fewest duplications (--rooting mindup). The alternatives are midpoint and asis.
  3. Mapping. Each internal node is mapped to the last common ancestor (LCA) of its species on the species tree. The node is a duplication when a child maps to the same species-tree node.
  4. Counting. A duplication is counted on its species-tree node when its support is at least --min-support (when the tree has support values) and both child clades contain at least --min-coverage of the species under that node. A high coverage keeps the large-scale, WGD-like duplications, where both copies were retained across the clade.
mcscan3 wgd tree-map species.nwk genetrees/ --sep "|" -o gd

Writes <prefix>.tsv (per species-tree node: descendant species, duplications, gene trees with at least one) and <prefix>.nwk (the species tree with N<id>_GD<count> node names). --plot draws the species tree with the counts. Needs the phylo extra (ete4).

Anchored placement. With --paralogs (gene1<TAB>gene2<TAB>event, e.g. syntenic duplicates labelled by the Ks peak they belong to), the known paralog pairs are placed instead of every duplication, the method of PUG (McKain et al. 2016, Genome Biol. Evol.), reimplemented from the paper: gene trees are rooted on the --outgroup's genes when they form a clade, each pair's last common ancestor is mapped to the species tree, and each gene tree gives one vote per event and node. <prefix>.events.tsv gives, per event, the node with most votes, its share of the votes and the retention: the gene trees voting there over those holding a pair of the event.

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: Argument Description SPECIES_TREE Rooted species tree (Newick). GENE_TREES Directory of gene trees, or a file with one Newick per line.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --prefix, -o Output prefix (.tsv, .nwk). --species-map genespecies file. --sep Species from the gene name, split on this (e.g. ' --field With --sep: the part that is the species (0-based). (default: 0) --rooting Gene-tree rooting: mindup, midpoint or asis. (default: mindup) --min-support Minimum support of a counted duplication. (default: 0) --min-coverage Both child clades cover at least this fraction of the species (0-1). (default: 0) --plot Also draw the species tree with the counts. --paralogs gene1gene2event: place these pairs instead (.events.tsv). --outgroup With --paralogs: root gene trees on its genes.

docs.title: Method and references
docs.text: New in MCscan3 (no JCVI equivalent). Chen Z, et al. (2023) Tree2GD: a phylogenomic method to detect large-scale gene duplication events. Bioinformatics 39:btad669; LCA reconciliation reimplemented from the paper. --paralogs: McKain MR, et al. (2016) A phylogenomic assessment of ancient polyploidy and genome evolution across the Poales. Genome Biol Evol 8:1150-1164 (PUG), reimplemented from the paper.

docs.title: Ancestral gene orders at every node
docs.text:
mcscan3 ancestral genomes species.nwk --families pan/pangenes.tsv --bed-dir data -o anc

For every internal node of the rooted species tree (leaf names = genome names), in the manner of AGORA (Muffato et al. 2023):

  1. ancestral genes: a gene family is in the ancestor when it is in at least two of the ancestor's descendant lineages and the outgroup, by parsimony;
  2. adjacencies: two families are adjacent in the ancestor when they are neighbours in descendants on different sides of the node, weighted by how many species pairs agree;
  3. CARs: the adjacency graph is linearised into contiguous ancestral regions, which are then joined into larger ones where their ends agree in the descendants (scaffolding).

--families takes pan-genes (pan genes), network clusters, OrthoFinder's Orthogroups.tsv or a gene<TAB>family table. It writes anc.<node>.cars.tsv per node and anc.summary.tsv (ancestral genes, adjacencies, CARs, N50 per node).

Warning

The topology must be right: on six eudicots, the correct tree gave 42% more ancestral adjacencies at the core-eudicot ancestor than OrthoFinder's (wrong) tree.

docs.title: Ancestral chromosomes
docs.text:
Real CARs are often many and short. ancestral karyotype groups the CARs of one ancestor into ancestral chromosomes, by where their genes lie in the descendants (CARs from one ancestral chromosome share chromosomes today), and paints every genome:

mcscan3 ancestral karyotype anc.N2.cars.tsv --families pan/pangenes.tsv --bed-dir data -o N2 --format png

The number of ancestral chromosomes is chosen by silhouette (or --groups); tiny groups merge into the group they overlap most (--min-group). Painting is smoothed (--smooth, --min-run). Outputs: N2.groups.tsv (CAR to ancestral chromosome), N2.segments.tsv (painted segments of every chromosome) and the figure: the ancestral karyotype above one row of chromosome ideograms per genome.

docs.title: Karyotypes on the species tree
docs.text:
mcscan3 ancestral tree-karyotype species.nwk --anc-prefix anc --families pan/pangenes.tsv \
    --bed-dir data --focal N2 --show-events --wgd wgd/consensus.tsv -o tree --format png

Every node gets its karyotype: ancestors on small cards at their branch points, genomes at the tips, all painted with the ancestral chromosomes of the --focal node (default the root), so fusions and fissions show as colours joining and splitting. --wgd adds the WGDs called by wgd consensus on their branches.

docs.title: Fusions, fissions, translocations
docs.text:
Along every branch, the ancestor's and the descendant's chromosomes are linked through their shared families (a link needs --event-genes families and --event-share of a chromosome). In each connected group of p ancestral and c descendant chromosomes with e links, ancestral chromosomes were broken e - p times (fissions, less duplicated copies: duplications) and descendant chromosomes joined from e - c extra pieces (fusions); groups with several chromosomes on both sides are translocations. Written to tree.events.tsv and drawn in tree.events.png; --show-events writes them on the karyotype tree. Scaffold-level genomes are reported as not countable.

How exact are the counts?

Duplications (WGDs) are found reliably. Fusion and fission counts are approximate: they depend on how complete the reconstructed ancestors are, and grouping errors in fragmented ancestors count as extra events. More genomes, especially unduplicated ones, give better ancestors and better counts.

docs.title: Painting by CARs (one genome)
docs.text: ancestral paint paints one genome by the largest CARs of an ancestor (no grouping), for looking at individual regions.

docs.title: The command line
docs.text:
Every feature is a command mcscan3 <group> <command>; -h shows its arguments and options:

mcscan3 -h                      # the groups
mcscan3 wgd -h                  # the commands of a group
mcscan3 wgd consensus -h        # one command

The command reference has one page per command, written from the same source as -h, with its method and citations.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text: Group What it does prep Turn annotations into BED, CDS and protein files align Homology searches (LAST, BLAST, DIAMOND) filter Filter hits (C-score, best hits, reciprocal best hits) synteny Find, summarise, extend and edit syntenic blocks quota Screen blocks to an expected copy ratio (quota alignment) ortholog The pairwise synteny pipeline; orthologous synteny (Orthology Index) ks Ks and Ka of gene pairs (PAML-based and MCscan3's own estimators) fractionation Gene loss after duplication (JCVI's tools) subgenome Fractionation bias, subgenome assignment of polyploids wgd Ks distributions, mixture models, WGD placement on trees, transcriptomes dup Duplicate-gene classes (WGD, tandem, proximal, transposed, dispersed) ancestral Ancestral gene orders, ancestral chromosomes, karyotypes on trees pan Pan-genes across many genomes network Synteny networks, clusters, phylogenomic profiles, network trees and figures pipeline Everything from a directory of genomes, with a report pad, synfind, phylo Pairwise ancestral decomposition, per-gene syntenic regions, trees plot Figures: dot plots, karyotypes, microsynteny, riparian, Ks, trees, ...

docs.title: Global options
docs.text:
They come before the group:

mcscan3 -v 1 synteny scan grape.peach.last grape.peach.anchors   # more log output
mcscan3 -q pipeline run genomes/ -o results                      # warnings and errors only

docs.title: Image options
docs.text:
Every plot command takes the same image options:

Option Meaning --format pdf (default), png, svg, eps, ... --dpi, --figsize resolution; size as widthxheight in inches --theme classic (the original JCVI look) or mcscan3 (colour-blind-safe, cleaner layout, extra features) --font, --style, --cmap, --diverge, --seed, --notex, --chinese fonts, axes style and colour maps

See Plotting and themes.

docs.title: Legacy JCVI command lines
docs.text:
Every MCscan-related JCVI command line runs unchanged through mcscan3 legacy:

mcscan3 legacy compara.catalog ortholog grape peach --no_strip_names

The migration guide maps each JCVI command to its MCscan3 command.

docs.title: Genomes are named by their files
docs.text:
Most commands refer to a genome by a short name, grape, and find its files by that name: grape.bed (genes), grape.cds (coding sequences), grape.pep (proteins). Pairwise results are named after both genomes: grape.peach.last (homology search), grape.peach.anchors (syntenic blocks). Keep names short and without dots.

Tip

pipeline inputs and prep genome turn raw annotations (GFF3 + genome or CDS, from Ensembl, NCBI, Phytozome, ...) into these files: one transcript per gene (the longest), clean IDs, and matching BED, CDS and protein records.

docs.title: BED: genes and their order
docs.text:
Six tab-separated columns per gene: chromosome, start, end, name, score, strand (0-based start). The order of genes along each chromosome (their rank) is what synteny uses: "collinear" means in the same order in both genomes.

Vv06    13421   15937   Vitis06g00001.t01   0   +

Gene tables in the MCScanX layout (chromosome, gene, start, end) are converted automatically by pipeline inputs and read by network build --genes-dir.

docs.title: CDS and protein FASTA
docs.text: One record per BED gene, named exactly like it. CDS are needed for Ks; proteins for protein searches (DIAMOND, OrthoFinder).

docs.title: BLAST / LAST tables
docs.text: The 12-column tabular format (query, subject, identity, length, mismatches, gaps, qstart, qend, sstart, send, evalue, bitscore), e.g. grape.peach.last, grape.peach.last.filtered.

docs.title: Anchors: syntenic blocks
docs.text:
One block per ### line, then one anchor (a pair of syntenic genes) per line with a score:

###
Vitis06g00014.t01   ONI31104    1160
Vitis06g00015.t02   ONI31105    939

.anchors are the blocks of synteny scan; .lifted.anchors add anchors recovered by liftover; .1x2.anchors (and similar) are screened by quota alignment; .soi.anchors keep the orthologous blocks only (ortholog soi). A genome against itself (grape.grape.anchors) gives its duplicated blocks.

docs.title: Simple blocks
docs.text: .simple files describe each block by its end genes, for figures (plot karyotype): startA endA startB endB score orientation.

docs.title: Ks tables
docs.text:
wgd ksd, wgd blocks and wgd transcriptome write the same TSV:

family gene1 gene2 ks ka weight node

weight makes each duplication count once (node weighting of paranome families; 1 for anchor pairs). wgd mix, wgd peaks, wgd compare read it; wgd blocks adds pairs, ks_q1, ks_q3.

docs.title: Families and ancestral regions
docs.text:
• pan/pangenes.tsv (pan genes): one pan-gene per row, the genes of each genome in columns.
  • <prefix>.<node>.cars.tsv (ancestral genomes): the contiguous ancestral regions (CARs) of an ancestor, car, position, family, <gene of each genome>.
  • <prefix>.clusters.tsv (network cluster): cluster, size, species, members with members written species|gene.

docs.title: Key ideas
docs.text:
Synteny and collinearity. Two genomic regions are syntenic when they share homologous genes; collinear when those genes are also in the same order. MCscan3 finds collinear blocks by chaining homologous gene pairs that lie close together on both genomes (synteny scan).

Orthologous and paralogous synteny. After a whole-genome duplication (WGD), one region has several syntenic copies in another genome. Only one of them is orthologous; the others descend from older duplications. The Orthology Index (ortholog soi) keeps the blocks made mostly of orthologues; quota alignment (quota align --quota 1:2) keeps the expected number of copies.

Synteny depth. How many blocks of one genome cover a region of the other: 1:2 for a tetraploid against a diploid relative. synteny depth, wgd consensus and subgenome fractionation use it.

Ks. The number of synonymous substitutions per synonymous site between two genes. Pairs of duplicates from one WGD have similar Ks, so a WGD shows as a peak in the Ks distribution of a genome's paralogs (its paranome) or of its syntenic duplicates (anchor pairs).

Fractionation. After a polyploidy, many duplicated genes are lost. When one parental subgenome keeps more genes than the other, fractionation is biased.

CARs and ancestral chromosomes. Contiguous ancestral regions are gene orders inferred for an ancestor from its descendants. Grouped by where their genes lie today, they give the ancestor's chromosomes (ancestral karyotype).

docs.title: Duplicate genes
docs.text:
mcscan3 ortholog run grape grape                     # self comparison: grape.grape.last
mcscan3 ortholog run grape peach                     # an outgroup comparison
mcscan3 dup classify grape.grape.last --bed grape.bed \
    --outgroup grape.peach.last --outgroup-bed peach.bed -o grape

After DupGen_finder (Qiao et al. 2019), each paralogous pair (the --top best hits of each gene, e-value at most --evalue) gets the first class that applies:

  1. WGD: an anchor of a syntenic block within the genome;
  2. tandem: adjacent genes;
  3. proximal: on one chromosome, at most --proximal-max genes apart;
  4. transposed: one copy at an ancestral locus (syntenic with the outgroup) and the other not (needs --outgroup; the transposed copy is listed first);
  5. dispersed: all other pairs.

Genes in no pair are singletons. Outputs: grape.<class>.pairs and grape.genes (each gene's highest-priority class). --unique counts each gene in one class only.

Combine with Ks to date each class:

mcscan3 ks kaks grape.wgd.pairs --cds grape.cds --method lpb93 -o grape.wgd.kaks.tsv
mcscan3 ks kaks grape.tandem.pairs --cds grape.cds --method lpb93 -o grape.tandem.kaks.tsv

docs.title: FAQ and troubleshooting
docs.text: X not found (searched --path, MCSCAN3_*_PATH and PATH) An external program is missing. Install it (see Installation), put it on PATH, or point to it with MCSCAN3_<NAME>_PATH. For Ks, the native methods (--method lpb93|ng86|gy94) need no external program. No anchors were found between two genomes. Check that BED names and FASTA names match (mcscan3 pipeline inputs <dir> -o prepared warns about genes without a sequence), try --no-strip-names, or protein searches (--dbtype prot) for distant genomes. My genome is a scaffold-level assembly. Figures leave out tiny sequences (--min-frac); dot plots take --skipempty; subgenome assignment needs --min-frac 0. Rearrangement counts are reported as not countable for scaffold-level genomes. The species tree from OrthoFinder or the network looks wrong. Both can be misled by WGDs and by few genomes. The pipeline report says when trees disagree. Give a trusted rooted tree with --tree: ancestral genomes and WGD placement depend on it. Ks values are huge (10, 50, 100). Maximum likelihood (gy94, codeml) on near-random pairs. Use --max-ks (WGD commands) or ks kaks --min-identity 0.3. Ks above ~3 is saturated for every method. A WGD peak I expect is missing. Paranome distributions can hide a subtle peak next to a strong recent one. Use syntenic anchors or block medians (wgd blocks), log-scale plots (wgd mix --log-plot), or wgd consensus, which combines four lines of evidence. OrthoFinder fails with "No module named numpy". Its script picked another Python. MCscan3 runs it with the Python next to it; otherwise run pipeline run --orthofinder no (MCscan3's own orthogroups) or fix OrthoFinder's environment. Figures: failed to load glyph. macOS Helvetica cannot draw text at 5 pt or less; MCscan3 switches font automatically. If it still happens, use --font Arial. How do I run old JCVI commands? mcscan3 legacy <jcvi module> <action> ...; see Migrating from JCVI. How do I cite MCscan3? mcscan3 cite. Each command page also cites the methods it implements.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: MCscan3 is a Python package (Python 3.10 or later) with a single command-line program, mcscan3. Some analyses call external programs (aligners, PAML, OrthoFinder); they are only needed for the commands that use them.

docs.title: Install the package
docs.text:
MCscan3 is not on PyPI or Bioconda; it is installed from its private GitHub repository (ank-man/mcscan3-py). Ask the authors for read access, then use any of the routes below.

conda (recommended)pipwheel filefrom a clone

One environment with MCscan3 and every external program it can call (aligners, PAML, OrthoFinder, IQ-TREE, HMMER, RepeatMasker, HelitronScanner and others):

mamba env create -f environment.yml     # or: conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate mcscan3
mcscan3 --version

environment.yml is in the repository root. Conda installs Python and the programs from conda-forge and Bioconda; pip installs MCscan3 into the same environment from GitHub over SSH. Two of MCscan3's Python dependencies (OR-Tools 9.15, ete4 4.4) are only on PyPI, which is why MCscan3 itself comes through pip and not as a conda package.

Into any Python 3.10+ environment, straight from GitHub:

pip install "mcscan3[plot,phylo,stats] @ git+ssh://git@github.com/ank-man/mcscan3-py.git"
mcscan3 --version

Without an SSH key, use HTTPS with a personal access token (read access to the repository): pip install "mcscan3[plot,phylo,stats] @ git+https://<token>@github.com/ank-man/mcscan3-py.git". A tag or commit pins a version: ...mcscan3-py.git@v0.1.0. The external programs are then installed separately (see External programs).

For machines without access to GitHub, build a wheel once and copy it over:

pip wheel --no-deps -w dist "git+ssh://git@github.com/ank-man/mcscan3-py.git"
pip install "dist/mcscan3-<version>-<platform>.whl[plot,phylo,stats]"

The wheel contains the C extensions for the platform it was built on; build one per platform (Linux x86-64, macOS arm64), or use the pure-Python fallback that is used automatically when the extensions are missing.

For development:

git clone git@github.com:ank-man/mcscan3-py.git mcscan3 && cd mcscan3
pip install -e ".[plot,phylo,stats,dev]"
mcscan3 --version

The extras add optional features:

Extra Adds Needed for plot matplotlib, pillow every figure (plot ..., --plot options, pipeline report) phylo ete4 species and gene trees: ancestral, wgd consensus, wgd tree-map, network plot, pipeline run stats scikit-learn the Bayesian mixture model (wgd mix --model bgmm) highs highspy the HiGHS solver for quota alignment (quota align --solver highs) dev pytest, ruff, mypy, mkdocs running the tests and building this documentation

Most users want [plot,phylo,stats]; the conda environment also adds network.

docs.title: External programs
docs.text:
MCscan3 finds each program on PATH, or through an environment variable MCSCAN3_<NAME>_PATH (for example MCSCAN3_LASTAL_PATH=/opt/last/bin/lastal). Bioconda has all of them:

The conda environment above installs all of them. To add them to another environment:

mamba install -c conda-forge -c bioconda last diamond blast mmseqs2 minimap2 miniprot \
    muscle mafft famsa clustalw pal2nal paml iqtree fasttree raxml aster orthofinder \
    bedtools samtools bwa hmmer repeatmasker helitronscanner openjdk
Program Used by Notes LAST (lastal, lastdb) align last, ortholog run (default aligner), pipeline run the default homology search for synteny DIAMOND align diamond, ortholog run --align-soft diamond_blastp, wgd transcriptome, pipeline run (orthogroups without OrthoFinder) protein searches BLAST+ (blastn, blastp, makeblastdb) align blast, ortholog run --align-soft blast OrthoFinder pipeline run --orthofinder auto/yes orthogroups, orthologues, gene trees, rooted species tree MUSCLE or ClustalW, PAL2NAL, PAML yn00 ks calc (the JCVI-compatible Ks), wgd ksd --method yn00 not needed with MCscan3's own Ks estimators PAML codeml wgd ksd --method codeml not needed with --method gy94 (same model) bedtools (intersectBed) fractionation validate, fractionation gaps, fractionation gff-select MMseqs2 align mmseqs fast protein searches minimap2 wga, annotate transfer, scaffold genome alignment miniprot annotate transfer protein-to-genome alignment FAMSA, MAFFT or MUSCLE; IQ-TREE or FastTree; ASTER (astral4) phylo busco one aligner is required; without ASTER no coalescent tree is made RAxML phylo build HMMER (hmmsearch) te classify, the domain checks of te tir and te helitron, phylo busco protein domains samtools, BWA scaffold (Hi-C and read evidence) RepeatMasker te annotate not needed with --from-out HelitronScanner, Java te helitron (used when installed) --engine native needs neither

Ks without PAML

wgd ksd --method lpb93 (or ng86, gy94), ks kaks and wgd transcriptome use MCscan3's own Ka/Ks estimators: no aligner or PAML is needed, and they are much faster. gy94 reproduces pairwise codeml (see Validation).

OrthoFinder from conda

OrthoFinder's script starts with #!/usr/bin/env python3, which can pick a Python without numpy. MCscan3 runs it with the Python of its own environment when one is next to it.

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
mcscan3 features            # every command, its status and its JCVI equivalent
mcscan3 cite                # how to cite MCscan3 and the work it builds on
pytest -q                   # the test suite (from the source directory, with [dev])

docs.title: Build this documentation
docs.text:
pip install ".[dev]"
mkdocs serve                # http://127.0.0.1:8000, rebuilt on every change
mkdocs build                # static site in site/

The same mkdocs.yml works on Read the Docs (with a .readthedocs.yaml that installs .[dev]).

docs.title: Pan-genes
docs.text:
mcscan3 pan genes grape peach poplar --ref grape --bed-dir data --anchors-dir synteny \
    --suffix lifted.anchors -o pan
mcscan3 plot riparian grape peach poplar --ref grape --bed-dir data --anchors-dir synteny \
    --suffix lifted.anchors -o riparian.png

Genes linked by syntenic anchors (any pair of genomes, either order) form pan-genes, placed on the reference genome; pan-genes without a reference gene take the position of a neighbour. Categories: core (all genomes), shell (several), private (one).

pipeline run builds pan-genes from anchors that are orthologous synteny and in one orthogroup, then lists the other members of the orthogroups as non-syntenic orthologues.

The riparian plot draws each genome as a row of chromosomes, with braids for syntenic blocks between neighbouring rows, coloured by the reference chromosome they descend from. Small scaffolds are left out (--min-frac), chromosomes are ordered and flipped to reduce crossings (--reorder), blocks smaller than --min-block anchors are not drawn.

docs.title: Synteny networks
docs.text:
After Zhao & Schranz (2017, 2019): genes are nodes, syntenic anchor pairs are edges, and clusters of the network are syntenic loci shared across genomes.

mcscan3 network build synteny/*.lifted.anchors -o net        # files named <a>.<b>.<suffix>
mcscan3 network cluster net.edges.tsv -o net --method mcl    # or louvain, components
mcscan3 network profile net.clusters.tsv -o net --phylip
mcscan3 network tree net.profile.tsv -o net --method nj
mcscan3 network plot net --tree species.nwk --kind all -o net --format png

Precomputed block tables (one row per pair: block, [score,] gene1, gene2) can be read directly, with gene-to-genome assignment from gene tables:

mcscan3 network build --table blocks.tsv.gz --genes-dir genomes/ -o net

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
• heatmap: genome x genome synteny similarity (Jaccard of shared clusters), raw below the diagonal and phylogeny-corrected above (each pair's similarity at the mean tree distance, after an exponential decay with tree distance), one colour scale. Pairs darker above than below kept more synteny than their divergence predicts.
  • profile: the phylogenomic profile: genomes as rows (species tree and clade strip on the left), clusters as columns ordered by their presence patterns (dendrogram on top), presence or copy number (--profile-style).
  • graph: the genome network, edges weighted by shared clusters.
  • cluster: the gene network of one cluster (--cluster), coloured by clade.

Clades come from --clades (genomeclade) or are cut from the tree.

Tip

A network tree built from profiles is a useful check, but with WGDs and few genomes it can be wrong; prefer a trusted species tree with --tree for the figures.

docs.title: One command: the pipeline
docs.text:
mcscan3 pipeline run takes a directory of genomes and runs a full comparative analysis, resuming where it stopped if interrupted, and writes an HTML report.

mcscan3 pipeline inputs genomes/                          # what was found, before running
mcscan3 pipeline run genomes/ -o results --ref grape --cpus 16 --ks
open results/report.html

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Put one or more files per genome in a directory, named <genome>.<anything>:

Files Mode What happens grape.gff3.gz + grape.dna.fa.gz genome longest coding transcript per gene, CDS spliced and translated (prep genome) grape.gff3.gz + grape.cds.fa.gz [+ grape.pep.fa.gz] gff+cds longest transcript per gene; the GFF attribute matching the FASTA names is found automatically grape.bed + grape.cds / grape.pep processed used as given; the BED may be in MCScanX layout

FASTA files are classified by their names (cds, pep, protein, dna, genome, ...) or, if the name does not tell, by their content. A sample sheet (--samples, columns species, gff, genome, bed, cds, pep) overrides the detection. Protein records are matched to the genes through their headers (transcript:, gene:, .CDS / -P suffixes); when they do not match, proteins are translated from the CDS.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. inputs: data/<genome>.bed/.cds/.pep.
  2. orthology: OrthoFinder when installed (--orthofinder auto, the default; yes to require it): orthogroups, orthologues, gene trees and a rooted species tree. Otherwise (no) MCscan3's own: DIAMOND all-against-all, MCL orthogroups, reciprocal best hits.
  3. synteny: ortholog run for every pair of genomes and each genome against itself.
  4. soi: the Orthology Index of every block; soi/<a>.<b>.soi.anchors keep orthologous synteny (--soi-cutoff).
  5. pan: pan-genes linked by anchors that are orthologous synteny and in one orthogroup, completed with the other members of their orthogroups (<genome>_nonsyntenic columns), and a riparian plot.
  6. network: synteny network, clusters, profiles and a network species tree; the trees are compared and disagreements reported.
  7. ancestral: ancestral gene orders at every node of the species tree, ancestral chromosomes painted on every genome, and all karyotypes on the tree.
  8. dup: duplicate-gene classes of every genome.
  9. wgd (--ks): anchor-pair Ks (MCscan3's LPB93 estimator: no PAML needed), block-median Ks and mixture models per genome.
  10. wgd-consensus (--ks): WGDs placed on the species tree by consensus of four lines of evidence (WGD guide).
  11. report: report.html.

The species tree matters

Ancestral genomes and WGD placement depend on the rooted species tree. With few genomes, or genomes with WGDs, OrthoFinder's and the synteny-network trees can both be wrong (on six eudicots neither matched the accepted tree). The report flags disagreements; give a trusted tree with --tree species.nwk when it matters.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
results/
  run.json            what ran: status, time and notes of every step, and the results shown in the report
  samples.tsv         what was found
  data/               prepared <genome>.bed/.cds/.pep
  orthology/          OrthoFinder results or MCscan3's own orthogroups
  synteny/            ortholog run per pair (.last, .anchors, .lifted.anchors, dot plots)
  soi/                Orthology Index per block, .soi.anchors
  pan/                pangenes.tsv, riparian.png
  network/            net.edges/.clusters/.profile.tsv, net.tree.nwk
  ancestral/          anc.<node>.cars.tsv, <node>.karyotype.png, tree.karyotype.png
  dup/                <genome>.<class>.pairs, <genome>.genes
  wgd/                <genome>.anchor.ksd.tsv, .blocks.tsv, .blocks.png, consensus.tsv/.png
  report_files/       figures and interactive dot plot data used by the report
  report.html

Steps that fail are listed in the report and in a table printed at the end of the run; the others still run. Re-running the same command skips finished work.

docs.title: Re-running some steps
docs.text:
--steps re-runs only the steps named; the results of the others are kept from run.json:

mcscan3 pipeline run genomes/ -o results --steps ancestral,report --tree species.nwk
mcscan3 pipeline report results          # only rebuild report.html (e.g. after an update)

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
report.html is one self-contained page (no internet access needed; share the whole results/ directory or just report.html with report_files/). It has:

  • summary cards: genomes, genes, orthogroups, orthologous blocks, pan-genes, ancestral CARs and WGDs placed;
  • interactive dot plots of every genome pair and every genome against itself: pick a pair, scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click a chromosome name to zoom to it, hover a dot for its two genes, block, orientation and Orthology Index; colour by orientation, block or Orthology Index; download the view as PNG;
  • pan-genes (core, shell, private), riparian plot, synteny network and species trees, ancestral karyotypes on the tree, duplicate-gene classes as stacked bars, Ks mixtures and WGDs on the species tree;
  • the run: every step with its status and time, and every note.

Figures open full size on click and tables sort by clicking a column header. The page follows the system's light or dark mode, with a toggle.

Report of six eudicot genomes (amborella, Arabidopsis, grape, peach, poplar, soybean).

docs.title: Run time
docs.text: Six plant genomes (27,000-56,000 genes each) on 10 CPUs: OrthoFinder is the longest step (hours on a laptop; much less on a server); synteny for 21 pairs takes about 30 minutes; the other steps minutes each; --ks adds anchor Ks of every genome (native LPB93: minutes) and the WGD consensus.

docs.title: Two themes
docs.text:
Every plot command takes --theme:

  • classic (default): the original JCVI look, pixel for pixel (MCscan3 tests its figures against JCVI's);
  • mcscan3: white panels, a colour-blind-safe palette (Okabe-Ito, Paul Tol) and plot-specific improvements:
Plot With --theme mcscan3 plot dotplot blocks coloured forward / inverted; the second genome's chromosomes ordered and flipped along the first (--order auto); every dot drawn (rasterised); chromosomes as light bands with short names (Chr01 -> 1); unplaced scaffolds (under 0.5% of the genes) hidden, with a note; --oi greys out older duplications plot karyotype ribbons coloured by the first genome's chromosomes (--color-by chr), by ancestral chromosome (car) or by any gene table (labels); --genomes a,b,c builds the layout; --auto-order reduces crossings plot riparian (always) small scaffolds left out, chromosomes reordered, small blocks fainter

Figures that are new in MCscan3 (Ks mixtures, WGDs on the tree, ancestral karyotypes, riparian plots, networks, subgenomes) always use the MCscan3 style: a bold left-aligned title with a grey subtitle that states the method and the numbers behind the figure.

docs.title: Interactive dot plots
docs.text:
Give plot dotplot an output name ending in .html for an interactive dot plot: scroll to zoom, drag to pan, click a chromosome name to zoom to it, hover a dot for its two genes and its block. The page is self-contained and opens in any browser, offline.

mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.lifted.anchors -o grape.peach.html
mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.peach.lifted.anchors --oi grape.peach.oi -o grape.peach.html  # + Orthology Index

The pipeline report has one for every pair of genomes. Try one in the gallery.

Fonts that cannot draw very small labels (macOS Helvetica at 5 pt or less) are replaced automatically.

docs.title: The figures of MCscan3
docs.text: Figure Command Dot plot of two genomes (or one against itself) plot dotplot Macrosynteny across genomes plot karyotype, plot riparian Local synteny with gene glyphs plot microsynteny Ks histograms plot ks, plot histogram, wgd mix --plot, wgd peaks --plot Ks of several genomes / transcriptomes wgd compare WGDs on the species tree wgd consensus Transcriptome summary wgd transcriptome (<prefix>.summary.*) Ancestral chromosomes painted on genomes ancestral karyotype Karyotypes on the species tree, rearrangement counts ancestral tree-karyotype Biased fractionation subgenome fractionation Subgenomes painted on the polyploid subgenome assign Network heatmap, profile, graph, cluster network plot Synteny depth histogram synteny depth --histogram, plot depth Trees, heatmaps, chromosome painting, BLAST dot plots plot tree, plot heatmap, plot chromosome, plot blastplot

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text:
mcscan3 plot gallery -o gallery          # every plot type in both themes, next to JCVI's original
open gallery/index.html

See also Figures.

docs.title: Biased fractionation
docs.text:
After a polyploidy many duplicated genes are lost. When one subgenome keeps more genes than the other(s), fractionation is biased, a sign of allopolyploidy and subgenome dominance.

mcscan3 ortholog run ath brapa --quota 1:3          # B. rapa is a mesohexaploid relative to Arabidopsis
mcscan3 subgenome fractionation ath.brapa.lifted.1x3.anchors --ref-bed ath.bed --poly-bed brapa.bed \
    --copies 3 -o brapa --format png

The reference must not share the polyploidy. Each block of the polyploid covers an interval of the reference; its retention is the share of the reference genes in that interval that the block kept. At every reference gene the covering blocks are ranked by retention: LF (least fractionated), MF1, MF2...

Ranking by retention alone makes LF look better than MF even without any bias, so the significance test shuffles which copies kept each gene (keeping how many) and re-ranks (--permutations). Outputs: brapa.genes.tsv (the polyploid gene of each rank per reference gene), brapa.blocks.tsv (retention and rank of each block), brapa.windows.tsv and a figure of retention along the reference chromosomes.

docs.title: Assigning chromosomes to subgenomes
docs.text:
With progenitor-like diploids (or their closest living relatives), every polyploid gene votes for the progenitor whose syntenic partner is closest; votes are smoothed along the chromosomes:

mcscan3 ortholog run bnapus brapa
mcscan3 ortholog run bnapus bole
mcscan3 subgenome assign bnapus --progenitor brapa=bnapus.brapa.lifted.anchors \
    --progenitor bole=bnapus.bole.lifted.anchors -o bnapus --format png

Closeness is the anchor score, or Ks with --ks NAME=FILE (wgd ksd tables). Votes closer than --margin abstain. Homoeologous exchanges show as segments of the other subgenome within a chromosome. For scaffold-level assemblies use --min-frac 0 (keep every scaffold) and a smaller --min-run. Outputs: bnapus.genes.tsv, bnapus.segments.tsv, bnapus.chromosomes.tsv (subgenome and confidence per chromosome) and a karyotype figure coloured by subgenome.

See Validation for B. rapa, maize and B. napus.

docs.title: Pairwise synteny
docs.text: The quick start walks through grape vs peach step by step. This page explains the choices along the way.

docs.title: The one-command pairwise run
docs.text:
mcscan3 ortholog run grape peach --cpus 8

ortholog run aligns the two gene sets (LAST on CDS by default; --dbtype prot uses proteins, --align-soft diamond_blastp|blast another aligner), filters the hits (tandem merging, C-score --cscore), finds collinear blocks (--dist, --min-size) and recovers extra anchors by liftover. It writes:

  • grape.peach.last, grape.peach.last.filtered: the hits;
  • grape.peach.anchors, grape.peach.lifted.anchors: the blocks;
  • grape.peach.pdf: a dot plot.

The same steps can be run one by one: align last, filter cscore / filter blastfilter, synteny scan, synteny liftover.

docs.title: Polyploidy and copy ratios
docs.text:
A genome with a WGD has several syntenic copies of each region of an unduplicated relative.

mcscan3 synteny depth grape.poplar.anchors --histogram    # e.g. 1:2
mcscan3 ortholog run grape poplar --quota 1:2             # keep at most 1 grape and 2 poplar blocks per region
mcscan3 quota align grape.poplar.anchors --quota 1:2 --screen

quota align solves a linear programme so that each region of the first genome is covered at most once and of the second at most twice (the ploidy ratio).

docs.title: Orthologous synteny
docs.text:
Older duplications make paralogous synteny: blocks between a region and the copies of its ortholog's duplication. The Orthology Index (OI) of a block is the share of its anchors that are orthologues:

mcscan3 ortholog soi grape.poplar.lifted.anchors --orthologs OrthoFinder/Orthologues -o grape.poplar.soi.anchors
mcscan3 ortholog soi grape.poplar.lifted.anchors --blast grape.poplar.last -o grape.poplar.soi.anchors   # RBH as orthologues

Blocks with OI at least --cutoff (0.6) are kept. soi also writes <anchors prefix>.oi, the OI of every block (numbered in the order of that anchors file). Orthologous synteny is what pan-genes, ancestral genomes and the WGD consensus use.

docs.title: Figures
docs.text:
mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.poplar.lifted.anchors --theme mcscan3              # forward / inverted blocks
mcscan3 plot dotplot grape.poplar.lifted.anchors --oi grape.poplar.lifted.oi --theme mcscan3   # older duplications grey
mcscan3 plot karyotype --genomes grape,peach,poplar --anchors-dir . --theme mcscan3   # no layout files needed

With --theme mcscan3, dot plots order and flip the second genome's chromosomes along the first (--order auto), so blocks fall on the diagonal and inversions stand out; karyotypes colour ribbons by the first genome's chromosomes (--color-by chr), order chromosomes to reduce crossings, and can colour by ancestral chromosome (--color-by car). See Plotting and themes.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use the same gene names in the BED and FASTA files; --no-strip-names keeps transcript suffixes such as .t01.
  • Scaffold-level assemblies: --skipempty drops scaffolds without anchors from dot plots; karyotype and riparian plots leave out sequences with few genes (--min-frac).
  • A genome against itself (ortholog run grape grape) finds its duplicated blocks, the input of anchor-pair Ks and duplicate classification.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: How MCscan3's results are checked.

docs.title: Parity with JCVI
docs.text: The 78 ported features are tested against the output of JCVI v1.6.7 on real genomes (grape, peach, poplar from Ensembl Plants): text outputs byte for byte, figures pixel for pixel (tests/golden). 4 features are kept as legacy-only. See Deviations for JCVI defects found and how MCscan3 handles them.

docs.title: New features: known answers
docs.text: Every new feature is tested on simulated data with a known answer (tests/features), for example: a simulated history of fusions, fissions and inversions recovered by ancestral genomes; biased and unbiased fractionation (calibrated: 2/40 false positives at the 5% level, 10/10 biases of 0.85 vs 0.60 found); a simulated WGD at Ks ~0.6 recovered from a simulated transcriptome.

docs.title: Ka/Ks against PAML
docs.text:
On identical codon alignments (40 grape paralog pairs):

MCscan3 PAML Agreement gy94 codeml (pairwise, F3x4) r = 0.99998 (largest dS difference 0.03) lpb93 yn00 (LPB93) r = 0.9995 ng86 yn00 (NG86) median dS difference 0.6%

Genome scale: 11,742 grape anchor pairs in 27 s (lpb93) or 4 min (gy94) on 10 CPUs.

docs.title: Real genomes
docs.text:
WGDs on the species tree (wgd consensus; Amborella, grape, Arabidopsis, poplar, peach, soybean; Ensembl Plants):

Known event Placed on Lines of evidence gamma triplication core-eudicot stem 4/4 Arabidopsis alpha and beta Arabidopsis 3/4 salicoid WGD poplar 3/4 Glycine and legume WGDs soybean 4/4

No WGD was called for grape, peach or Amborella.

Fractionation and subgenomes:

Data Result Published B. rapa vs Arabidopsis LF 60.5%, MF1 46.3%, MF2 39.6%, p = 0.005 the same ordering (Wang et al. 2011; Cheng et al. 2012) maize vs sorghum maize1 53.9%, maize2 38.6%, p = 0.005 maize2 more fractionated (Schnable et al. 2011) B. napus vs B. rapa and B. oleracea 99.2% of genes on the right subgenome (smoothed), 96.8% of scaffolds A/C subgenomes from the gene names

Transcriptomes without a genome (wgd transcriptome, NCBI TSA assemblies):

Species Peaks (Ks) Known WGDs Arabidopsis 0.75, 1.91 alpha, beta maize 0.24, 0.93, 2.10 maize WGD, grass rho, older soybean 0.08, 1.92 Glycine WGD, gamma; the legume WGD (~0.6) is not resolved from the paranome

Ancestral genomes: on the six eudicots, the core-eudicot ancestor resolves into 18 ancestral chromosomes (21 published post-gamma protochromosomes); most grape chromosomes paint as one or two ancestral chromosomes.

Synteny network: 47 of 51 genomes of the SynNet demo set (7.4 million syntenic links); the network tree recovers the grasses, Brassicaceae, legumes and Rosaceae.

docs.title: Ks of gene pairs
docs.text:
MCscan3 has its own Ka/Ks estimators, and can also run PAML:

Method Command option Speed Notes lpb93 --method lpb93 ~0.1 ms / pair Li (1993), Pamilo & Bianchi (1993); corrects transition bias. A good default ng86 --method ng86 ~0.02 ms / pair Nei & Gojobori (1986) gy94 --method gy94 ~60 ms / pair maximum likelihood (Goldman & Yang 1994), as pairwise codeml yn00 --method yn00 slow PAML yn00 (needs MUSCLE, PAL2NAL, PAML) codeml --method codeml slow PAML codeml

Times are after the codon alignment (about 4 ms per pair). All native methods run in parallel with --cpus.

mcscan3 ks kaks grape.grape.anchors --cds grape.cds --method lpb93,gy94 --cpus 8 -o grape.kaks.tsv

Saturation

Ks above about 3 is unreliable for every method. Maximum likelihood (gy94, codeml) gives very large values for near-random pairs (protein identity below ~0.3) where counting methods give moderate ones; ks kaks --min-identity 0.3 leaves such pairs out, and the WGD commands use --max-ks (default 5).

docs.title: Ks distributions of a genome
docs.text:
There are three kinds, from the noisiest to the cleanest WGD signal:

# 1. paranome: all paralog pairs, in families, each duplication counted once
mcscan3 wgd ksd grape.cds --blast grape.grape.last -o grape.paranome.tsv --method lpb93 --cpus 8
# 2. anchor pairs: syntenic duplicates only (from a self comparison)
mcscan3 wgd ksd grape.cds --anchors grape.grape.lifted.anchors -o grape.anchor.tsv --method lpb93 --cpus 8
# 3. block medians: one Ks per syntenic block
mcscan3 wgd blocks grape.anchor.tsv -o grape.blocks.tsv --max-ks 3 --bed grape.bed

Block medians are the steadiest: all anchors of a block come from one duplication.

docs.title: Finding the peaks
docs.text:
mcscan3 wgd mix grape.blocks.tsv --model all --plot grape.mix.pdf     # GMM, ELMM, Bayesian GMM; best by BIC
mcscan3 wgd peaks grape.blocks.tsv --log --plot grape.peaks.pdf       # kernel density peaks
  • GMM: log-normal components, one per WGD.
  • ELMM: an exponential for the steady stream of small-scale duplicates near Ks 0, plus log-normal WGD components (wgd v2's model). Best for paranomes.
  • Bayesian GMM (bgmm, needs [stats]): chooses its number of components itself.

--bootstrap gives confidence intervals of the peaks, --assign the component of every pair. wgd mix reports possibly saturated peaks near --max-ks.

docs.title: WGDs on the species tree
docs.text:
wgd consensus places WGDs on the branches of a rooted species tree where at least --min-support (2) of four independent lines of evidence agree:

  1. block ratio: the synteny depth of each genome against a genome without the events;
  2. quota ratio: the copy ratio at which quota alignment stops gaining anchors;
  3. Ks: block-Ks peaks placed against rate-corrected speciation Ks (each genome's own branch length since a split, from orthologous Ks with an outgroup, as in ksrates);
  4. gene trees: where the syntenic paralogs of each Ks peak coalesce in the gene trees (e.g. OrthoFinder's resolved gene trees), the method of PUG. Gene trees are rooted on the outgroup's genes; each pair's last common ancestor is mapped to the species tree when both of its child clades hold at least half the species below it; each gene tree votes once per event and node. This places each event by itself, whatever the rates of evolution.

The gene trees also check the Ks peaks. Pairs of a real WGD are spread over many gene families, about one gene tree for every 2 to 10 pairs. A mixture component made of tandem arrays or a few large families puts thousands of pairs into a handful of trees. A peak with fewer than --min-tree-rate (0.05) gene trees per pair is rejected, and it gets no Ks vote either. A peak whose placement is split between two adjacent branches is flagged as possible allopolyploidy (see subgenome assign). Without syntenic paralogs, duplication bursts of the reconciled gene trees are counted instead (Tree2GD-style).

The number of WGDs on a branch is the median count over the lines that saw events. Ks peaks less than 1.35 times apart count as one event (a mixture often splits a broad peak in two), and the Ks and gene-tree counts are capped by the copy ratios when those saw events on the branch.

On six eudicots (Amborella, Arabidopsis, grape, peach, poplar, soybean) with OrthoFinder's gene trees, this calls the γ triplication at the core-eudicot stem, α and β in Arabidopsis, two WGDs in soybean, the salicoid WGD in poplar, and none in grape or peach. It also rejects a grape Ks component at 0.35: 7,594 pairs in only 60 gene trees.

Copy ratios are chained from the outgroup through the nearest less-duplicated genome and split into x2 (duplication) and x3 (triplication) events by parsimony on the tree.

mcscan3 wgd consensus species.nwk --bed-dir data --anchors-dir synteny --cds-dir data \
    --blocks-dir wgd --soi-dir soi --outgroup amborella \
    --gene-trees OrthoFinder/Resolved_Gene_Trees/Resolved_Gene_Trees.txt --cpus 8 -o wgd/consensus

It writes consensus.tsv (per branch: each line of evidence, support, calls), consensus.events.tsv (per Ks peak: its branch by Ks and by gene trees, gene trees per pair, votes, share and status), consensus.evidence.tsv (per genome: multipliers and Ks peaks, and the rejected ones), consensus.pair_ks.tsv and a figure. ancestral tree-karyotype --wgd consensus.tsv draws the calls on the karyotype tree. pipeline run --ks runs all of this.

Related: wgd tree-map (duplications from gene trees alone; --paralogs pairs.tsv --outgroup X places your own pairs gene1<TAB>gene2<TAB>event), wgd correct (rate-correct one speciation Ks onto a genome's scale).

docs.title: Transcriptomes (no genome)
docs.text:
mcscan3 wgd transcriptome trinity.fasta -o sample --cpus 8 --format png

Longest ORFs per transcript, isoforms and alleles collapsed (--collapse, 97% identity), DIAMOND paralog families, node-weighted Ks with the native estimators (--method), and mixture models. It writes sample.ksd.tsv, sample.mix.tsv, sample.ks.png and a four-panel sample.summary.png (Ks with the mixture, Ka/Ks against Ks, ORF lengths, family sizes).

Note

Paranomes resolve clear WGDs well, but a subtle older peak next to a very recent WGD can be absorbed by the small-scale duplicates (soybean's legume WGD near Ks 0.6; see Validation). Synteny resolves such cases when a genome is available.

docs.title: Comparing genomes and transcriptomes
docs.text:
mcscan3 wgd compare ath=ath.ksd.tsv soybean=soybean.ksd.tsv maize=maize.ksd.tsv -o compare --format png

Stacked Ks distributions on one axis with each sample's peaks, so shared WGDs line up.
